title: Director of People Operations
description:
About ALSO.

We’re ALSO, an electric mobility company originally conceived as a part of Rivian. We’re a passionate team of builders, dreamers, doers and innovators, focused on creating entirely new (not to mention, innovative and delightful) vertically integrated, small EVs designed to meet the global mobility challenges of today and tomorrow. Our mission is to inspire everyone to ride ALSO—replacing many local car, truck and SUV miles with ones on vehicles that are more affordable, more enjoyable and 10-50x more efficient.



We’re bringing on a Director of People Operations to be the operational engine of our People function, driving the full spectrum of people programs. Total rewards is your core strength and the capability that complements our existing People team, but this role goes well beyond comp and benefits. You’ll build and scale the processes, infrastructure, and programs that support a fast-moving, global business, and you’ll do it with direct access to business leaders. This is a lean, high-trust role: you’ll report to our VP of People, lead a small team, and operate with the autonomy that comes from being close to the decisions that matter. If you’re energized by building the machine, not just running it, this is your kind of role.



What You'll Do

Total Rewards - Your Core Strength

•     Evolve and steward ALSO's compensation philosophy — job architecture, salary bands, leveling frameworks, and equity programs that work across our US and global teams

•     Lead compensation cycles on a regular cadence: merit, bonus, and additional equity grants, in close partnership with Finance and the VP of People

•     Own benefits strategy end-to-end — plan design, broker and vendor relationships, open enrollment, and ongoing benchmarking to ensure we remain competitive as we grow into new markets

•     Partner with the People Partner and Talent Acquisition on compensation for new hires and promotions, maintaining consistency and fairness at every level



People Operations & People Infrastructure

•     Partner with our People Ops Manager to evolve our HRIS and broader People tech stack, building on the deep investment of these systems and experience on the team — data integrity, system integrations, and self-service tooling that makes life easier for employees and managers alike

•     Build and maintain scalable People Ops processes across the full employee lifecycle: onboarding, offboarding, leave administration, performance cycles, and internal mobility

•     Ensure compliance across federal, state, local, and international employment law requirements — with a particular focus on our growing global footprint

•     Keep our people infrastructure lean and smart; we're not building for headcount, we're building for impact



Employee Experience & Engagement

•     Partner with the People Partner to develop and run employee engagement programs, recognition initiatives, and feedback loops that reflect ALSO's culture and values

•     Use people data and surveys to surface insights that help leadership make better decisions about our team



Team Leadership & Strategic People Partnership

•     Serve as a trusted advisor to the VP of People and senior leadership on compensation, org design, and people operations

•     Translate complexity into clarity — whether that's communicating a new comp framework to the team or presenting a benefits recommendation to the exec team

•     Lead and develop a small, high-impact team: setting clear priorities, modeling operational excellence, and creating an environment where people do their best work

•     Be a player-coach: you set direction and you also do the work, and you're proud of both



What You’ll Bring

We're looking for someone with deep roots in total rewards and the breadth to hold everything else that comes with running People Ops at a global, pre-IPO company. You'll likely bring:



•     8–12 years of progressive People or People Ops experience, with at least 5–7 years focused specifically on compensation, benefits, or total rewards

•     Experience leading people and programs in a high-growth or startup environment — you know what it means to build, not just maintain

•     Deep knowledge of compensation design, equity programs (ISOs, RSUs), and benefits administration in a multi-state and/or international context

•     Comfort operating across multiple geographies and navigating the compliance complexity that comes with global teams

•     Strong analytical skills — you can build a comp model and you know how to use data to tell a story that lands with leadership

•     High emotional intelligence and discretion; people trust you with sensitive information at every level of the org

•     A builder's mindset: you're energized by creating structure where there isn't any, and you don't need a large team to do great work



Nice to Have

•     Experience in EV, or consumer product companies

•     Familiarity with pre-IPO equity compensation and the complexity that comes with it

•     Experience supporting global market entry and the people infrastructure it requires

•     CCP, SHRM-SCP, or CEBS certification


The salary for this position ranges from $180,000 - $230,000 per year, depending on experience, qualifications, and location.

 

This is an onsite position requiring attendance in the office 5 days per week. Once fully ramped and in alignment with their manager, employees may have the opportunity for limited flexibility, including the potential to work remotely up to two days per week, based on business and team needs.

 

Perks & Benefits

 - Robust health coverage — excellent health, dental and vision insurance covered up to 100% by ALSO with FSA & HSA options

 - One Medical membership and dedicated insurance advocates

 - Rich fertility and family building benefits with Progyny

 - Flexible time off

 - 401(k) match

Why ALSO.

We’re passionate about helping the world find a better way to get there—wherever it is you’re headed.

We’re located in the heart of Silicon Valley and have brought together a world-class team from some of the biggest brands in the technology, automotive, cycling, outdoor recreation and retail spaces. 

Together we’re working hands-on to imagine, design and build an entirely new solution to a global set of transportation challenges.

title: Account Specialist, Urology - Chicago, IL
description:

AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. For more information about AbbVie, please visit us at  www.abbvie.com . Follow @abbvie on  LinkedIn,   Facebook ,  Instagram ,  X  and  YouTube.
The Account Specialist role promotes a product to community practices and health systems. Customer accounts may include community/private practices, community-based hospitals, academic medical centers, and government accounts (military treatment facilities and/or Veteran’s Affairs Medical Centers). The Account Specialist develops and maintains relationships with various accounts/departments such as neurology, pain medicine, physical medicine and rehabilitation, primary care, and pharmacy. Or in Urology, specialists such as urology, urogynecology, obstetrics and gynecology, female pelvic medicine, ambulatory surgical centers, and reconstructive surgery.
Responsibilities
Promote a product to meet/exceed sales goals in community/private practices as well as hospitals/health systems.
Identify/uncover customer needs (training, clinical, operational, reimbursement) and address with appropriate AbbVie resources
Provide education and clinical/injection training for residents, fellows, and other key hospital personnel.
Expert delivery of anatomical/procedural information and training, including the appropriate use of anatomical terminology to train injection paradigms/postures while highlighting various anatomical and injection insights and considerations.
Effectively utilize AbbVie's sales and data resources to enhance productivity and growth of AbbVie products while implementing U.S. Marketing Plan.
Collaborate with other Account Specialist to promote the product for approved indications and execute individual, department, or group resident/fellow trainings within hospital/health system accounts.
Bachelor’s degree in health, sciences, pharmacy or business-related field preferred or relevant and equivalent industry experience required.
Relevant and equivalent industry experience required in lieu of a bachelor’s degree is at least five (5) years of technical experience with three (3) or more years of experience within sales preferred and a high school diploma/GED required
Experience with Buy & Bill and/or Specialty Pharmacy products is preferred, in both health systems and private practice
Ability to lift/pull 25–100 lb. training models and meet necessary hospital credentialing/vaccination requirements
Valid driver’s license: Ability to pass a pre-employment drug screening test and meet safe driving requirements
Ability to travel adequately to cover territory, as well as overnight attendance at scheduled training events and sales meetings
Documented history of strong sales performance, preferably in a clinical/technical/consultative sales role with multiple decision makers is preferred. Ability to manage a complex sell, learn procedural, technical, clinical, and anatomical information quickly and communicate/present/train to a variety of audiences
An essential requirement of your position is to satisfy all applicable health care industry representative (HCIR) credentialing requirements to gain and maintain entry into facilities and organizations that are in your assigned territory. You must also be in good standing and/or eligible to obtain these credentials.
These HCIR credentialing requirements may include, but are not limited to, background checks, drug screens, proof of immunization/vaccination for various diseases, fingerprinting and specific licenses required by individual state or cities. Please remember that you are solely responsible for ensuring that you satisfy all HCIR credentialing requirements and for any associated liability for failing to do so. AbbVie has resources available to you to help answer questions you may have.

title: Associate Director, Biomarker Program Management
description:
About AbbVie
AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. For more information about AbbVie, please visit us at  www.abbvie.com . Follow @abbvie on  LinkedIn,   Facebook ,  Instagram ,  X  and  YouTube.
The Precision Medicine (PMed) Immunology and Neuroscience organization at AbbVie uses advanced methods to discover biomarkers and implement translational strategies to advance AbbVie’s innovative Immunology and Neuroscience pipeline.
The Associate Director, Biomarker Program Management, leads a team within the Immunology and Neuroscience therapeutic area that connects science and operations to manage biomarker research for multiple Phase 1-3 clinical trials. This role provides vision for operational and logistical strategies to ensure clinical trials are executed with quality and efficiency, on-time, within budget, and meet objectives. The Associate Director achieves these objectives via scientific expertise, strategic thinking, a global mindset, team building and cross-functional collaboration. This role can be based in North Chicago, IL, Waltham, MA, or South San Francisco, CA.
Responsibilities:
Lead team of Biomarker Project Managers and Sample Operations Managers to facilitate the implementation of PMed research into AbbVie clinical trials. Provide management and mentoring for team members; responsible for developing the expertise of team members. Set a positive and motivating work environment that encourages mutual respect, innovation, and accountability at all levels.
Assign approved programs and trials to team members and ensure team members are resourced, trained, and employed to start up, manage and close clinical trials. This includes partnering with PMed Biomarker Leads and being responsible for editing clinical documents, sample management, data management, cross-functional teams, budget management and strategy documents. Programs are executed to meet required timelines, budgets, and regulatory requirements. May directly manage key clinical projects within PMed.
Manage biomarker operations and logistics to support the clinical trial schedule. Proactively identify, resolve, mitigate, and/or escalate biomarker study-related risks and issues.
Ensure vendors are managed per AbbVie procedures including selection, contract execution and management. Assist in the management of Oncology budgets, ensuring accurate projections are provided to Finance monthly, quarterly, and yearly, adjusting as appropriate to keep actual variances low.
Help set Vision for Biomarker Program Management group that enables continuous improvement in processes and efficiency. Explore potential opportunities for expanding services and capabilities of BPM. Identify gaps and spearhead special development projects, as needed.
Serve as liaison with leaders of cross-functional stakeholders within AbbVie. Responsible for collaborating with personnel in other Precision Medicine groups to drive consistency within and between groups.
Apply and adhere to ICH/GCP, biosample storage procedures, biosample management best practices and ethical guidelines.
Ph.D. Degree with 8+ years project management, life science and/or clinical trial experience or Master’s Degree with 10+ years project management, life science and/or clinical trial experience or Bachelor’s Degree with 14+ years of project management, life science and/or clinical trial experience
Excellent oral and written communication skills in English. Expertise in MS Office applications including Excel, Word, Project and PowerPoint.
Organization, attention to detail and effective time management with an ability to adapt to changing priorities. Excellent analytical and interpersonal skills. Experience interacting with various levels within the organization as well as vendors.
Proven success in running meetings, working collaboratively in a cross-functional environment, and driving for success
3+ years of people management experience. Effective people management and leadership skills with a proven ability to foster team productivity and cohesiveness.
Preferred:
PMP certification desired.
Competent in application of standard business procedures (standard operating procedures, International Conference on Harmonization {ICH}, Global Regulations, Ethics and Compliance)
Experience working in a quality control and regulatory-rich environment. Experience holding meetings by teleconference and working with colleagues remotely.
Scientific background and knowledge of biomarkers. Exposure to companion diagnostic development. Knowledge of image data and associated testing.
Key Leadership Competencies:
Builds strong relationships with peers and cross-functionally with partners outside of team to enable higher performance
Learns fast, grasps the “essence,” and can change course quickly when required
Raises the bar and is never satisfied with the status quo
Creates a learning environment, open to suggestions and experimentation for improvement
Embraces the ideas of others, nurtures innovation and manages innovation to reality
Thinks beyond the program being managed to the strategy and operations of the broader Precision Medicine organization and the Development division
Act as a thought leader and mentor for team members; seek to develop the skillsets of others

description:
About AbbVie
AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. For more information about AbbVie, please visit us at  www.abbvie.com . Follow @abbvie on  LinkedIn,   Facebook ,  Instagram ,  X  and  YouTube.
Purpose
The Associate Director, Customs Valuation Compliance & Reporting, is a critical compliance role that actively partners across the enterprise and leads the operations and strategic design of the end-to-end customs valuation and reconciliation process.  Responsibilities include leading the financial planning and reporting of customs tariff impact to AbbVie’s imports (primarily focused on the Americas region) by conducting relevant variance analyses, scenario modeling and developing executive-ready reports; leading customs valuation initiatives in collaboration with stakeholders from other departments; and ensuring accuracy and predictability of tariff costs and other customs reporting metrics.
Responsibilities
Ensure compliance with U.S. Customs and Border Protection laws and regulations in the areas of customs valuation reporting
Lead QA / data integrity work in partnership with key cross functional partners (e.g.  Tax, Corporate Accounting, Operations Controller Team, Supply Chain)
Lead scenario planning and modeling collaboratively with key stakeholders to identify tariff costs of various levels of the supply chain that will contribute to production planning decisions
Develop opportunities to utilize technology and enhance existing processes related to declaring and reporting final customs values through the reconciliation process
Develop and manage the program governance and controls for key trade program strategies for AbbVie
Primary SME on the review of contracts to determine potential customs valuation considerations (e.g., royalties)
Manage resource(s) supporting the existing customs valuation processes and strategies
Participate in governance forums and interface with various levels of leadership
Advise and support cross-functional activities as new tariff regulations are enacted
Qualifications:
Bachelor’s Degree in Finance or Accounting, CPA or MBA a plus
Minimum [7+] years of leadership experience, including Operations / Supply Chain Finance
Proficiency in SAP (S4/Hana) module expertise particularly in Finance and Controlling and Materials Management
Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint are essential
Strong financial acumen, including cost accounting principles and financial analysis
Exceptional analytical and problem-solving skills, with proven ability to make data-driven decisions
Demonstrated cross-functional leadership skills
Superior organizational skills and attention to detail
Ability to recognize opportunities to simplify processes and create efficiencies
Highly adaptable to new information and shifting priorities; demonstrated ability to multitask
Strong executive-ready communication skills
Preferred Qualifications:
MBA or advanced degree
International or global work experience
Key Leadership Competencies:
Solid business judgment capable of driving a diverse organization to the right results with a focused, pragmatic approach
Builds strong cross-functional relationships with business partners and geographically dispersed team members to enable higher performance
Demonstrated “executive presence” and ability to represent team in a professional manner with Senior Leadership
Ability to work independently in a fast-paced and rapidly changing environment; adaptable to last-minute changes in requirements or priorities
Advanced analytical and process diagnostic skills and the ability to get into the details, while also understanding and driving the full team to achieve results in line with the “big picture” objectives
Learns fast, grasps the 'essence' and can change course quickly
Ability to make solid decisions with minimal information

The Data Protection Specialist works with various internal and external groups to ensure that AbbVie information security policies, practices, and procedures are properly implemented within AbbVie. They support the Data Protection Office in strengthening company data security controls and maturing operational processes. The individual will interface with a wide variety of people from different internal organizational units, interface with organizational personnel and staff to ensure that the policy is understood by those required to implement, monitor, and enforce the policy. This role is designed for a professional with an engineering, computer science, software development, or related technical background who is interested in the business, governance, and assurance aspects of data security. Conduct assessments of controls to ensure data protection controls are in place.
Leverage AI to analyze volumes of data across File Labeling, Application logs, and infrastructure datasets to automate control assurance.
Engage AbbVie Third Party Vendors to assess security posture, remediation requirements, and compensating controls as they apply to Business Applications.
Develop in-depth knowledge of AbbVie Information Security policies, processes, and procedures, as well as compliance processes and initiatives to provide subject matter expertise and guidance to other organizations (Commercial, R&D, Audit, Legal, Purchasing, etc.) within AbbVie in these matters.
Provide Information Security expertise and guidance to Business group leaders and IT Owners to ensure an appropriate balance between security risks and business enablement for identified business programs and initiatives.
Provide reporting to management on potential Data Privacy risks and planned remediation.
Act as point of contact regarding Information Security matters and AbbVie security policies for AbbVie Purchasing, Legal/Privacy and Quality.
Review current technology and information policies and practices for continued applicability with respect to AbbVie commercial and R&D business programs. Provide recommendations for improvements.
Required:
Bachelor’s Degree with 5 years of experience; OR Master's Degree with 4 years of experience in Information Security, Data Privacy, or IT Compliance experience.
Familiarity with, and experience using, a variety of information security control frameworks, including, but not limited to: NIST Cybersecurity Framework, ISO 2700X, PCI-DSS, SWIFT, Cloud Controls Matrix, HITRUST, NIST 800-171, CIS Controls, etc.
Familiarity with global and regional Data Privacy regulations such as GDPR, HIPAA, and CCPA.
Experience aligning and testing information security controls and frameworks.
Experience writing policies and procedures.

Strong project management, collaboration, communication, and organizational skills.

Purpose:
For the Biologics Analytical R&D department at the AbbVie site in North Chicago, we are looking for an experienced leader to guide a diverse team of scientists supporting AbbVie's pipeline of monoclonal antibodies (mAbs), multispecific antibodies, Antibody Drug Conjugates (ADCs), Antibody Oligonucleotide Conjugates (AOCs), tLNPs, Peptides and other biologics. The team develops state-of-the-art, innovative potency assays, including cell-based and binding assays, using the latest technology standards, and drives industry-leading analytical methods and control strategies that advance programs through clinical development.
Responsibilities:
Build and leads a newly formed team of up to 10 dedicated scientists and people leaders, with recruitment and hiring required to staff the team, in charge of potency and molecule characterization assay development for single and combined biological mode of actions (MoA) as single point of contact and center of excellence in Development Sciences. This includes formulation and process development support, QC-ability assessment of discovery assays, improvement or development of alternative and new assay formats, assay validation, routine testing and tech transfers for early, mid and late-stage development programs e.g. for traditional antibody formats, multispecific antibodies, fusion proteins, ADCs, AOCs, and other biologics, directed against neurological, immunological and oncological diseases, as well as novel complex therapeutic areas such as gene therapies.
Builds a strong scientific interface to structural characterization units globally and locally to support assessment and elucidation of molecule liabilities and critical quality attributes related to binding and biological activity (structure-function relationship). Supports and guides adjacent organizations with scientific expertise on novel binding and biological activity formats for internal and external programs as global center of excellence (e. g. due diligences, partnered programs).
Defines and sets the framework for a global development strategy of potency assays for traditional and novel therapeutic areas: assay format of cell-based and binding assays, potency assay implementation, validation and method comparability strategy in a GMP and scientific environment.
Fosters innovation and implementation of new technologies and platformability assessments in the field of traditional and novel formats such as automation and robotics to streamline development routine testing and cell banking, for early and mid-stage development programs.
Provides infrastructure, processes and scientific and quality oversight for cell cultivation, critical reagent management, business and compliance processes in assigned area of responsibility, interacts with external service providers (e. g. transfer or co-validation of test methods). Ensures potency assay and knowledge transfer to commercial organizations. Also serves as R&D subject matter expert for troubleshooting and investigation of NBE pipeline assets.
Provides leadership, strategic guidance and talent development for groups of highly skilled analytical scientists, and ensures analytical deliverables are achieved within set timelines, budgets and regulatory frameworks.
Recruit, promote, and retain top talents via coaching and mentoring and assures effective succession planning.
Collaborates with stakeholders and partner organizations, such as:
Discovery for technical transfer or development of MoA assay formats
Analytical Leads across sites
NBE tech centers (AIMS/Characterization Teams)
NBE project teams
Outsourcing

Operations

Experience in research and/or development environment.

title: Head of Patient Advocacy and Professional Societies Engagement - Oncology (Medical Affairs)
description:
About AbbVie
AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. For more information about AbbVie, please visit us at  www.abbvie.com . Follow @abbvie on  LinkedIn,   Facebook ,  Instagram ,  X  and  YouTube.
The  Head of Patient Advocacy and Professional Societies Engagement - Oncology  leads the global strategy for building, managing, and sustaining authentic, high-impact relationships with cancer patient advocacy organizations (PAOs), professional oncology societies, and key policy stakeholders.
This leadership role will embed a patient-centric mindset across the Global Oncology Medical Affairs enterprise. will ensure the patient voice shapes clinical pathways across our robust portfolio of Antibody-Drug Conjugates (ADCs), T-Cell Engagers (TCEs), and targeted small molecules.  Will manage, mentor, and develop a high-performing global team of 4 direct reports focused entirely on the hematology and solid tumor landscape.
Position will be based from an AbbVie major R&D site and follow a hybrid model of 3 days/week on-site. Locations include Mettawa, IL (headquarters), Florham Park, NJ, Waltham, MA, San Francisco, CA, and Irvine, CA.
Key Responsibilities
Global Strategy & Pipeline Integration:  Design and execute the multi-year global engagement strategy for oncology PAOs aligned with AbbVie’s core therapeutic focus areas, spanning  Hematologic Malignancies  (CLL, AML, DLBCL, Multiple Myeloma) and  Solid Tumors  (NSCLC, SCLC, Ovarian Cancer, Colorectal Cancer).
Modality-Specific Advocacy:  Develop specialized, tailored patient engagement frameworks for next-generation modalities, capturing patient and caregiver insights unique to  Topoisomerase I inhibitor (Top1i)–based ADCs  and immune-based pipelines.
Team Leadership & Development:  Lead, mentor, and scale a team of 4 direct reports, fostering a culture of compliance, clinical fluency, and cross-functional collaboration in the complex global oncology space.
Clinical Trial Co-Creation:  Partner with clinical development to leverage patient organization insights to optimize trial designs, decentralized trial models, and patient-reported outcomes (PROs) for late-stage and registrational pipeline assets.
Professional Oncology Alliances:  Cultivate strategic partnerships with primary global professional organizations (such as  ASCO, ESMO, ASH, WCLC, and SGO ) to advance scientific exchange, consensus-building, and independent medical educational grants.
Launch Readiness & Access Advocacy:  Work cross-functionally to bridge medical strategy with health equity, supporting access and addressing policy and reimbursement barriers ahead of major regulatory approvals and label expansions.
Compliance & Transparency:  Ensure all team interactions adhere to regional legal/compliance codes (such as PhRMA, EFPIA, IFPMA) and navigate rigorous Fair Market Value (FMV) standards for multi-stakeholder healthcare collaborations.
Education:  Advanced degree in a health science, life sciences, public health, or healthcare policy field (PharmD, PhD, MSN, or Master’s/MBA in Health Administration or Policy preferred).
Experience:  10+ years of progressive experience in pharmaceutical Global/US Medical Affairs, Patient Advocacy, Corporate Affairs, or External Relations, with a minimum of 5 years dedicated exclusively to the Oncology/Hematology ecosystem.
People Management:  Proven experience managing, coaching, and developing direct reports (prior experience leading a team of 3–5+ matrix or direct reports is required).
Scientific & Pipeline Literacy:  Solid comprehension of cancer biology markers (e.g., c-Met, BCMA, SEZ6) and the operational nuances of managing clinical expectations around breakthrough designations.
Competencies: Strong existing networks within international oncology advocacy coalitions and professional society executive teams.
Exceptional interpersonal, diplomacy, and executive communication skills.
Demonstrated commitment to driving health equity and reducing disease awareness gaps in underserved cancer patient populations.
Ability to navigate complex matrix organizations on a global scale.

Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts in clear, customer-friendly language.
Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills, with attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple priorities.
Demonstrated ability to collaborate across product, engineering, operations, support, security, and business teams.
Customer-centered mindset with an interest in simplifying complex processes and improving how people interact with technology.
Ability to use feedback and data to identify patterns, recommend improvements, and measure results.

Data Review Rules
SDTM mapping

Study-level tables, listings, or figures
Product-level safety analysis displays

Ensuring consistency across standard types (e.g. eCRF standards align with TLF standards, SDTM standards align with ADaM standards, etc.)
Develop training materials to the organization on the proper use of standards in pipeline activities

Providing feedback on CRF design and SDTM datasets to ensure data are collected and represented in a manner that support regulatory requirements to comply with CDISC standards (CDASH, SDTM and ADaM) and AbbVie standard extensions to CDISC
Review and provide feedback on SDTM Trial Design Domains
SDTM Programming based on SDTM specifications
Oversee the creation of SDTM datasets, define.xml, annotated CRF and Clinical Study Data Reviewer’s Guides for both FDA and PMDA submissions
Consult on conformance issues for SDTM and/or ADaM and work with the study team to resolve the problem either by correcting the data or metadata, or by providing an appropriate explanation
Other responsibilities include:
representing AbbVie’s interests in industry standards development projects,
staying current with industry standards such as CDISC, and the regulatory requirements related to their use
identifying improvements to the processes and content of standards, and driving those improvements to completion

Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.
The Community You Will Join:
Airbnb is seeking an Advanced Analytics Intern to join the Finance Data Science & Strategy team within the Finance organization for the 2027 Summer Intern Program.
The Finance Data Science & Strategy team builds the statistical models behind Airbnb’s top line forecast and explains how the business performs against it. The work runs as a loop. We figure out where actuals differ from forecast and why, share the answer with partners across Finance and the business, and feed what we learned into the next version of the forecast, so each cycle starts from a better baseline than the last.
We are looking for someone curious about business and data, who can understand both the ‘what’ and the ‘why’ behind a number and help translate them into decisions. An ideal candidate would have some familiarity with analytical methodologies, BI tooling, and business communication.
The Difference You Will Make:
As an Advanced Analytics Intern on our team, you’ll help explain how the business performed against the forecast and use what you find to improve it. You’ll have the opportunity to:
Build comprehensive and high quality analyses of how the business is performing against the forecast, and explain what drove the difference
Work with the team’s data scientists to turn those findings into improvements in the next version of the forecast
Communicate findings clearly to partners across Finance and the business, in written readouts and recurring reviews
A Typical Day:
During your internship you’ll be integrated into a team where you’ll contribute to challenging projects. Your manager, team, and our incredible employee community will strive to be superhosts to you during the summer. We provide the support, mentorship, fun, and real world experience needed to accelerate your learning and make a real impact on our business, as Airbnb revolutionizes connection, belonging, and travel. You’ll be expected to:
Own and complete a capstone project from beginning to end
Collaborate with multiple team members to achieve project milestones
Communicate with stakeholders across different teams to provide project updates
Seek and provide feedback throughout the internship
Actively participate in and contribute to the Finance Data Science & Strategy team and broader Airbnb community
Your Expertise:
This opportunity is for full-time students completing a Master’s degree in a quantitative field (e.g. Data Science, Mathematics, Analytics, Statistics, Econometrics, etc.) with at least one semester of school remaining after the internship.
Proficient in communication and collaboration, with the ability to effectively engage with diverse teams and individuals
Skilled in conducting thorough and inclusive analyses, ensuring that findings are communicated clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.
Possesses robust data, statistical analysis, and analytics skills, contributing to a comprehensive understanding of complex datasets.
Substantial experience in SQL, along with a solid foundation in at least one programming language (Python or R)
Preferred (not required): Familiarity with forecasting, time series, and/or A/B testing
Demonstrated interest in high growth, technology, and/or hospitality companies

title: Lead, Quality, Elevated Support
description:
Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.
The Community You Will Join:
The Partner QA Lead is the Airbnb Quality owner for the Elevated Support service tier across a portfolio of Community Support BPO partner sites. Working across partner QA teams, this role makes sure that each site scores interactions consistently, calibrates to the same standard as Airbnb, and turns what it finds into insight that Delivery and Partners can act on.
The Difference You Will Make:
Elevated Support is Airbnb's newest Community Support service tier, built for guests with urgent, complex or high-stakes issues. Cases are identified by an Elevated decisioning model, routed to a dedicated pool of specialized Specialists across voice, async and back-office queues, and supported around the clock by partner sites in multiple regions and languages. Its north-star metric is NPS, case resolution, cost per case, and reopen rate. Because the tier is new, its quality targets, scorecard and evaluation approach are still maturing, and this role helps set them.
The Partner QA Lead is paired with a Delivery (Ops) counterpart: Quality owns the standard, the evidence and the diagnosis, and Delivery and Quality partner on actions.
This is a hands-on, partner-facing execution role and a subject matter expert on Airbnb's quality standards. The Partner QA Lead is responsible for making the Quality program work on the ground: holding partner QA teams accountable, running calibration on the Lead With Hospitality (LWH) COPC form, diagnosing behavior opportunities before the weekly business reviews, and driving actions to address issues and opportunities for guests with urgent, high-stakes needs. The role works closely with the Quality Leads, other Partner QA Leads, Delivery, Training, Knowledge Management, the Elevated Support program team and Business Process Improvement (BPI), and is expected to become an expert in new standards and tools, such as Lead With Hospitality (LWH) QA framework and Observe.AI, and then to drive adoption across its partners.
A Typical Day:
Partner Quality Program Execution
Own the day-to-day execution of the Quality program for the Elevated Support service tier and the corresponding partner sites, languages and queues (voice, async and back office), including weekly QA evaluation targets, evaluation completeness, and coaching activity within your portfolio.
Validate performance data before every business review (WBR, MBR, QBR): confirm that partner QA scores are complete, accurate and comparable, then explain week-over-week movements in a short, clear narrative that Delivery and partner leadership can act on.
Run the Quality portion of each partner's operating cadence: weekly QA syncs, a pre-sync with your ROM/POM before each WBR, and the monthly and quarterly business reviews.
Partner Governance & Accountability
Hold partner QA teams to the Partner Scorecard: evaluation completeness, calibration accuracy, coaching effectiveness and actionable insights. Document gaps and agree action plans with owners and dates.
Audit the auditors: sample and re-score partner evaluations to confirm they follow the standard, and escalate sustained performance gaps to the Quality Lead.
Support new partner site onboarding, language expansion and site visits, making sure each new Elevated Support site and cohort is certified and calibrated to Airbnb standards before it scales, including interim QA coverage by experienced partner QAs while a new site stands up its own team.
Calibration & LWH Standards
Run calibration sessions across your Elevated Support partner sites on the LWH form, including evaluations scored at case level across every Specialist who touched the case, and track alignment at attribute and causal-factor level, so that quality is measured the same way regardless of partner or geography.
Support partner Team Lead calibration, including the weekly sessions that Partner Quality runs within each site, so Team Leads coach specialists in the same language as Quality.
Triage partner feedback on the form and recommend scoring guide updates through the Calibration DRI. Quality owns the standard; partners do not change it locally.
Insights, NPS Detractor Analysis & Escalation
Lead NPS detractor analysis, including the Global Detractor Analysis (GDA) framework, for Elevated Support, where NPS is the north-star metric. Correlate QA results with NPS, reopen rate, AQS and other operational KPIs, and point partner QA effort toward the sites, languages and case types that need it most.
Partner with Delivery, WFM and the Elevated Support program team to establish and refine QA targets and the tier scorecard, using LWH data to recommend realistic, evidence-based targets (for example where sites report they cannot reach targets carried over from volume tiers) and to monitor early-life performance of new sites and cohorts.
Validate the Elevated model end to end: sample cases to confirm the right cases are being identified and escalated to the tier, that handoffs and transfers (including to Premium Support and language queues) work as intended, and that the tier is staffed and routed so guests reach an Elevated Specialist.
Deep-dive repeat trends and build the business case for them. Route issues by type: tactical issues (coaching, site issues fixable with Learning Loft content) go to partner QA teams and Delivery, and macro issues go to OneTrack with an evidence pack, together with your ROM/POM.
Give partner QA teams and Delivery the data they need to find root cause: by partner, site, Specialist cohort, Specialist quartile and contact reason.
Share best practices with other Partner QA Leads, and cover for peers or the Quality Lead during staffing gaps, including language or regional coverage and short rotations.
Tools, Reporting & Cross-Functional Rollouts
Drive adoption of Observe.AI across your Elevated Support partner sites, including AutoQA review and annotation, access and permission hygiene, and the transition from interim evaluation forms to Observe.AI.
Be an expert on every new Quality initiative, such as LWH, Global Detractor Analysis, and Specialist Investigation Skills, and cascade it to your partners with clear expectations, training and follow-up.
Represent Quality for Elevated Support in cross-functional working groups (Product, program management, Knowledge Management, Training, Workforce and Routing) as the single point of contact for your partners, and make sure quality findings that point to policy, workflow or product gaps are raised, not left as coaching notes.
Protect partner QA capacity for strategic work such as deep dives and root-cause analysis, rather than ad hoc requests that are outside agreed scope.
Your Expertise:
6+ years of experience in Community or Customer Support Quality, Operations or a related field, including direct experience with QA programs across BPO or partner networks and experience supporting high-touch, escalated or premium service tiers.
Bachelor's Degree, preferably in related field required.
Demonstrated experience driving partner accountability: running calibration sessions, reviewing partner QA scorecards, and writing and following through on improvement plans with BPO QA teams.
Working knowledge of COPC methodology or an equivalent governance model: sampling requirements, calibration, and objective, behavior-based scoring forms.
Strong analytical skills: able to read weekly QA and KPI data (NPS, CSAT, iSAT, reopen rate, cost per case), diagnose the cause of score movements, and turn it into a clear narrative for Delivery and partner leadership.
Experience with QA platforms such as Observe.AI, or equivalent, including calibration management, form use and review of automated or AI-assisted scoring.
Excellent written and verbal communication; able to run a productive calibration session across time zones and present quality findings to senior Delivery stakeholders with confidence.

description:
An execution-focused project/program manager responsible for the hands-on coordination and completion of power capacity and hydrogen fuel cell projects across the Amazon fulfillment network. This is a delivery role with a strong bias for action: the PM owns the details, gets into the field, and drives projects from feasibility through commissioning and handover. Oversees multiple concurrent projects spanning temporary and permanent power deployment (utility upgrades, generator installations, switchgear deployments, and air permitting) as well as hydrogen fuel cell execution — including decommissioning of existing assets, launch of new hydrogen infrastructure and fuel cells per Amazon standards and processes, and conversions of existing sites. Sets deadlines, assigns responsibilities, and personally tracks and unblocks progress. Prepares reports for upper management regarding the status of all projects.
Requires a bachelor's degree and at least 4 years of project management experience in power infrastructure, electrical systems, hydrogen/fuel cell systems, or a related area. The ideal candidate is a hands-on, detail-oriented operator who thrives in ambiguity, dives deep into technical and schedule details, and acts with urgency rather than waiting for direction. Must be familiar with a variety of the field's concepts, practices, and procedures across both power and hydrogen domains. Relies on sound judgment to plan and accomplish goals, and is comfortable rolling up sleeves — walking the site, reading the drawings, chasing the long-lead order, and closing out the punch list. Leads and directs the work of contractors, vendors, and cross-functional teams. A wide degree of creativity and latitude is expected to solve complex energy infrastructure challenges across diverse site conditions and regulatory environments. Typically reports to a manager or head of a unit/department.
Key job responsibilities
Project Management & Bias for Action
- Own delivery end to end and act with urgency — move projects forward every day rather than waiting for direction or escalation
• Get into the details: read the drawings, interrogate the schedule, understand the single-line and the hydrogen P&ID, and verify the numbers personally

• Proactively identify blockers and drive them to closure; dive deep on root cause and remove obstacles for contractors and cross-functional teams
• Run a tight operating rhythm — stand-ups, weekly reviews, and crisp written updates that make status and risks unambiguous
• Make decisions with incomplete information, bias toward action, and course-correct quickly as new data emerges
Program Coordination & Oversight
• Responsible for the coordination and completion of multiple simultaneous power and hydrogen execution projects across U.S. sites
• Oversee all aspects of the execution program from feasibility through commissioning and handover
• Set deadlines, assign responsibilities, and monitor and summarize the progress of all projects
• Prepare reports for upper management regarding program status, including monthly flash updates and executive summaries
• Lead and direct the work of contractors, vendors, consultants, and cross-functional teams
• Perform a variety of tasks ranging from technical design review to stakeholder management to regulatory coordination
Amazon Standards, Specifications & Quality Assurance
• Follow and verify that Amazon standards, specifications, and processes are met across all power and hydrogen infrastructure installations
• Ensure electrical equipment, switchgear, generators, fuel cells, hydrogen storage/dispensing systems, and associated systems comply with Amazon technical standards and design requirements
• Conduct quality reviews at each project phase to validate adherence to Amazon specifications before progressing to the next milestone
• Verify vendor deliverables, shop drawings, and equipment submittals meet Amazon engineering standards
• Coordinate with Amazon internal engineering teams to resolve specification questions and obtain approvals
• Document and track any deviations from Amazon specifications, securing proper waivers or corrective actions (e.g., Supplier Corrective Action Reports / SCARs)
Power Capacity Execution
• Drive execution of temporary and permanent power deployment projects — utility upgrades, generator installations, switchgear deployments, and service upgrades
• Oversee deployment of temporary and permanent natural gas and diesel generator systems (1–5MW scale), including rental genset mobilization and conversion to permanent power
• Manage utility coordination including transformer upgrades, switchgear installations, and service upgrades with utility companies
• Own the end-to-end switchgear (SWGR) procurement process: specification development, vendor selection, purchase order issuance, and delivery tracking
• Track SWGR lead times (typically 10–26 weeks) across all sites and ensure orders are placed to meet project timelines; monitor factory acceptance testing (FAT) and coordinate site delivery logistics
• Review and validate electrical designs, single-line diagrams, load calculations, and power distribution configurations
• Ensure compliance with NEC, NFPA, and local electrical codes
Hydrogen Fuel Cell Execution
• Decommissioning: Plan and execute safe decommissioning of existing hydrogen infrastructure and fuel cell assets — isolation, purging/inerting, asset removal, site restoration, and disposition in accordance with Amazon standards and applicable safety codes
• Infrastructure & fuel cell launch: Lead the launch of new hydrogen infrastructure and fuel cells per Amazon standards and processes — hydrogen storage and dispensing systems, hydrogen pads, piping, fueling infrastructure, and fuel cell power modules, from design review through installation, commissioning, and startup
• Conversions: Manage conversions of existing sites to hydrogen fuel cell operation (or between configurations), coordinating the transition sequencing, infrastructure modifications, and cutover to minimize operational disruption
• Coordinate with hydrogen fuel cell vendors and OEMs (e.g., Plug Power and equivalents) on equipment specifications, delivery schedules, and field support
• Verify hydrogen systems meet Amazon specifications and applicable hydrogen safety and fire codes (e.g., NFPA 2, NFPA 55) throughout design, installation, and commissioning
• Oversee fuel cell capacity planning, dispenser configuration, and integration with site power and operations
Procurement & Long-Lead Equipment Management
• Own procurement for long-lead equipment across both domains — switchgear, generators, fuel cells, and hydrogen infrastructure components
• Specify, order, track lead times, verify specifications, and coordinate delivery for critical-path equipment
• Coordinate with manufacturers and vendors on custom configurations and delivery schedules
• Escalate equipment delivery risks immediately when lead times threaten project schedules
Permitting & Regulatory
• Own the permitting process for all sites — air permit applications for stationary generator installations and hydrogen-related permits and approvals
• Prepare and submit permit applications across multiple jurisdictions and regulatory environments; track application status, agency review timelines, and approval milestones for each site
• Navigate complex permitting scenarios including CEQA approvals, non-attainment areas, emission offset requirements, and hydrogen/fire code approvals
• Coordinate with environmental and fire/life-safety consultants to develop applications, emission calculations, and hazard analyses
• Maintain a permit tracking log with submission dates, agency contacts, expected approval dates, and required follow-ups
• Proactively identify permitting risks and develop contingency plans to avoid schedule impacts; ensure all required emission and safety data is obtained from generator and fuel cell vendors
Project Execution & Delivery
• Drive the end-to-end project lifecycle: feasibility, design, procurement, permitting, installation, commissioning, and handover
• Develop and maintain detailed project schedules, budgets, risk registers, and status reports
• Coordinate contractor mobilization, equipment procurement, and installation activities
• Identify and resolve critical-path blockers with urgency; escalate issues proactively
• Rely on extensive experience and judgment to plan and accomplish goals under compressed timelines
Stakeholder Management
• Serve as the primary point of contact and single-threaded owner across all project stakeholders, aligning internal and external parties and holding each accountable to deliverables and timelines
• Customer — Amazon Operations: partner with Amazon Operations (the internal customer) to understand site requirements, manage expectations, minimize operational disruption, and secure buy-in through launch and handover
• General Contractor (GC): direct and hold the GC accountable for construction scope, schedule, RFIs, submittals, and field execution
• Engineer of Record (EOR) & Architect of Record (AOR): coordinate design intent, drawing reviews, RFIs, and design changes; ensure the installed work conforms to the stamped design
• Electrical Contractor (EC): coordinate electrical installation, terminations, testing, and energization activities and sequencing
• Air permitting agencies & consultants: engage regulatory agencies and environmental consultants (e.g., Trinity) to secure and maintain air permits and keep applications on the critical path
• Utility engagement — gas pipeline: drive utility coordination for natural gas pipeline connections, metering, pressure requirements, service applications, and interconnection timelines
• Equipment vendors & OEMs: manage generator, switchgear, fuel cell, and hydrogen infrastructure vendors on specifications, lead times, and field support
• Coordinate with Property/Construction Managers (PCMs) and Construction Managers at each site
• Provide weekly status updates and monthly program reports to leadership
Site Launches, Commissioning & Energization
• Travel to project sites during critical installation, commissioning, and decommissioning phases
• Oversee equipment startup, testing, and acceptance procedures for both power and hydrogen systems
• Ensure safe energization, hydrogen system startup, and transition to operations

- Experience using data and metrics to determine and drive improvements

Direct to Device (D2D) extends Leo to standard mobile phones and devices: a fully regenerative fifth-generation (5G) mobile base station on each satellite, delivering service to standard handsets through mobile network operators (MNOs). D2D Software builds the embedded software that flies, the cloud and ground software that runs the service, and the platform that connects them. Our target is under a day from a defect being found to the fix deployed across the entire constellation, achieved by automating everything that a person would otherwise do by hand.
This role leads the program for integration, verification and reliability, labs, and release in Software Delivery & Business Ops, reporting to the Director, Software Delivery & Business Ops. It owns the integrated lab plan, lead times, and fallbacks; the technical program manager for Software Integration, Verification & Reliability; the release train and the six-eyes sign-off process; supplier delivery for lab and test vendors. Before anything is handed on, the bar is: positive float for every lab need-by date; every release with its three sign-offs. It hands off to its customers as follows: integrated lab plan and release calendar to Software Integration, Verification & Reliability, DevOps, and the hardware teams.
What the team needs to achieve
• Positive float for every lab need-by date; every release with its three sign-offs.
• Experience that meet their service level: integrated lab plan and release calendar to Software Integration, Verification & Reliability, DevOps, and the hardware teams.
• Measured, rising capability and efficiency of the team, with manual work falling release over release.
How the team is measured
• Lab readiness float against every gate's need-by date.
• Rig queue wait within its service level.
• Releases shipped with their sign-offs on time.
Key job responsibilities
• Own the integrated lab plan, lead times, and fallbacks; the technical program manager for Software Integration, Verification & Reliability; the release train and the six-eyes sign-off process; supplier delivery for lab and test vendors.
• Meet the bar before every hand-off: positive float for every lab need-by date; every release with its three sign-offs.
• Work directly with engineers in the boundary teams as partners, through agreed contracts and service levels.

• Run the program's mechanisms, metrics, and reviews, and clear blockers with the right people, escalating when needed.
• Identify and mitigate program risks early, build consensus across teams, and mentor other program managers.
This role is the technical program manager for Software Integration, Verification & Reliability. It owns the integrated lab plan for D2D Software (lab and rig lead times, capacity, fallbacks, and escalation), runs the release train and the six-eyes sign-off process, and owns supplier delivery for lab, rig, and test vendors. The sign-offs themselves stay independent: integration and verification, DevOps & Release, and this function each sign for their own part. It matters because embedded software testing depends on scarce rigs, benches, and chambers that take months to build, and because every release needs its sign-offs on time. Without it, labs arrive after the gates need them, releases wait on paperwork, and development and test teams wait for hardware.

Milestones are committed deadlines for delivery with quality, not gates to wait on, and every team runs on one toolchain and one system of record. Every measure is derived from the systems of record, never self-reported, and we improve release over release with a target of perfection.

title: Program Manager II, Transportation Engineering Systems, Transportation Engineering Systems
description:
As a Program Manager on the Transportation Engineering Systems (TESS) team, you will learn how Amazon's proprietary transportation systems make decisions to move packages from the fulfillment network to customers. You will manage system configuration changes that control those systems, working directly with business leaders and program teams to create new transportation flows and design configurations that execute at scale. In this role, you will execute network design changes, dive deep into package flows, troubleshoot system errors, identify process improvements, and build automation, analytics, and reporting capabilities leveraging AI.
Key job responsibilities
Manage system configuration changes across Amazon's proprietary transportation systems to support new and existing package flows
Track program milestones and communicate status to business leaders and stakeholders
Execute network design changes end-to-end, coordinating with business leaders and program teams to ensure timely delivery
Dive deep into package flow data to troubleshoot system errors, identify root causes, and implement fixes
Identify process improvement opportunities and build automation to reduce manual effort and increase accuracy
Develop analytics and reporting capabilities leveraging AI to drive data-driven decision-making
Proactively identify and mitigate risks in system configurations before they impact customers
Document processes, standard operating procedures, and configuration playbooks for the team

Your daily execution responsibilities will come via an intake queue which generates work tickets assigned to you. There could be a variety of audit and reporting duties as well. You'll work autonomously to solve ambiguous problems, whether that's defining requirements for a new system feature or analyzing why a particular network configuration isn't performing as expected. Your work directly influences decisions about how Amazon moves packages from fulfillment centers to customers' doorsteps.

The Transportation Engineering Systems (TESS) team sits at the critical intersection of Amazon's business operations and technical infrastructure. We're responsible for configuring and optimizing the transportation network that powers Amazon's logistics operations globally. Our team culture values data-driven decision-making, customer obsession, and innovative problem-solving. We work collaboratively across organizational boundaries, partnering with operations teams, software engineers, and business leaders to deliver solutions that scale. As part of TESS, you'll contribute to systems that impact millions of customer deliveries while working with talented professionals who are passionate about operational excellence.

title: Senior Product Manager - Tech, Advertising, Full-Funnel Campaigns
description:
Amazon Advertising is looking for a Senior Product Manager to help define the product strategy for Full-Funnel Campaigns. You will own advertiser growth, running experiments and launching features to drive activation and retention. You will dive deep in the data, engage with advertisers, decide what to build, and ship it. This role offers the opportunity to shape the direction of one of Amazon's most important new advertising products from the ground up.
Key job responsibilities
Responsibilities:
- Own the FFC growth funnel end to end, including the outcomes, the key inputs, and the weekly mechanism that reviews them with leadership.
- Find where advertisers drop out and why, using SQL and console data yourself. Turn each finding into a prioritized bet with a stated size and a test that can prove it wrong.
- Run the growth roadmap: design and run experiments with tech partners, evaluate the results, and launch successful features at high velocity.
- Own the product relationships with key partner teams across Amazon Ads. Negotiate shared roadmaps, bring FFC requirements through their intake and design reviews, and make FFC a team they want to build with.
- Work with Sales, Marketing and Account Management on launch, onboarding and advertiser feedback, so what we hear from advertisers reaches the roadmap.
- Represent FFC growth in business reviews and annual planning.
Your contributions will be highly visible and instrumental in hitting goals carried by Amazon's leadership team (S-Team). A diverse group of stakeholders will rely on your vision and messaging, including advertisers, agencies, and internal ad sales and operations teams.
A day in the life
You start the morning on the growth dashboard. Yesterday's launches came in below trend, so you dive into the data to quickly root cause the change and decide whether any action is needed. Midmorning you meet a partner team to close requirements for a change to the ingress experience. After lunch you read out an experiment with your scientist: the change improved first-week retention, but only for one advertiser segment. Together you decide whether that's worth a second test or a targeted launch. You spend the afternoon working on a spec your engineers will start building next sprint.
About the team
Full-Funnel Campaigns make it easy for any advertiser who sells on Amazon to launch a coordinated campaign across sponsored ads, display, video, and streaming TV, with the goal of finding new customers and growing total sales with one budget and one optimization engine. We are a small product team with dedicated engineering, science and program management, working with partner teams across Ads. We move fast, with high judgement and a strong sense of ownership. Our PMs are expected to drive outcomes, not just launch features.

- Experience with feature delivery and tradeoffs of a product
- Experience contributing to engineering discussions around technology decisions and strategy related to a product
- Experience managing technical products or online services
- Experience in representing and advocating for a variety of critical customers and stakeholders during executive-level prioritization and planning
- Experience in advertising

description:
Fauna Robotics is building capable, safe, and delightful robots for everyday life. Before a new skill reaches a customer’s home, we need to know how well it works: how often it succeeds, how fast it is, and where it fails, across the range of homes and conditions our customers live in. We are hiring a Senior Technical Program Manager to run the operation that produces that evidence.
In this role, you will own robot evaluation operations end to end, in lab and home environments. Our scientists define what to measure; you make it happen at scale, on schedule, and with results the team can trust. You will turn evaluation requests from science and engineering into planned campaigns, keep robots, test environments, and operators ready, and deliver results that leaders use to decide what ships. You will treat evaluation as a production operation with measurable output, not a support function.
Key job responsibilities
- Own the evaluation program from intake to results: take requests from science and engineering teams, prioritize them against shared robot and lab capacity, and publish the campaign schedule
- Run evaluation campaigns in lab and home environments, with clear entry and exit criteria and standard run procedures
- Build and maintain the physical test environments: home-like lab setups, object and fixture inventories, scene resets, and versioned configurations so results stay comparable across software releases and robot hardware revisions
- Stand up in-home evaluation operations with legal, privacy, safety, and research partners, including scheduling, data handling, and on-site safety procedures
- Direct the work of evaluation operators and vendor teams: training and certification, shift coverage, and scoring standards that stay consistent across raters and sites
- Partner with hardware and fleet teams on robot availability for testing, including maintenance windows, repairs, and per-unit acceptance runs
- Enforce logging and traceability standards so every evaluation trial is reproducible and accounted for
- Deliver results as a product: standard scorecards and dashboards, triage of failures to the right owning team, and evidence that feeds launch and release go/no-go decisions
- Track throughput, valid-trial yield, cost per trial, and turnaround time, own the evaluation budget, and identify manual evaluations that are ready for automation or simulation
- Present evaluation status, risks, and tradeoffs to senior leadership, and say “not yet” when demand exceeds capacity
About the team
Fauna Robotics, an Amazon company, is building capable, safe, and genuinely delightful robots for everyday life. Our goal is simple: make robots people actually want to live and interact with in everyday human spaces.
We believe that future won’t arrive until building for robotics becomes far more accessible. Today, too much effort is spent reinventing the fundamentals. We’re changing that by developing tightly integrated hardware and software systems that make it faster, safer, and more intuitive to create real-world robotic products.
Our work spans the full stack: mechanical design, control systems, dynamic modeling, and intelligent software. The focus is not just functionality, but experience. We’re building robots that feel responsive, expressive, and genuinely useful.
At Fauna, you’ll work at the frontier of this space, helping define how robots move, manipulate, and interact with people in natural environments. It’s an opportunity to solve hard problems across hardware and software with a team focused on making robotics accessible and joyful to build.
If you care about making robotics real for everyone and building systems that are as delightful as they are capable, we’re interested in hearing from you.

title: Hardware Reliability Engineer - Mac System Reliability
description:
Apple is seeking a Reliability Engineer to join our Mac Hardware Reliability team!
In this role, you’ll collaborate with diverse hardware teams to ensure our products are not only durable and reliable, but also built to exceed expectations. From early concepts to field returns, you’ll lead cross-functional teams, design innovative reliability tests, and drive continuous product improvements.
At Apple, we don’t just follow industry standards—we push beyond them. We value creative problem-solving, dynamic thinking, and the ability to quickly adapt to new technical challenges. If you’re excited about tackling tough problems and shaping the future of amazing products, we’d love to have you on board!
As a System Reliability Engineer, you will play a key role in shaping our products, ensuring longevity by design. With these results, you will collaborate through design iterations ensuring our products meet high standards for customer experience.
You bring exceptional problem-solving skills and technical expertise, including:
- A deep understanding of material and device properties (mechanical, electrical, optical, thermal) and the underlying physics
- Proficiency in statistical data analysis and clear reporting, providing design risk assessments and guiding product improvements

- Proven ability to develop new reliability test procedures, create detailed test plans, and analyze results to assess design risks
Additional strengths that will set you apart:
- Ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously
- Capability to perform tests and troubleshoot issues independently
- Openness to take on new tasks
- A proactive, can-do attitude, with a passion for working alongside an amazing team and innovative products

Good written and verbal English communication skills. Ability to effectively communicate through email, WebEx, and phone
Ability to make clear and concise slides and presentations through keynote, excel, etc.
Strong attention to detail and curiosity of how technologies work
Able to use basic productivity apps such as email, web browser, calendar, WebEx/Zoom, spreadsheet, keynote/ppt, etc.
Preferred qualifications: M.S. or PhD in Materials Science, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or an equivalent field
Statistical experience such as Weibull, JMP, or familiarity with accelerated test models

Collaborative attitude and ability to cross-functionally work effectively
Ability to travel internationally without restriction (up to 10%)

This is a working manager role: you will personally originate and run a portfolio of strategic partnerships and market activation plans for Apple's highest-priority emerging technology initiatives, while building and coaching a team that runs the same playbook with increasing independence. No other platform company can pair this kind of ecosystem reach with Apple's architecture for privacy, security, and on-device intelligence — your job is to turn that architectural advantage into a commercial one, continuously, as hybrid AI redraws what partners and customers expect.
Because these partnerships are won on technology, you're a fit if you can go deep with engineers and architects on how it works and why it differentiates, and carry that substance into a funded, resourced, measurable commercial motion with C-suite leaders. You also bring the people instincts to grow a team of originators rather than just carry the portfolio yourself. We're looking for someone with big ideas who also knows how to get things built, funded, and shipped — a rare combination, and the core of this role.
As the Head of Emerging Technology Strategy & Partnerships, you will personally own a set of strategic initiatives and partnership pursuits end-to-end, while leading a team that owns equivalent portfolios across other emerging technology initiatives — from market activation and ecosystem engagement to technical solutioning and go-to-market design. As a working manager, you'll balance hands-on deal leadership with accountability for the people doing the same work: setting direction, developing capability, and ensuring the team operates as a high-performing, well-coached unit.
In this role, you will:
- Shape the How of Strategic Initiatives: Translate Apple's emerging technology bets into concrete market activation plans: the ecosystem required to pull the Apple platform through, the early adopters positioned to become lighthouse customers, and the enabling technologies and integrations needed to get there. You decide the motions, not just the destination — and you're accountable for measurable outcomes, not activity.

Your own deals set the standard and the playbooks your team is expected to run.

Each is a win-win anchored in a specific product or platform advantage, and you'll solution it hands-on with partner and Apple engineers: evaluating integration architectures, finding the gaps, and defining the software enhancements on both sides that unlock adoption. Carry what you learn into Apple's product and platform roadmap discussions with clear technical rationale and business impact, and hold your team to the same standard — every partnership rests on a technology thesis, not just a commercial one.
- Build Apple's Differentiated Advantage: Architect joint value propositions and go-to-market strategies that establish clear, differentiated advantage through Apple's platform — on-device AI, security, and privacy architecture — and the ecosystem around it. Articulate precisely where Apple's silicon, OS, and services differentiate from alternatives, and translate that into what a partner gains by building on Apple. As hybrid AI becomes the defining lever in enterprise technology, continuously evolve Apple's partner value proposition, and your team's skill set, to keep that advantage expanding.

description:
This is an exciting opportunity to work in a fast-paced environment and help shape the Company’s future. Get ready for your perfect job, one that encourages you to think analytically and work collaboratively with Apple business partners across the world.
The Places Finance team is seeking a manager to help support and drive the accounting and reporting for our global worldwide lease footprint, coupled with coordinating and assisting in operations on the lease payments side. This role manages Financial Analysts that are responsible for real estate lease accounting, external and management reporting, lease payment abstractions, and SOX compliance activities and controls to ensure the reporting accuracy of the Corporate and Retail Real Estate space. The Lease Accounting Manager will be responsible for accurate abstraction and reporting of leases associated with the real estate portfolio, 1600+, around the world for P&L and balance sheet. The Lease Accounting Manager will further provide strategic oversight to the Payments Team and support any system or operational initiatives. In this role, the Lease Accounting Manager will have a close partnership with Corporate and Retail Real Estate and Global Business Solution (GBS) teams to ensure accurate lease accounting and on-time payments worldwide in accordance with ASC 842 and Company policy. This position partners with many cross-functional business partners including Places (Corporate and Retail Real Estate), Technical Accounting, Legal, Tax, Business Assurance, software development teams, and Apple Global Business Solution teams around the world.
As a Lease Accounting Manager, you will perform senior level review of new lease agreements and amendments, as well as validation of lease accounting treatment assessments (finance vs. operating). title: Power Performance Modeling Architect - Platform Architecture
description:
Do you have a desire to seek out and solve exceedingly difficult challenges rather than the easy ones? Do you grow with adversity? Do you believe that truly valuable and meaningful accomplishments are the result of pushing the limits of perseverance? Do you believe that a world-class team with relentless drive can surpass even their own high expectations? We do! But we also realize this job isn’t for everyone. Experience in high-performance and low power microprocessor architecture and design techniques.
Experience coding in C, Python or similar programming languages.
Preferred qualifications: 20+ years relevant industry experience.
MS or PhD in Electrical or Computer Engineering or related engineering degree.
In depth understanding of CPU, GPU, Neural and ML workloads and applications.
Good understanding in control system application and behavior.
Expertise in high-performance SoC power delivery and thermals.
Excellent modeling and simulator development skills.
Ability to work with Claude to produce high quality code with validation.
