We are seeking a full-time Program Manager for Customer Support Strategy, based on-site at our DFW1 facility in Lewisville, TX. Your focus is reducing ticket volume, claims, and contra revenue, and improving the merchant experience. You will do this by improving support processes, ops processes, and engineering, by gathering merchant feedback (starting with NPS) and working cross-functionally to turn it into changes merchants feel, and by keeping content current and owning merchant communications. AI strategy and Zendesk optimization are key levers along the way.
Key Responsibilities
Program Ownership and Strategy:
Own omnichannel customer support programs from inception to execution, aligned to business goals and merchant needs.
Develop strategies with cross-functional teams, incorporating stakeholder feedback and industry best practices.
Drive implementation, overseeing timelines, resources, and budgets.
Ticket Reduction:
Analyze ticket data to find the top contact drivers, size them by volume, handle time, and cost, and build a prioritized reduction roadmap with clear targets.
Support processes: redesign workflows, macros, routing, and agent guidance so issues are resolved faster with fewer repeat contacts.
Ops processes: work with operations and site teams to fix the upstream breakdowns that create tickets, such as inbound, inventory, order, and billing issues.
Engineering: partner with engineering and product to prioritize and track the fixes and self-serve tools that remove root causes.
Merchant Experience and Feedback:
Own the feedback program, starting with NPS and adding other channels such as post-ticket surveys, agent and account manager input, ticket themes, and direct merchant conversations.
Analyze feedback themes and share insights with leadership and partners on a regular cadence.
Work cross-functionally with product, engineering, and operations to apply feedback to the merchant’s actual experience, track changes to completion, and close the loop with merchants.
Claims and Contra Revenue Management:
Own the claims process end to end, including intake, investigation, resolution, and recovery from carriers and vendors where applicable.
Manage and improve contra revenue (credits, refunds, reimbursements, and adjustments) by setting policies, approval thresholds, and controls, and partnering with finance on accurate tracking and reporting.
Analyze claim and contra revenue drivers, and work with operations and engineering to fix root causes and reduce both over time.
Content and Merchant Communications:
Keep all support content current and managed (help center, knowledge base, macros, internal guides, process documentation), with clear owners and review cadences.
Own merchant communications, including notices, announcements, policy and process change letters, banners, and templates.
AI Strategy and Implementation:
Build and own the roadmap for AI in support, focused on ticket reduction and merchant experience: agent assist, summarization, auto-categorization and routing, self-service and deflection, QA automation, and knowledge content.
Evaluate vendors and models, run pilots with clear success criteria, and take proven use cases into production.
Set guardrails for accuracy, human escalation, data privacy, and quality review, and lead training and change management for onsite and offshore teams.
Zendesk Management and Optimization:
Own Zendesk configuration and governance: forms and fields, triggers, automations, macros, views, SLAs, routing, groups, and roles. Audit regularly and manage a clear change process.
Manage integrations and reporting that turn Zendesk data into decisions, and turn agent pain points into workflow improvements.
Performance, Collaboration, and Stakeholders:
Establish and track KPIs: ticket volume, tickets per order or merchant, repeat contact rate, handle time, first-contact resolution, CSAT, NPS, claims, contra revenue, and cost per ticket.
Work closely with product, engineering, finance, and operations to integrate support initiatives into overall business operations.
Give stakeholders at all levels regular updates on status, challenges, and opportunities.
Continuously evaluate and refine programs based on feedback, industry trends, evolving merchant needs, and new AI capabilities.
Qualifications
Bachelor's degree in business administration, marketing, or related field.
5+ years of program management experience, preferably in customer support or a related role, with a proven record of delivering complex programs from concept to completion with measurable results.
Strong understanding of omnichannel customer support principles, strategies, and technologies.
Experience analyzing ticket, claims, or contact data to find root causes and reduce volume or cost, working with operations and engineering to fix them.
Experience running or using a merchant or customer feedback program such as NPS, and turning insights into cross-functional changes.
Strong writing skills, with experience owning customer communications and keeping support content current.
Hands-on Zendesk administration experience (triggers, automations, macros, views, SLAs, reporting).
Experience evaluating or implementing AI or automation in support, with a practical view of risks and limits.
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, able to collaborate cross-functionally and influence stakeholders at all levels.
Analytical mindset, able to use data to drive decisions and continuous improvement.
Strong project management skills: prioritizing, managing timelines, and allocating resources.
Experience in a fast-paced, dynamic environment, adapting to changing priorities. A resilient, focused problem solver and self-starter who can multitask and prioritize in a complex and occasionally ambiguous environment.
Physical requirements:
Must be able to lift up to 49 pounds with or without reasonable accommodation.
Must be willing and able to frequently push, pull, squat, bend, and reach.
Must be able to stand/walk for up to 10-12 hours.
Must be able to work in an environment where the noise level varies and can be loud.

Exciting Trade Advisory Opportunity to Help Make Global Trade Easy
The Opportunity:
The global supply chain is one of the most heavily regulated industries for all parties involved.  Everyone from the carriers, intermediaries, trucking companies, 3rd party logistics, freight forwarders, shippers, consignees, importers, exporters, and brokers face a challenging and complex task of navigating through a myriad of laws from the originating country, destination country as well as international treaties and conventions.
The Trade Advisory team, consisting of business consultants, lawyers and licensed customs brokers, offers advanced customs and trade expertise to help clients identify supply chain risks and cost savings opportunities. We are looking for a Trade Advisory Associate - Entry Audit to join our Trade Advisory team. This team member will work closely with the Trade Advisory Lead to execute client entry audit projects, managing the day-to-day work associated with each engagement from data intake through final reporting and recommendations.
Audit scope: Entry audits review a client's historical import entries to validate compliance and uncover risk and savings opportunities. Scope typically includes tariff classification, customs valuation, country of origin, duty rates and special program eligibility (including free trade agreements and additional tariff programs), antidumping and countervailing duty exposure, and the accuracy of entry data filed in ACE. Findings are quantified, documented, and translated into corrective actions such as prior disclosures, post summary corrections, and duty refund or recovery opportunities.
You Will:
Work closely with the Trade Advisory Lead to scope, plan, and execute client entry audit projects.
Manage the day-to-day activities of multiple audit projects, including data requests, timelines, status updates, and deliverables.
Pull, clean, and analyze large volumes of entry-level data from sources such as ACE, client database, entry packets (7501, commercial invoice, packing list, etc.)
Build and maintain Excel models and workbooks to map data from ACE to client specific business rules.
Design, build, and maintain automated workflows and data pipelines using N8N, Parabola, or equivalent tools to streamline audit analysis and reporting.
Identify discrepancies, quantify duty and fee impact, and document audit findings with supporting evidence.
Prepare clear audit reports and client-ready summaries of findings, root causes, and recommended corrective actions.
Support remediation efforts resulting from audit findings, such as post summary corrections, prior disclosures, and refund or recovery filings.
Maintain internal audit trackers, workpapers, and documentation to ensure projects are organized, consistent, and auditable.
Proactively stay informed on the latest customs and other government agency regulations, ruling issuances, and industry trends that are relevant to our clients.
Ensure project timelines, statuses, and invoices are appropriately managed and delivered.
Identify opportunities to improve audit SOPs, templates, and automation to increase accuracy and efficiency.
Maintain active communication with clients, customs and other government authorities, and internal stakeholders, elevating issues where necessary.
Support Trade Advisory infrastructure and administrative requirements.
You should have:
Bachelor's degree from an accredited college/university.
Licensed Customs Broker (LCB) preferred.
2-4 years experience working in house, at a customs brokerage, importer, trade industry, preferred.
Strong data analytical skills, with the ability to analyze large data sets and draw accurate conclusions.
Extensive experience with Excel, including advanced formulas, pivot tables, lookups, and large data set analysis.
Experience with workflow automation and data tools such as N8N, python, or equivalent.
Exceptional attention to detail and a high standard of accuracy.
Strong organizational skills and the ability to stay on top of multiple tasks and projects.
Strong technical and business writing skills.
Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to work collaboratively with a team and with clients.
Expertise with Microsoft Office suite and Google equivalents.
Working knowledge of classification, valuation, country of origin, duty programs, and government regulations and rulings, preferred.

title: Engineering Technician, Electrical
description:
Are you ready to build America’s energy future? Form Energy is an American manufacturing and energy technology company. We’re revolutionizing energy storage with cost-effective, multi-day technology designed to keep the electric grid secure and reliable, even during extended periods of stress. By strengthening the electric system and reimagining what’s possible, we’re giving clean energy a whole new form! 



In recent years, Form Energy has earned a number of accolades, including being named by TIME as a “Best Invention”, MIT Technology Review as a “Top Climate Tech Company To Watch”, and Fast Company as “One of the Next Big Things In Tech”. We are making rapid progress on our mission of delivering energy storage for a better world, and our team is growing just as rapidly to meet demand. We have signed contracts with leading electric utilities across the United States and production of our iron-air batteries is underway at our first high-volume manufacturing facility in West Virginia. 



Working for Form Energy is more than just a job, it’s a chance to be part of something extraordinary. And now - right as we significantly scale up battery manufacturing -  might be the most exciting moment in the company’s history to join. We are assembling a team of highly talented and driven individuals across the country. Driven by our core values of humanity, excellence, and creativity, our team is determined to deliver on our mission and transform the energy landscape for the better.



Feeling energized to make a meaningful impact on the world? Then keep reading - you’ve come to the right place.




ROLE DESCRIPTION

The Advanced Product Development team at Form Energy is hiring a Engineering Technician with an electrical focus for our team in Somerville, MA. This role is embedded directly in the APD engineering team and supports the electrical build-out, wiring, and commissioning of battery test systems that enable the development of Form Energy’s multi-day batteries.



A successful candidate can work independently with limited instruction and can give design feedback and suggestions to engineers. The ideal candidate has strong electrical intuition, understands prototyping, and can build, troubleshoot, and commission first-of-a-kind test hardware. This is an exciting opportunity to be part of the growth of a fast-moving company with breakthrough technology and an incredible mission!




WHAT YOU'LL DO:

 - Build and assemble control panels, harnesses, and test stand wiring as specified by engineers and schematics

 - Fabricate and maintain build or test related infrastructure and safety systems as specified by designs and schematics

 - Install and verify sensors, power distribution, and data acquisition hardware on battery test systems

 - Basic design tasks (e.g., lay out and fabricate a control panel) with only high-level instruction from engineers

 - Troubleshoot electrical faults on test equipment and support system commissioning

 - Participate in design reviews and give design feedback to engineers

 - Use shop tools (soldering, crimping, hand tools, 3D printers, etc.) to build prototypes and one-offs

 - Be a champion for safety in the development of new equipment and processes


WHAT YOU'LL BRING:

 - Minimum 4+ years experience as an electrical technician or hands-on role, ideally 2-3 years in a startup environment

 - Experience with industrial control wiring, power distribution, and panel building

 - Can read electrical schematics and wiring diagrams

 - Comfortable using sensors and data acquisition systems (e.g., multimeter, oscilloscope, thermocouple logger)

 - Familiarity with PLCs, HMIs, or other automation components is a plus

 - Working knowledge of electrical safety practices (e.g., NFPA 70E, lockout/tagout)

 - Strong written and verbal communication skills

 - Comfortable using G Suite

 - Very comfortable in a fast-paced startup environment

 - A positive, get-it-done attitude

title: Product Manager, Machine Tending
description:
Who we are:
Formic is on a mission to reshape American manufacturing by making automation accessible to every factory. As labor constraints rise, costs increase, and global competition intensifies, automation is no longer optional for manufacturers that want to stay competitive.
We deliver automation through a Robotics-as-a-Service model that combines industrial robotics, proprietary software, and full-service support into a single, integrated solution. By removing the traditional barriers of cost, complexity, and risk, we enable manufacturers to deploy automation quickly and realize measurable gains in throughput, safety, and operational efficiency without large upfront capital investment.
Backed by leading investors including Lux Capital, Initialized Capital, Blackhorn Ventures, and Mitsubishi HC Capital North America, Formic is scaling rapidly and building the foundation for a new era of high-performance, Made in America production.
About the team:
The Automation Engineering Team is responsible for delivering robotics-driven automation deployments across a wide range of customer applications. The team partners cross-functionally to translate customer requirements into deployed systems, ensuring solutions are integrated, commissioned, and validated to perform reliably in real manufacturing environments. Automation Engineering works closely with customers, internal technical teams, and external integrators to execute deployments on schedule while maintaining high standards for quality, safety, and repeatability.
About the role:
As Product Manager, Machine Tending, you will own the development, commercialization, and growth of Formic's machine tending offering across both tracks. You will decide which applications we pursue, define standard configurations and pricing, and lead the engineering work that makes them repeatable to deploy.
You will need enough engineering depth to make technical decisions and enough business sense to make commercial ones. You will set direction, get hands-on when needed, and serve as Formic's subject matter expert for the vertical. The goal is an offering Sales can confidently sell, Engineering can consistently deliver, and customers can rely on.
In this role you will:
Own the machine tending product:
Own the strategy, roadmap, and portfolio across third-party and internally developed solutions
Prioritize applications across CNC mills, lathes, machining centers, and press equipment, and define standard configurations and application boundaries
Set requirements for robots, CNC interfaces, workholding, EOAT, controls, software, and safety, favoring compact footprints, quick changeovers, and minimal programming
Develop a robust portfolio of offerings that span the common use cases of our customers. This will include systems to sport a full range of offerings in the High Mix / Low Volume and High Volume / Low Mix applications.
Develop third-party system integration and partnerships:
Evaluate and select third-party machine tending platforms and integration partners against Formic standards for safety, uptime, serviceability, and cost
Define integration standards for partner systems (Formic telemetry, remote monitoring, safety review, documentation, and spares) so each one is supported like any other fleet asset
Negotiate and manage relationships with integrators, machine tool builders, and OEMs, including pricing, lead times, support terms, and co-marketing
Aggregate lessons from partner deployments into the requirements for Formic's internal product
Develop Formic-designed machine tending systems:
Lead robot arm selection across collaborative and industrial platforms (FANUC, Yaskawa, Universal Robots, ABB, KUKA, Others), weighing payload, reach, cycle time, safety architecture, CNC integration support, cost, and serviceability
Scope a modular design framework that covers turning, milling, grinding, Swiss-type, and press applications from a common base of cell frame, controls, safety, and software
Define part presentation options (drawers, grids, carts, pallets) and EOAT libraries scaled to part size, weight, and batch volume
Validate designs on reference cells before release, and partner with Project Engineering on controlled models, BOMs, and documentation
Lead technical development and deployment:
Turn requirements into development plans, scope, and milestones across mechanical, electrical, controls, software, and applications engineering
Development of standardized options for Machine Tool interface.  Determination of the best practice for the most common machine tools and supplementary system for models that are unique
Own the deployment playbook from site survey through FAT, SAT, commissioning, and handoff to Field Operations, including safety risk assessments
Reduce install time and support needs using field feedback, and evaluate vision and AI where they add reliable value
Support sales and commercialization:
Serve as the technical subject matter expert for Sales, Solutions Engineering, and customers across active and queued clusters
Build a qualification framework that fits applications to standard offerings and flags custom work early, enabling accurate one-shot quoting
Support scoping, estimates, and quotations, ensuring NRE and application-specific costs are captured
Create specifications, application guidelines, and sales materials, and support launch events, IMTS, and named-customer case studies
Manage product economics and partnerships:
Own cost targets and improve margins through design, standardization, sourcing, and reconditioned equipment
Compare the full cost of third-party versus internal products, including development, deployment, and support
Build relationships with integrators, machine tool builders, and technology suppliers
What makes you a great fit:
Bachelor's degree in Engineering; MBA is a plus
7+ years in industrial automation and robotics spanning engineering and product or project management
Direct experience deploying or productizing robotic machine tending for CNC equipment
Hands-on CNC machining or machine shop experience
Experience leading cross-functional development and owning product pricing, quotations, or cost
Equipment commissioning, FAT/SAT, and on-site debugging experience
Familiarity with FANUC, Yaskawa Motoman, Universal Robots, ABB, or KUKA robots and common CNC controls
Knowledge of robot safety standards (ISO 10218, ANSI/RIA R15.06, ISO/TS 15066)
Exposure to machine vision
Commercially driven, comfortable with customers, and a strong communicator
Ability to travel up to 30%
#LB1
Our Total Rewards:
At Formic, we believe people do their best work when they feel supported both professionally and personally. That’s why we offer a comprehensive benefits and perks package for full-time, U.S.-based team members, including:
Equity in Formic: Participate in our stock option program and share in the success of a fast-growing start-up backed by leading global investors
Competitive & Uncapped Commission Structure: Designed to reward performance and impact in commission-eligible roles
Comprehensive Healthcare Coverage: Medical, dental, and vision insurance through Blue Cross Blue Shield and Unum, with 99% of employee premiums covered and 75% coverage for dependents, with optional buy-up plans available
Additional Insurance Benefits: FSA and DCFSA, life insurance, short-term disability, and long-term disability through Unum, all 100% employer-paid
Employee Assistance Program (EAP): Fully funded by Formic, offering support when you need it most
Paid Parental Leave Program: Up to 12 weeks of paid parental leave
Company-sponsored 401(k): Invest in your future with our company-facilitated retirement savings plan
Home Office Stipend: A one-time allowance for fully remote and hybrid employees to support an at-home or on-the-road work setup
Monthly Cell Phone Reimbursement: Monthly stipend toward personal phone and internet expenses
Flexible Time Off: Take the time you need, when you need it, supported by our flexible PTO policy
Compensation Philosophy
Formic’s pay and equity packages are thoughtfully benchmarked against peer companies at a similar growth stage. Equity represents a meaningful part of our mutual investment: when Formic succeeds, so do you.
Final offers are customized based on experience, geographic location, market considerations, and a candidate’s preferred balance of cash and equity. Our goal is to attract and reward top talent who will have significant impact, and we are open to thoughtful discussions to align on the right structure.
Compensation Range: $135,000 — $175,000 USD What we look for:
We’re building this company from the ground up, and every person we hire has an outsized impact on our culture, performance, and trajectory. While each team member brings unique strengths and perspectives, we look for people who align with our Operating Principles and embody them in action. If this sounds like you, Formic may be the right place for you!
Fearless Optimism: You make bold bets and default optimistic. You believe in the mission, aren’t paralyzed by risk, and fear inaction more than failure. You see ambiguity as opportunity and bring energy to building what doesn’t yet exist.
Create the Magic: You absorb complexity so customers don’t have to. Whether your customer is external or internal, you focus on delivering experiences that are clear, fast, value-added, and outcome-driven. You don’t say “not my job.” You make things work.
Today, Not Tomorrow: You have a bias to action. You close the loop. You take extreme ownership. You understand that speed compounds, and you don’t confuse activity with results.
Seek Truth: You think from first principles. You value data over ego and strong opinions loosely held. You’re willing to challenge assumptions, including your own, in pursuit of the best answer.
Made of Rubber: You are resolute and adaptable. When things break or priorities shift, you rebound stronger. You treat setbacks as learning moments and move forward with grit.
One Formic: You operate without silos. You practice radical helpfulness, document clearly, and make clean handoffs. You assume positive intent and prioritize team success over individual credit.

The team partners cross-functionally to translate customer requirements into deployed systems, ensuring solutions are integrated, commissioned, and validated to perform reliably in real manufacturing environments. Automation Engineering works closely with customers, internal technical teams, and external integrators to execute deployments on schedule while maintaining high standards for quality, safety, and repeatability.
About the role:
As Product Manager, Machine Tending, you will own the development, commercialization, and growth of Formic's machine tending offering across both tracks. You will decide which applications we pursue, define standard configurations and pricing, and lead the engineering work that makes them repeatable to deploy.
You will need enough engineering depth to make technical decisions and enough business sense to make commercial ones. You will set direction, get hands-on when needed, and serve as Formic's subject matter expert for the vertical. The goal is an offering Sales can confidently sell, Engineering can consistently deliver, and customers can rely on.
In this role you will:
Own the machine tending product:
Own the strategy, roadmap, and portfolio across third-party and internally developed solutions
Prioritize applications across CNC mills, lathes, machining centers, and press equipment, and define standard configurations and application boundaries
Set requirements for robots, CNC interfaces, workholding, EOAT, controls, software, and safety, favoring compact footprints, quick changeovers, and minimal programming
Develop a robust portfolio of offerings that span the common use cases of our customers. This will include systems to sport a full range of offerings in the High Mix / Low Volume and High Volume / Low Mix applications.
Develop third-party system integration and partnerships:
Evaluate and select third-party machine tending platforms and integration partners against Formic standards for safety, uptime, serviceability, and cost
Define integration standards for partner systems (Formic telemetry, remote monitoring, safety review, documentation, and spares) so each one is supported like any other fleet asset
Negotiate and manage relationships with integrators, machine tool builders, and OEMs, including pricing, lead times, support terms, and co-marketing
Aggregate lessons from partner deployments into the requirements for Formic's internal product
Develop Formic-designed machine tending systems:
Lead robot arm selection across collaborative and industrial platforms (FANUC, Yaskawa, Universal Robots, ABB, KUKA, Others), weighing payload, reach, cycle time, safety architecture, CNC integration support, cost, and serviceability
Scope a modular design framework that covers turning, milling, grinding, Swiss-type, and press applications from a common base of cell frame, controls, safety, and software
Define part presentation options (drawers, grids, carts, pallets) and EOAT libraries scaled to part size, weight, and batch volume
Validate designs on reference cells before release, and partner with Project Engineering on controlled models, BOMs, and documentation
Lead technical development and deployment:
Turn requirements into development plans, scope, and milestones across mechanical, electrical, controls, software, and applications engineering
Development of standardized options for Machine Tool interface.  Determination of the best practice for the most common machine tools and supplementary system for models that are unique
Own the deployment playbook from site survey through FAT, SAT, commissioning, and handoff to Field Operations, including safety risk assessments
Reduce install time and support needs using field feedback, and evaluate vision and AI where they add reliable value
Support sales and commercialization:
Serve as the technical subject matter expert for Sales, Solutions Engineering, and customers across active and queued clusters
Build a qualification framework that fits applications to standard offerings and flags custom work early, enabling accurate one-shot quoting
Support scoping, estimates, and quotations, ensuring NRE and application-specific costs are captured
Create specifications, application guidelines, and sales materials, and support launch events, IMTS, and named-customer case studies
Manage product economics and partnerships:
Own cost targets and improve margins through design, standardization, sourcing, and reconditioned equipment
Compare the full cost of third-party versus internal products, including development, deployment, and support
Build relationships with integrators, machine tool builders, and technology suppliers

Bachelor's degree in Engineering; MBA is a plus
7+ years in industrial automation and robotics spanning engineering and product or project management
Direct experience deploying or productizing robotic machine tending for CNC equipment
Hands-on CNC machining or machine shop experience
Experience leading cross-functional development and owning product pricing, quotations, or cost
Equipment commissioning, FAT/SAT, and on-site debugging experience
Familiarity with FANUC, Yaskawa Motoman, Universal Robots, ABB, or KUKA robots and common CNC controls

We partner with major Consumer Packaged Goods (CPG) companies to deliver innovative, environmentally responsible secondary packaging systems. Position Summary
The Senior Process Engineer serves as the technical leader for extrusion, material conversion, and labeling processes across Hi-Cone's global manufacturing network. This role is responsible for driving process capability, operational excellence, equipment reliability, material utilization, and technology advancement initiatives. Leveraging extensive hands-on manufacturing experience, the Senior Process Engineer develops and implements global manufacturing standards, leads process optimization efforts, supports capital investment projects, and provides technical leadership for strategic initiatives including PCR integration, sustainability objectives, and new product commercialization. The position acts as a subject matter expert for polymer processing, die-cutting/punch press operations, and labeling technologies while partnering with operations, maintenance, quality, and product development teams to improve safety, quality, delivery performance, and cost.
Key Responsibilities
Technology Leadership:
Serve as global Subject Matter Expert (SME) for extrusion, material conversion, and labeling operations.
Establish global process standards, operating windows, control plans, and best practices across all manufacturing facilities.
Lead troubleshooting and resolution of complex manufacturing issues impacting safety, quality, throughput, waste, and equipment reliability.
Establish, monitor, and improve process capability metrics and operational benchmarks to drive consistency and performance across global production assets.
Provide technical leadership, coaching, and training to plant engineering, operations, maintenance, and quality teams in process optimization, root cause analysis, and problem-solving methodologies.
Lead root cause investigations and corrective actions for chronic process issues related to extrusion performance, material conversion, labeling quality, and product consistency.
Asset & Performance Management:
Develop and maintain a comprehensive global equipment inventory and manufacturing capability matrix for extrusion, conversion, and labeling assets.
Establish maintenance standards, critical spare parts strategies, and equipment care plans for extrusion, punch press, and labeling operations.
Conduct global audits of extrusion, punch press, and labeling assets to identify reliability risks, capacity constraints, and equipment rebuild priorities.
Partner with operations and maintenance teams to identify and execute asset improvement opportunities that increase productivity, quality, and equipment uptime.
Support capital planning, equipment upgrades, and technology implementations through technical evaluation and performance analysis.
Develop and deploy a global preventive maintenance framework and asset care strategy in collaboration with maintenance, quality, and engineering teams.
Establish maintenance standards and critical spare parts strategies for extrusion, tooling, conversion, and labeling equipment.
Drive continuous improvement initiatives focused on safety, quality, throughput, material utilization, waste reduction, and operational efficiency utilizing ITW Toolbox principles.
Process Monitoring & Innovation Support:
Implement process monitoring and condition-tracking systems to identify deviations, improve process stability, and ensure consistent product quality.
Assess manufacturing capability and process readiness to support 55% PCR processing requirements under varying material and supply chain conditions.
Lead process trials and evaluate the manufacturing impacts of alternate materials, new product developments, and CBI initiatives.
Support qualification, validation, and commercialization of new products, materials, and manufacturing technologies.
Evaluate emerging technologies, automation opportunities, and process improvements that enhance safety, productivity, quality, and sustainability across the global manufacturing network.
Education and Experience
Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Plastics Engineering, Industrial Engineering, or related technical field required.

Analytics products and dashboards

The purpose of this role is to serve as a Scientific Research Program Manager (SRPM) supporting evidence strategy and research programs across Intuitive Surgical’s da Vinci platforms, products, and services. The SRPM will collaborate with cross-functional stakeholders to identify evidence needs and priorities and support the development and execution of evidence-generation strategies and research plans. This role oversees the initiation, progress, and conduct of evidence-generation studies, including those conducted by internal scientific teams, Intuitive-sponsored studies, and studies conducted in collaboration with external research partners. The SRPM serves as a key contact for internal and external parties involved in assigned programs and projects.
Essential Job Duties
Collaborate with da Vinci and Multiport program leaders and cross-functional evidence stakeholders to identify evidence requirements and gaps, align on evidence priorities, and develop evidence strategies and plans.
Manage and execute a portfolio of internal and external collaborative research studies and evidence-generation activities for Intuitive Surgical's da Vinci platforms, products, and services, with support from research coordinators as applicable.
Manage research studies across the study lifecycle, including project development, budgeting, investigator selection, analysis of potential participant recruitment, preparation of study-related documents (e.g., protocols, case report forms, informed consents, research agreements), and management of Institutional Review Board and/or Ethics Committee submissions through successful outcome.
Collaborate with data management professionals and statisticians as needed; maintain required study documentation; and plan and manage project timelines and budgets to support timely execution.
Proactively identify and communicate project concerns, issues, and delays; develop risk assessments and contingency plans; and prepare project status updates, presentations, and reports for internal and external stakeholders and steering or advisory committees.
Manage publication development, submission, and responses to peer review related to research studies.
Ensure compliance with corporate requirements (e.g., SOPs) and applicable regulatory requirements (e.g., GCP and U.S. and international guidelines), and maintain audit readiness to relevant regulatory and legal standards.
Manage Contract Research Organizations (CROs) and independent research service providers, including partner identification, contract or statement-of-work development, and stakeholder management; facilitate meetings and reporting in accordance with Intuitive Surgical policies; and support review and development of internal research processes (e.g., SOPs).
Build, nurture, and maintain relationships with external research partners and stakeholders, including surgeon key opinion leaders, operating room staff, hospital and health system administrative and technology leaders, surgical and scientific professional society leaders, and healthcare technology industry partners.
Skills, Experience, Education, & Training:
Bachelor's degree or equivalent in life sciences, medicine, medical sciences, engineering, computer science, data science, or a related field
Minimum five years of experience in an academic setting or healthcare technology industry in a clinical affairs or scientific research function, with evidece of full project management responsibility; industry research management experience preferred.
Knowledge of applicable clinical research and medical device regulations and guidelines, including GCP, ISO 14155, MEDDEV, MDR, and data protection requirements.
Experience developing research protocols and case report forms (CRFs).
Strong organizational skills and ability to manage multiple projects with competing priorities, including a minimum of three to five research projects across different surgical disciplines and/or products.
Strong communication, interpersonal, and negotiation skills, with the ability to manage work autonomously and collaborate across teams while maintaining open communication with key stakeholders.
Strong quantitative and literature analysis skills, with the ability to assess data and scientific literature and review data sets for data quality.
Ability to manage CROs, external consultants, research coordinators, or other research staff in the execution of research studies.
Strong problem-solving skills and initiative; English-language proficiency required.
English language required, a second language is an advantage
Work may require presence in hospital and surgical/operating room environments. Ability to travel 25%-50% of the time.
Preferred Skills and Experience
Graduate degree in life sciences, medicine, medical sciences, engineering, computer science, data science, or a related field.
Five years of experience in the management of research, including clinical research management experience in both academic/hospital and industry settings.
Experience with studies of health information technologies, including artificial intelligence.
Experience publishing research in an academic or industry capacity.
Proficiency in a second language.

Working closely with the Finance Product Owner, this role will serve as an onsite analytical partner to Finance stakeholders and a key link between business, application, data engineering, and reporting teams.
The ideal candidate combines Finance and ERP process knowledge with strong SQL, data analysis, and business intelligence capabilities. Operating at the intersection of business logic and data engineering, you will understand complex business processes, trace data lineage across systems, investigate discrepancies, and translate business needs into clear reporting models and technical requirements. You will design and deliver trusted dashboards, BI data models, operational monitoring, and self-service analytics while evaluating practical automation and AI-assisted analytics opportunities (deep AI/ML engineering experience is not required).

Technical Translation & Requirements Gathering: Partner with the Finance Product Owner and Finance stakeholders to understand business processes, controls, and reporting needs. Translate business needs into functional and data requirements, business rules, report specifications, user stories, and acceptance criteria.
BI Design & Solution Delivery: Design, build, and maintain Finance dashboards, published data sources, BI data models, operational reports, and self-service analytics solutions using Tableau, Power BI, or comparable platforms.
Lineage, Reconciliation & Root-Cause Analysis: Analyze end-to-end processes and data flows across ERP (SAP), CRM, billing, data warehouse, and reporting platforms. Use advanced SQL and analytical tools to reconcile data, validate business rules, investigate discrepancies, and identify root causes.
Performance Tuning & Reporting Reliability: Optimize dashboard usability, query performance, data refresh schedules, metric consistency, and overall reporting reliability.
Delivery Leadership & Governance : Lead assigned workstreams through requirements, solution design, UAT, regression testing, reconciliation, implementation readiness, and stakeholder sign-off. Internal Controls & Quality Monitoring: Support automated monitoring, exception management, data-quality controls, and financially significant/SOX-governed reporting processes.
Cross-Functional & Global Collaboration: Collaborate with application, Data Engineering, Data Science, AI, and platform teams while coordinating and reviewing deliverables across distributed onsite and offshore resources.
Applied AI & Automation Evaluation: Evaluate and support opportunities to implement intelligent alerts, natural-language analytics, AI-assisted analysis, and workflow automation within core Finance processes.

7+ years of progressive experience in business intelligence, Finance analytics, reporting, business systems analysis, or enterprise data solutions.
ERP & Finance Domain: Experience with SAP or another enterprise ERP platform, including strong understanding of Finance-related processes and cross-system data flows.
Advanced SQL Mastery: Expert-level SQL skills for complex querying, source-to-target reconciliation, data troubleshooting, root-cause analysis, and query performance optimization.

Experience developing robotic or complex electromechanical products in a regulated industry, with demonstrated independent subsystem ownership from concept through design transfer.
Working knowledge of design controls, risk management, verification and validation.
Deep expertise in first-principles mechanics and precision mechanisms, with demonstrated ability to perform stiffness, dynamics and fatigue analysis.
Proficiency in GD&T, tolerancing, materials, DFM/DFA and manufacturing processes.
Experience designing rotary or linear joints, sizing components, and justifying decisions through analysis; integrating actuation and sensing; and collaborating effectively with controls and electrical engineers.
Hands-on prototyping experience, including assembly, testing, debugging, and rapid iterations.
Proficient with CAD, simulation, and PLM tools such as SolidWorks, ANSYS, and Windchill.
Demonstrated technical leadership through design reviews, cross-functional decision-making, stakeholder influence and engineer mentorship.
Experience with risk management activities including FMEA, risk mitigation, and reliability assessments.
Required Education and Training
Required: Typical minimum Bachelor’s degree plus 12 years of relevant experience, or a Master’s degree plus 8 years, or a PhD plus 5 years.
Preferred: Master’s or PhD degree in Mechanical Engineering or a related discipline.

On-site four days per week in Sunnyvale, CA.
May involve extended periods of computer-based design and analysis work.
Must be comfortable occasionally working in lab environments, including prototype assembly, mechanical testing, and safe use of standard mechanical tools and fixtures.
Must be able to occasionally lift and handle 25 pounds.

Experience developing Class II or Class III medical devices, particularly surgical robotics or medical device capital equipment.
Direct application of standards and documentation frameworks such as ISO 13485, FDA QMSR (21 CFR Part 820), IEC 60601, ISO 14971, and DHF.

The DaVinci Specialist is a dedicated program execution & clinical education partner for hospitals running a da Vinci robotic surgery program.   Based on its expertise, this role focuses on identifies and tailors the nature and extent of staff in-servicing, day-to-day program execution, technology onboarding and operational support, communicating identified needs to hospital OR operations and leadership. Collaboration & Field Partnership (Within a CSM Team)
Partner with the local CSR/CSM and cross-functional business partners to create, own, scale and execute best practices and deployment of ecosystem resources.
Lead account support plans that drive safe program execution and increase customer autonomy over time, including setting objectives, timelines and resources for relevant customers, in consultation with CSR/CSM.
Identify, solicit and provide field feedback and customer insights to internal teams to improve training, support resources, and customer experience.
Support adoption of digital solutions by helping customers build comfort and capability through in-servicing and troubleshooting.
Clinical & Technical Support
Identify and provide on-site, non-scrubbed operating room support for procedures utilizing the da Vinci Surgical System and associated technologies.
Support OR teams with room readiness and procedural workflow, including system setup support, docking workflow support, and intraoperative troubleshooting.
Serve as a clinical product expert to help ensure optimal, safe system use and adherence to applicable IFUs, hospital policies, and safety protocols.
Motivate and support adoption of advanced instruments and accessories by ensuring teams understand proper setup, handling, and intended use.
Partner with and promote consistent readiness and workflow by supporting day-to-day execution of the robotic program, coordinating with OR leadership, nursing, SPD/sterile processing, and biomedical teams.
Assist with operational support activities such as facilitating appropriate internal handoffs for service needs.
Ensure the right stakeholders are aligned (OR, SPD, biomed, IT) for successful day-to-day operation and new technology onboarding to help reduce friction.
Maintain accurate internal documentation of support activities per company process (e.g., case support notes, training records, service/escalation tracking).
Training & Education (Care Team Enablement)
Determine the need for, customize and deliver customer-specific hands-on training and in-services to nurses, surgical technologists, SPD teams, and other care team members on safe and effective use of da Vinci platforms and associated technologies.
Support onboarding and education for new users through structured training touchpoints (e.g., new staff orientation, refresher training, workflow standardization).
Lead new site start-ups by identifying and delivering onboarding programs and coordinating training logistics with the CSR/CSM and hospital stakeholders.
Support new technology installs by coordinating readiness activities and providing post-install education to care teams.
Act as a resource for ongoing education, product updates, and workflow optimization.

Analyze and leverage utilization, turnover, and other relevant case data to recommend operational changes to customers
Provide first-line support and expertise for common setup and workflow issues during live cases and training sessions.
Identify, resolve and where necessary escalate issues appropriately to internal partners (e.g., Technical Support, Field Service, Clinical/Medical counterparts).
Market & Clinical Insights
Collect and communicate customer feedback  and experiences  to clinical counterparts and internal business partners.  Prioritizing, distilling and reporting relevant customer feedback, in real time.
Stay up to date on clinical literature, competitive products, and evolving treatment guidelines.
Assist in clinical trial support when required.
Assist in field action activities when necessary.

Experience: 2+ years in an operating room-related role
Clinical experience is preferred.
Experience as a robotics coordinator, surgical assistant, and/or surgical nurse plus industry experience strongly preferred.
Understanding of soft tissue anatomy & procedures.
Exhibit a working knowledge of typical hospital policies.
Excellent communication, teaching, and interpersonal skills.
Strong problem solving and troubleshooting skills.
Ability to work in high-pressure environments (managing multiple ORs) and coordination of multiple tasks at one time.
Adaptability to evolving technologies and complex procedures.
Team oriented with a commercial mindset.
Willingness to travel up to 40%. Primary travel will be within a CSM team.
Ability to travel within a Clinical Sales Manager team geography, supporting multiple hospitals.
Flexibility to support early starts, after-hours cases, and weekend procedures based on customer need and territory utilization.
Required Education and Training
Associates degree. Bachelor’s degree preferred.
Degrees in (RN, PA, NP, RT, or other clinical credentials) are welcomed.

Ability to stand for extended periods and provide in-person case support within an operating room (OR) environment, which includes pushing, pulling, lifting and squatting.

title: Quality Manager
location: Coshocton Plant, Ohio, United States of America
description:
Job Purpose The plant Quality Manager develops and maintains a strong culture of quality and food safety plant-wide. They develop and execute quality and food safety strategic initiative for the entire manufacturing site to drive continuous improvement while delivering against all Kraft Heinz internal quality measures (KPIs), external regulatory standards, and 3rd party customer requirements.   This position plays a key role in contributing to our vision of growing sustainably and delighting more consumers by ensuring the quality and protection of our brands. This position also plays an important role aligned with our values "we are consumer obsessed, we own it, and dare to do better every day".   Essential Functions & Responsibilities: Leads a core team of Quality and Sanitation professionals capable of delivering on quality and production strategies, including but not limited to: Laboratory, Quality Compliance, Sanitation, Department Quality Supervisors, Sanitation Supervisors, and other supporting staff.
Works with the corporate quality team and various support function to deliver on quality excellence programs to driving performance in consumer complaint reduction, hold reduction, sanitation execution, and regulatory compliance.
Utilization of industry and Kraft Heinz quality tools (RCFA, SPC, Green Belt, etc.) to improve quality and product superiority.
Leads and implements best-in-class quality and food safety KPIs to measure performance of team members, ultimately aligning with the larger factory and business priorities.
Drives team member engagement through strong leadership, career development, and conflict management.
Builds strong relationships with plant leadership team members to ensure quality programs are driven through cross-functional partnerships with shared goals.
Partners with corporate to drive automation and digital solutions.
Capable of evaluating performance and competencies of plant QA staff while providing leadership training, coaching, and accountability as needed.
Drives consistency through development of work instructions and training to set standards.
Manages the plant's Corrective Action and Preventive Action program to drive continuous improvement.
Drives excellence in innovation thru supporting R&D plant trials and feedback, ensuring successful end-to-end commercialization of brand maintenance and innovation projects.
Maintains plant GMPs, HACCP, pre-requisite programs while serving as the primary liaison between plant and external regulatory agencies (USDA) during routine and unannounced visits.
Provides direction and subject matter expertise on plant Quality-related activities and inquiries
Prepares for and leads all internal and external quality audits, ensuring all corrective and preventative action timelines are adhered to.
Routinely monitors KHC quality systems, tools, and data sources to proactively address potential risks before they occur.
Oversees record keeping for all mandated quality checks, testing, sampling and sanitation activities.
Tracks, analyzes, and supports RCFA initiatives for consumer complaints.
Prepares and maintains relevant FSQ permitting and licensing for the plant.
Manages departmental budgeting, purchasing and inventory of plant quality supplies such as filters, chemicals, tools and lab supplies.
Serves as the plant lead for company quality and manufacturing initiatives including the implementation of the Kraft Heinz Management System (KHMS).
Develops strong working relationships with key suppliers and vendors.
Communicates effectively across all levels of the factory and corporate leadership team.
Expected Experience & Required Skills: Bachelor's degree in food science, chemistry, microbiology or related field preferred
Must be a self-directed individual with a high level of integrity and maturity with proven leadership skills related to coaching/development of team members.
Ability to work well under pressure through times of crisis management.
Must be an effective communicator with excellent follow-up skills and comfortable interacting with all levels of the organization.
Strong knowledge of GFSI (FSSC 22000) requirements and previous experience as an audit facilitator.
Demonstrates understanding of Statistical Process Control (SPC), HACCP, sanitation, analytical/microbiology testing principles, and hygienic design principals.
Has project management skills and a working knowledge of Microsoft Word, Excel, Access and PowerPoint.
ERP system and Quality system experience, SAP and Infinity preferred.
Demonstrates the ability to drive continuous improvement, is results-driven and delivers against set targets.
Capable of fostering a strong Quality Culture that supports transformational change in line with the Kraft Heinz Company strategy.

title: Quality Supervisor
location: Fremont Factory, Ohio, United States of America
description:
Job Purpose The position of the off shift Quality Supervisor is instrumental to the daily success of the facility. This leader responsibility is to lead the quality food safety initiatives on off shift while supporting Sanitation supervision on 3rd shift. This candidate can achieve this task by evaluating daily production, updating programs and documents to improve and simplify our process, and verify all Food Safety Quality and Food Defense Programs are compliant on an ongoing daily basis throughout the year so no gaps exist. Some areas of focus consist of Kraft Heinz policies, KHMS, HACCP, FDA regulations, FSSC, religious laws, and state laws. This candidate must have a mentality every day to learn the production floor processes across the facility and all the required regulatory equipment in the facility. They will be supporting the verification for the functionality of the equipment and compliance to all hourly trained programs and initiatives. This candidate must be able to coach/teach/communicate at all levels from the hourly employees to the facility manager on site.
Essential Functions & Responsibilities: Be the off shift quality supervisor leader for the department that maintains all programs to a very high Food Safety level for compliance.
Actively engaged support in planning, defining, and directing the site auditing control program to ensure compliance to all procedures, and policies, GMP standards, Kraft Heinz requirements, and regulatory, federal and local laws.
Perform assignment in accordance with 5S, Sig Sigma and lean Manufacturing initiative.
Support the KHMS system and operational standards as outlined in the plant accountability list.
Trains, mentors, and leads off shift site Quality, Maintenance, Materials, and Production team members to ensure quality program goals are met. Strong support to site KHMS/ISO Coordinator. Monitors and maintains plant KHMS program by complying to current Kraft Heinz and International Audit (FSSC/ISO) standards. Facilitate and co-lead site cross functional quality team and participate with Kraft Heinz corporate to insure successful certifications for site.
Ensure all Specification/KPI/ KHMS/FSSC/ISO/Golden Rules plans are maintained and executed
Support all internal and external inspections/regulatory visits. Support and lead off shift audit preparation activities, accompany inspector, and complete necessary reports for communication and process owner postings.
Lead follow-ups to non-conformances found and provide responses as appropriate for all off shift risks. Review and approve minor change requests.
Monitors all weekly sanitation records for compliance and follows-up to ensure adherence to programs and established limits to ensure food safety.
Complete Sanitation Positive Release Standard.
Leads plant sanitation improvement projects, automation, and expansion projects.
Directs and reports on overall plant sanitation programs including PSS, RSS, PIC/PEC, expansion, and extended runs.
Directs sanitation environmental control programs like clean equipment swabs, environmental monitoring, and pathogen testing.
Coordinates and conducts full sanitation audits including equipment tear downs to ensure effectiveness of equipment cleaning procedures.
Performs assignments in accordance with established Good Manufacturing Practices (GMPs), policies and procedures
Support the compliance for Hold/Release documentation and dispositioning of products.
Complete and lead validation studies for all CCPs, OPRPs and other significant controls in accordance with approved methodologies.
Maintain Quality Suite to track and trend quality checks data and create new project as needed.
Perform Net content calculation analysis for New SKU to meet the NIST requirement or for retargeting for current SKUs.
Ensures compliance to Golden Rules and other Quality principles through routine auditing, reporting and trending compliance appropriately.
Provides expertise on off shift and supporting shifts while actively participating in equipment commissioning and startup, ensuring standardization of all applicable quality and food safety procedures are followed and gaps are called out for future corrective actions.
Adhere to approved Control of change procedures, to include reviewing partial HACCP plans and issuing Agile change requests, as needed. You will be point of contact for all meetings impacting third shift.
Expected Experience & Required Skills: Prefer minimum of 5+ years of experience working in a quality, production, or sanitation departments within the food industry, with at least 3 years in a leadership position in a food manufacturing facility.
Prefer strong understanding of HACCP principles, food safety regulations, quality system management system, sanitation run rules, production processes, and the KHMS framework if applicable.
Prefer strong leadership, technical, communication, delegation, and organizational skills along with keen attention to detail.
Prefer being proficient in Microsoft Office, SAP, Agile, and matrix databases.

Foster a continuous improvement culture and leverage technology tools, such as Alteryx, Excel, and Power BI, to automate and refine tax workflows
Utilize automation tools to enhance existing and future processes and document those processes and procedures

title: Area Maintenance Technician Days
description:

Job Description
The Area Maintenance Technician is responsible for maintaining, troubleshooting, repairing, and improving manufacturing equipment and processes within their assigned area. This role serves as both a skilled maintenance resource and a system owner, driving equipment reliability, preventive maintenance optimization, continuous improvement, and technical knowledge development. Ability to train, mentor, and support other associates. Strong problem-solving, planning, and organizational abilities. Commitment to continuous improvement and operational excellence. Recommend and implement improvements to equipment reliability and maintainability. Influence and implement preventive maintenance strategies and maintenance priorities. Recommend critical spare parts and inventory levels. Support decisions regarding equipment modifications, upgrades, and reliability improvements within established processes. Provide technical recommendations for maintenance and capital improvement projects. Ability to identify recurring failures and implement sustainable countermeasures. Demonstrates advanced proficiency and autonomy within established procedures and practices. Frequently consulted by peers. May act as lead coordinating the work of others.
Functional Knowledge:
Applies proficiency in a range of business or technical support processes and procedures.
Business Expertise: Has a good understanding of how the team integrates with others to achieve objectives.
Leadership: Typically has no supervisory or Line Manager responsibilities. May act as informal resource for others. Can be a team leader; allocates work coordinating activities, checking on quality and work progress.
Problem Solving: Solves non-routine problems based on experience and established practices. Identifies new solutions and recommends changes to existing procedures as needed.
Impact: Impacts the quality and timelines of own work and the work of others. May influence team outcomes.
Interpersonal Skills: Communicates functional information within the team and outside the team. May help resolve conflicts.
Demonstrated ability to work independently with minimal supervision.
Key Responsibilities
Equipment maintenance and troubleshooting

description:

Microsoft Customer and Partner Solutions-Core (MCAPS) accelerates customer outcomes and business growth. Services Sales is changing how it sells. New AI agents, tooling, processes, policies and go-to-market priorities are reaching sellers, managers, sales excellence and deal operations teams at a steady pace, and each one changes how deals are priced, built, recorded and closed. The value of those investments is only realized when the field actually works differently.
We are looking for an Adoption Lead to serve as the single accountable owner for adoption across the Services Sales Organization. Working from changes assessed and approved through the organizations change management process, you will translate organizational priorities and transformation initiatives into adoption strategies, turn a high volume of change into a small number of planned, field-ready landings, and be accountable for whether people adopt and sustain the new ways of working. You will orchestrate with the teams that build, approve and broadcast changes rather than duplicate them: product and engineering teams build, intake and governance teams approve, and established landing channels broadcast. You own the adoption journey that connects them.
This role sits at the center of the business. Success is measured not by what is launched, but by adoption, sustained behavior change and measurable business outcomes. The ideal candidate combines strong program management discipline with proven adoption and change practice, understands how change affects frontline roles, is comfortable with AI and sales technology, and has the credibility to lead across organizational boundaries without direct authority.
Candidates who live within 50 miles of Microsoft's Redmond campus will be required to work in the office 3 days per week.
Microsoft's mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.

Drive organizational change by securing leadership sponsorship, defining adoption plans, and coordinating communications, onboarding, and reskilling.
Evaluate program impact through success measures, cost-benefit analysis, and business reviews, using insights to manage risks and improve or retire programs.
Coach cross-functional teams to simplify processes, resolve root causes, and communicate program value in ways that build stakeholder buy-in.

Influence sponsorship and build trusted partnerships with Director, GM and CVP leaders to hold the field accountable for adopting new ways of working.
Equip leaders and managers to sponsor, model and reinforce adoption within their organizations.
Partner with change intake and go/no-go owners to sequence approved changes into a predictable landing cadence that limits field fatigue and maximizes adoption.
Align stakeholders across organizational boundaries on adoption accountabilities (RACI), resolving dependencies that block adoption.

Build on impact assessments from change intake to define what each audience needs to know, understand and do differently, and the behaviors that signal adoption.
Identify readiness gaps, adoption barriers and potential resistance, and plan how to address them before launch.
Lead the identification of skilling and reskilling needs that adoption depends on, in partnership with enablement and HR.
Set adoption-readiness criteria and feed them into go/no-go decisions, so changes reach the field with audiences, materials and support routes ready and security, privacy, compliance and responsible AI requirements met.

Translate complex changes into role-specific, scenario-based guidance anchored in one authoritative destination for the field.
Own adoption after launch, tracking usage by role and region and running targeted follow-up with lagging teams until new ways of working are sustained.
Lead the definition and tracking of adoption metrics across awareness, readiness, usage, behavioral change and business impact.

Provide insight into value realization and recommend when to accelerate, adjust or retire a change.

OR equivalent experience.

Experience leading adoption of AI, automation or sales technology (for example Copilot, CRM, deal or pricing tools) in enterprise sales, customer success or other field-facing organizations.
Working knowledge of professional services sales motions, deal processes and sales systems.
Adoption analytics skills, including defining usage and behavior metrics and using dashboards (for example Power BI) to drive decisions.
Demonstrated ability to influence senior leaders in a matrixed organization and translate complex change into clear, actionable guidance for diverse audiences.

title: Director of Datacenter IT Operations
description:
Overview
Microsoft's Cloud Operations & Innovation (CO+I) is the engine that powers our cloud services. It delivers the core infrastructure and foundational technologies for Microsoft's online services, including Bing, Microsoft 365, Xbox, OneDrive and the Microsoft Azure platform. Our infrastructure is a global portfolio of more than 200 datacenters in 32 countries and millions of servers. It supports more than 1 billion customers and 20 million businesses in over 90 countries.
Reporting to the Charlotte Metro Director, the Director of Datacenter IT Operations is the senior IT Operations leader for the Charlotte Metro. This leader owns end-to-end IT operations, IT outfitting and IT infrastructure delivery across all Class A and Class B datacenter facilities in the metro. That organization is accountable for safe, secure, on-time and defect-free delivery of customer capacity, and for reliable, SLA-compliant operation of IT infrastructure once it is live.
The role covers the full IT lifecycle. That starts with design input and construction coordination, continues through IT outfitting, network and server deployment, operational readiness and turnover, and extends into steady-state operations, hardware lifecycle management and decommissioning. The Director partners closely with Critical Environment (CE), IAM/Logistics, Datacenter Delivery (DCD), Datacenter Engineering (DCE), Commissioning, network and hardware engineering teams, and vendors. Together they ensure IT requirements are built in from the start and that Operations is ready to take ownership on Day 1.
Success in this role requires strong organizational leadership, disciplined service management, financial acumen, and the ability to turn technical and operational risk into clear, decision-ready recommendations for metro, regional and CO+I leadership. With environmental sustainability and optimization at the forefront of our datacenter design and operations, we continue to grow and evolve to meet the business demands that make Microsoft a world-class cloud provider.
Do you want to empower billions across the world? Come and join us in CO+I and be at the forefront of the action!
Responsibilities
Organizational Leadership and People Management
Build, lead, coach and develop the Charlotte Metro IT Operations organization, including Datacenter Technician Managers, Datacenter Program Managers and Datacenter Technicians across all Class A and Class B facilities.
Deliver success through empowerment and accountability by modeling, coaching and caring. Live our culture, embody our values and practice our leadership principles.
Set the IT organization's strategy, priorities, operating rhythm, performance expectations and long-term capability roadmap in line with metro and CO+I priorities.
Lead IT workforce, capacity and succession planning across the metro. Allocate resources across campuses and sites based on business priority, infrastructure complexity, operational risk and future demand.
Attract, hire and retain great people. Know everyone's capabilities and aspirations, invest in the growth of others, and develop the next generation of leaders through intentional delegation and succession planning.
Make sure teams complete required training and certifications. Partner with Learning & Development to evolve the training portfolio as technology and site requirements change.
Recognize team successes and reward teamwork while keeping the culture focused on strategic goals.
2. IT Operations and Service Delivery
Own end-to-end service compliance, quality and client satisfaction for all IT services in the metro, against agreed SLAs, OLAs, KPIs and OKRs.
Oversee all IT operations activity, including server and rack deployment, network turn-up, structured cabling, break-fix and hardware repair, asset tracking, decommissions, and secure media handling and destruction.
Apply deep subject-matter expertise and escalate as needed to meet SLA/OLA commitments with minimal disruption to customers and the business. Review metrics with leaders so everyone understands targets and current performance.
Manage relationships with internal clients and service-line partners so expectations are clear and understood, and deliver solutions with a strong customer focus.
Understand future business demand in each facility so that IT staffing, tooling, spares and resources keep pace with growth.
Share common and recurring issues with regional and global teams, and promote best practices that prevent recurrence and make resolution more efficient.
3. IT Outfitting, Capacity Delivery and Operational Readiness
Own IT outfitting and infrastructure delivery for new builds, expansions, retrofits and live-site changes across all Class A and Class B facilities in the metro.
Make sure IT requirements are built into infrastructure designs and formal design reviews, including network, structured cabling, rack/enclosure layouts, power distribution to IT, maintainability, security and supportability.
Keep IT Operations engaged throughout construction and commissioning, including quality reviews, readiness assessments, commissioning participation and resolution of IT concerns before turnover.
Make sure documentation, procedures, spares, tooling, systems access, training and operational dependencies are in place before operational acceptance, so IT teams can safely and effectively take ownership on Day 1.
Support Go/No-Go and readiness decisions with clear, data-driven assessments of IT infrastructure and operational risk.
Ensure on-time, defect-free delivery of customer capacity within SLA commitments. Govern post-turnover stabilization, early-life performance and defect resolution.
Plan with business partners when carrying out their requirements so that datacenter availability, safety and security are maintained.
4. Incident Management, Reliability and Risk
Serve as the senior IT escalation point for the metro. Take part in, and lead where appropriate, every Sev 1 and Sev 2 incident bridge affecting Microsoft cloud services in Charlotte, including communication with customers and senior leadership.
Approve root-cause analyses and postmortem reports, and drive improvement plans and corrective and preventive actions to completion.
Prevent IT infrastructure and operational risk before it affects safety, security, availability, capacity delivery, cost or schedule, or creates long-term technical debt.
Use incident trends, hardware failure data, commissioning findings and field experience to find systemic risks. Partner with engineering, OEMs and vendors to resolve them.
Make sure IT work in live environments goes through rigorous change management, including risk assessment, Method of Procedure (MOP) and Emergency Operating Procedure (EOP) review, and maintenance-window planning, to protect customer availability.
Own the metro IT risk register and make sure risks, dependencies and ownership gaps are tracked, escalated and closed.
5. Financial and Vendor Management
Own the metro IT Operations budget, including detailed budgets, forecasts, and management of operating and capital spend. Make tradeoff decisions that follow sound fiscal practices.
Lead budget planning and demand-cost forecasting. Make sure business leaders understand how service-management issues affect cost, risk and staffing, and negotiate for the resources the organization needs.
Manage and oversee IT vendor and partner contracts and relationships, including IT service providers, contracted labor, OEMs and partner support teams. For leased facilities, coordinate with landlords and their operators on IT-related requirements.
Hold vendors accountable for performance, quality and commercial results, and recommend extra funding or resources for pilots, task forces or growth where needed.
6. Governance, Metrics and Executive Communication
Establish consistent IT Operations governance across the metro, with clear decision rights, escalation paths, response expectations and accountability.
Set and monitor meaningful KPIs. Examples include SLA attainment, on-time capacity delivery, readiness milestone completion, incident and repair turnaround, issue aging, turnover defect trends, asset accuracy, safety performance and cost efficiency.
Give the Metro Director and regional leadership concise reports on IT portfolio health, readiness, schedule, financial performance, risk and key decisions.
Translate complex technical and operational issues into clear, decision-ready information for senior leadership.
Represent IT Operations in metro, regional and CO+I leadership forums, design reviews and readiness governance.
7. Cross-Functional Partnership and One Microsoft
Serve as the single point of IT Operations integration for the metro across CE, IAM/Logistics, DCD, DCE, Commissioning, Physical Security, Environment Health & Safety, network and hardware engineering, and global and regional teams.
Partner with the Metro Director and peer functional leaders to align metro priorities, coordinate cross-campus planning, manage dependencies and resolve ownership gaps.
Find opportunities to collaborate across groups, make sure cross-team commitments are set, and achieve scale by enabling the work of others.
Support global and regional initiatives such as environmental health and safety programs, risk assessments, audits, compliance and certifications.
Act as a trusted advisor to a wide network of colleagues and bring diverse viewpoints together to solve organization-wide problems.
8. Safety, Security, Culture and Ownership
Build a culture of safety, security, quality, compliance and customer obsession in every part of IT operations.
Follow the runbooks provided by the Environment, Health & Safety division, and report any safety or security issue or concern immediately.
Take pride and personal accountability for end-to-end service quality, completeness and the resulting customer experience. Find unaddressed issues and resolve them, escalate them, or find the right owner.
Remove barriers to agility so teams can shift priorities quickly without losing productivity.
Learn, live and coach the One Microsoft culture and values. Lead through change by bringing clarity, generating energy and delivering success.
Qualifications
Required Qualifications
High School Qualification or equivalent AND 10+ years experience of mission-critical service management (e.g., providing IT services, manufacturing, warehouse, retail, military, or managing physical operations in an IT and/or critical environment infrastructure) OR equivalent experience
3+ years people management experience.
Other Requirements:

Microsoft Cloud Background Check: This position will be required to pass the Microsoft Cloud background check upon hire/transfer and every two years thereafter.

7+ years' enterprise-level experience managing large scale and complex projects/programs AND 7+ years' experience in Critical Environment infrastructures (e.g., UPS, Generator, AHU) AND 7+ years' experience in physical IT infrastructures (e.g., Servers, SANs, Networking, Capacity, DC Rack/Enclosures, structured cabling) AND Experience managing budget $5M+.
