title: Director, Social & Creator Marketing - Minecraft
description:
Overview
At Mojang Studios, the creators of Minecraft, we are on a mission to build a better world through the power of play.
Why play? Well, play is at the heart of everything we do. It’s the blocky backbone of our games, the core of our development philosophy, and even the origin of our name. From the relentless experimentation of our endlessly inspiring community to the classrooms where Minecraft has become an essential teaching tool, play is the bedrock of our existence.
We enable millions to create and play together, connect people across the globe, and foster a community that is among the most active and passionate in the world. Our community is global and incredibly diverse. When we are developing anything within our franchise, we keep this in mind. We want everyone to not only feel included in Minecraft, but also to see themselves in what we make. Our goal is for the Mojang Studios team to be as diverse as our community.
Minecraft leads how Minecraft builds audiences, participates in culture, and deepens relationships with players, creators, and fans globally. The Director, Social & Creator Marketing is responsible for a connected global organization spanning organic social, including international and local market channels, influencer and community marketing, affiliate marketing and creator commerce, and editorial and direct-to-fan programming.
Exceptional cultural and creative judgment is essential. The leader must understand culture and community, recognize what is authentically Minecraft, and translate emerging audience and creator signals into distinctive ideas, stories, programming, and experiences that people want to watch, share, create with, and participate in.
The Director, Social & Creator Marketing works closely with Performance Marketing to connect these capabilities with paid media and player lifecycle marketing around shared audience, franchise, and business priorities. The leader builds the organization, talent, capabilities, partnerships, and ways of working needed to deliver impact on a global scale and compound that impact over time.
In the end, it’s the people of Mojang Studios that make this place truly special. When you join, you’ll find yourself in the company of incredibly bright, warm, and creative individuals – all united and working toward a single goal. Come help us reach it!

title: Growth Channel Incubation & Product Strategy Director
description:
Overview
As the Growth Channel Incubation & Product Strategy Director , you will identify, shape, and prove the next generation of growth capabilities across Microsoft product surfaces. You will work at the intersection of product strategy, engineering, marketing, customer experience, and business growth to determine where new product-led growth opportunities exist and what Microsoft must build to realize them.
This is a builder role, not a traditional campaign management role. You will develop growth hypotheses, translate customer and business opportunities into product and capability requirements, influence product roadmaps, and lead incubation from concept through evidence-based scale, iteration, or stop decisions. You will establish the initial strategy, partnerships, success measures, and operating model for new capabilities, then transition proven capabilities to the teams responsible for activation and scaled operations.
Responsibilities
•    Define the next growth opportunities: Identify product surfaces, customer moments, ecosystem signals, and emerging capabilities that could become new growth channels. Develop a clear point of view on where Microsoft should invest and why.
•    Create product-led growth strategy: Translate customer needs and growth opportunities into strategies, value propositions, product requirements, experience principles, and measurable growth hypotheses.
•    Influence product and engineering roadmaps: Build trusted partnerships with senior product, engineering, design, data, and marketing leaders. Represent growth requirements early in product planning and influence what is built, how it is instrumented, and how it can be activated.
•    Lead incubation from concept to proof: Design and lead pilots that test new channel mechanics, customer experiences, and product capabilities. Establish success criteria, learning agendas, dependencies, and decision points before work begins.
•    Drive evidence-based investment decisions: Synthesize customer, performance, technical, and business evidence to recommend whether capabilities should scale, iterate, or stop. Communicate recommendations clearly to executive stakeholders.
•    Build reusable capabilities, not one-off programs: Create repeatable frameworks, design patterns, playbooks, governance, and initial operating models that enable successful concepts to be used across products, audiences, and growth motions.
•    Establish capability handoffs: Define readiness criteria and partner with growth activation and channel operations leaders to transition proven capabilities into scaled execution with clear ownership, documentation, and measurement.
•    Shape the external and internal point of view: Develop a deep understanding of product-led growth practices inside and outside Microsoft. Apply relevant insights to Microsoft’s ecosystem and articulate a compelling vision for how growth capabilities should evolve.
•    Lead through influence: Drive clarity and momentum across complex, cross-organizational initiatives without relying on direct authority. Anticipate barriers, align stakeholders, make tradeoffs visible, and accelerate decisions.
Qualifications
Required/minimum qualifications
Bachelor's Degree in Business, Marketing, Communications, Economics, Public Relations, or related field AND 5+ years integrated marketing (e.g., digital, relationship, social media, campaign), event management, marketing strategy, business planning, marketing operations, or related work experience OR equivalent experience.
Additional or preferred qualifications
Master's Degree in Business, Marketing, Communications, Economics, Public Relations, or related field AND 3+ years integrated marketing (e.g., digital, relationship, social media, campaign), event management, marketing strategy, business planning, marketing operations, or related experience OR Bachelor's Degree in Business, Marketing, Communications, Economics, Public Relations, or related field AND 7+ years integrated marketing (e.g., digital, relationship, social media, campaign), event management, marketing strategy, business planning, marketing operations, or related experience OR equivalent experience.
Experience developing and influencing product, platform, channel, or customer-experience strategy in partnership with product and engineering teams.
Experience taking ambiguous, net-new opportunities from problem definition through hypothesis, pilot, measurement, and a scale, iterate, or stop recommendation.
Experience leading complex cross-functional initiatives across organizational boundaries and influencing senior stakeholders without direct authority.
Experience translating customer, business, and performance insights into clear product or capability requirements and executive-level recommendations.
Executive communication skills, including the ability to create a compelling vision, simplify complex choices, and build support ahead of delivery.
Experience with product-led growth, lifecycle growth, growth experimentation, in-product engagement, or digital platform ecosystems.
Experience partnering with engineering, product management, design, data science, privacy, legal, and marketing teams to launch new capabilities.

Microsoft Commerce is building the shopping layer that spans Copilot, Bing, Edge, and partner surfaces. The Principal Product Manager - Vertical Expansion  extends that platform into new verticals—taking the shopping experience and the capabilities behind it into fresh categories of consumer spend, and building each one on the same shared foundation.

The challenge is more than adding AI to existing workflows. We are bringing together resilient infrastructure, agent-ready capabilities, and agents that put those capabilities to work: provisioning capacity, responding to events, guiding service teams, and driving hands-free recovery and optimization where safe. title: Principal Value Creation Lead
location: United States, Multiple Locations, Multiple Locations
description:
Overview
The Frontier Transformation Framework helps our customers become Frontier Firms: organizations where AI is not a tool added to the business but part of the operating system the business runs on. The single biggest reason AI programs stall is not the technology; 95% of AI pilots fail to deliver meaningful P&L impact because they are deployed without a value hypothesis, measure the wrong things, or never baseline before building. Value Creation and Management is the discipline that closes that gap, turning AI from a cost center with unclear returns into a tracked investment with board-level visibility. The Frontier Transformation team is how the Microsoft Frontier Company, the organization this role sits within, delivers this: a small, human-agent team in which each member carries one of the Framework's eight capabilities into the customer, directs a set of digital co-workers to deliver at a scale headcount alone could not, and is designed to fade into a customer counterpart who can carry the work forward.
We are seeking a Principal Value Creation Lead  to define, design, and prove the business value of AI and agentic investment across strategic customer engagements. In this role, you will own the Value Realization Framework end to end: surfacing where AI investment aligns with a customer's strategic objectives, building the value hypotheses and investment cases that unlock funding, declaring the measurement approach before anything is built, and proving realized outcomes against baselines once solutions are live. You will operate at the intersection of finance, business strategy, engineering, and field delivery, working directly with CFOs, executive sponsors, account teams, Industry Business Architects, and delivery pods.
This is a role for people who are equally comfortable in a CFO-led value workshop and in the detail of a P&L model, who can move from strategic ambition to a defensible financial figure, and who are energized by making value real rather than anecdotal. You will help customers see, fund, and capture the value of becoming a Frontier Firm, while shaping the reusable value patterns, benchmarks, and playbooks that scale this discipline across industries. If you are excited by the opportunity to make AI investment measurable, fundable, and provable, this role is for you.
Responsibilities
Lead value discovery through the Value Realization Framework, running facilitated (often CFO-led) workshops that identify where AI and agent investment aligns with the customer's strategic business objectives.
Build and own value hypotheses for each candidate use case, framed as a single testable statement and mapped to the four value themes: Enrich Employee Experience, Reinvent Customer Experience, Reshape Business Processes, and Bend the Innovation Curve.
Produce value-ranked agent backlogs, prioritizing opportunities by business value, feasibility, and time-to-impact using the Value Rubric and Frontier Guide (Today-vs-Frontier benchmarks).
Develop the Business Case that unlocks funding: a three-scenario financial model (Conservative, Expected, Optimistic) with ROI, time-to-break-even, sensitivity analysis, and an explicit cost of inaction.
Design the Measurement Spine, decomposing the sponsor's Impact KPI into Value Driver KPIs, and defining Adoption Diagnostics (Reach and Depth) that explain why the numbers moved.
Capture before-and-after baselines for every use case ahead of deployment, using quantitative snapshots, user surveys, and stakeholder interviews, so impact can be proven afterward.
Build and run measurement instruments, including the Copilot Dashboard in Viva Insights and the per-engagement Pulse Dashboard (Power BI) that reads the Measurement Spine live.
Produce the Agentic Business Impact Report, correlating AI and agent deployment to financial KPIs such as cycle time, cost-to-serve reduction, and throughput improvements tied to specific workflows.
Own the P&L of every Frontier Loop, accounting for human labor, agents, tokens, licenses, and value leakage, and surfacing where projected value is or is not being realized.
Assess Scale Readiness at the end of each engagement (Scale / Sustain / Pivot) and translate the final value assessment into a defensible financial figure that informs the scale decision.
Develop reusable value patterns, rubrics, benchmarks, and playbooks that scale the Value Creation and Management discipline across industries and regions, and transfer the practice to the customer's own finance and value owners.
Success in this role looks like
Every AI and agent investment is anchored to a value hypothesis and a strategic KPI, with a clear baseline captured before anything is built.
Sponsors secure funding because the Business Case is credible, transparent, and directly tied to the customer's strategic priorities.
Customers move from concept to funded delivery to proven, board-visible P&L impact rather than anecdotal productivity gains.
Value is measured live against baselines, and the scale decision (Scale / Sustain / Pivot) is grounded in evidence.
The customer's own finance and value owners can run the Value Realization Framework after the engagement fades, and field learnings improve the value playbooks and benchmarks used everywhere else.

OR Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, or related field AND 8+ years experience in technology solutions, practice development, architecture, consulting, and/or technology domain (e.g., Security)

We are seeking a Principal Security Researcher to build and improve the AI-powered, agentic system at the heart of MDASH vulnerability discovery, validation, and resolution. The Microsoft 365 for Individuals team owns end-to-end marketing experiences for consumers across Microsoft 365 subscriptions and individual products in the portfolio.
In this role, you will build and own the usage consumption-to-upgrade measurement framework, helping the business understand the factors that influence Copilot engagement and subscription conversion. You will evaluate opportunities across key levers, including usage growth, engagement intensity, paywall experiences, campaigns, and in-product surfaces.
You will also help establish attribution across customer touchpoints and turn complex behavioral data, business performance signals, and research into clear recommendations that influence marketing, product, and investment decisions.
This role is great for someone who enjoys working at the intersection of data, marketing, product, and business strategy. You will work deeply with data, but your most important deliverable is not the dashboard. It is the insight, recommendation, or decision that comes from it.
The successful candidate will bring proficient analytical rigor, marketing and customer fluency, curiosity, and an ability to communicate complex insights in ways that enable action. You will also have opportunities to apply AI tools to modern marketing and analytical challenges.
What Success Looks Like?
Success in this role means helping the organization move beyond simply reporting what happened to understanding why it happened, what matters most, and what we should do next.
You will help create a shared understanding of the Copilot customer journey, identify the opportunities with the highest potential to improve engagement and subscription conversion, and provide leaders and partner teams with trusted insights they can use to make better decisions.

Build and evolve the Copilot subscription usage to upgrade funnel: Define the measurement approach for the customer journey from Copilot usage and engagement through paywall interactions and Premium subscription upgrades.

The team is seeking a Senior Data & Applied Scientist to apply advanced data science, machine learning, and artificial intelligence to transform how these professionals capture knowledge, manage work, and respond to a rapidly changing regulatory environment.
This role is aligned to the Data Science IC4 career stage. You will identify and frame complex, ambiguous problems; create project plans that account for risks, constraints, assumptions, and available resources; and connect technical measures to meaningful outcomes for legal professionals, business clients, and engineering teams.
You will build AI-enabled knowledge-management capabilities that convert fragmented requests, guidance, communications, and work product into structured, governed, and reusable institutional knowledge. The work includes improving intake and triage, enabling high-quality search and summarization, generating draft guidance, extracting insights, and automate decision support into the tools and workflows that CELA professionals use every day.
You will also develop AI solutions for continuous regulatory intelligence, including detecting and prioritizing regulatory changes, extracting and structuring requirements, mapping changes to obligations, policies, products, and controls, and producing traceable impact assessments for expert review. Success requires strong technical judgment, partnership with legal and regulatory experts, disciplined evaluation, human-in-the-loop design, clear communication, and a commitment to responsible, secure, and auditable AI.

Own complex data science engagements by translating ambiguous legal, knowledge-management, and regulatory problems into clear objectives, project plans, measurable success criteria, and roadmaps that improve outcomes over time.
Acquire, assess, and prepare structured and unstructured data from communications, documents, matters, regulatory sources, and operational systems; identify data-quality, integrity, privacy, security, bias, and ethical risks; and establish reliable data foundations for AI.
Design, develop, and evaluate statistical, machine learning, and generative AI approaches for classification, routing, retrieval, summarization, knowledge drafting, metadata extraction, regulatory monitoring, requirements extraction, and impact analysis.
Write efficient, readable, extensible, production-quality analysis and software code; diagnose complex issues; prototype and operationalize scalable solutions; and partner with engineering teams on deployment, monitoring, maintenance, and continuous improvement.
Define evaluation metrics and human-review workflows that connect technical performance to accuracy, consistency, traceability, adoption, capacity returned, and business value, while ensuring that legal and regulatory judgment remains with accountable experts.
Build trusted partnerships with legal professionals, policy experts, engineers, researchers, and business stakeholders; influence decisions through clear narratives and visualizations; mentor less experienced practitioners; and establish responsible AI, data, and engineering best practices across the team.

Do you want to be at the forefront of innovating the latest hardware designs to propel Microsoft’s cloud growth? Are you seeking a unique career opportunity that combines technical capabilities, cross-team collaboration, with business insight and strategy?
Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees, we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to achieve our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond. In alignment with our Microsoft values, we are committed to cultivating an inclusive work environment for all employees to positively impact our culture every day.
Join the Systems Planning and Architecture (SPARC) team within Microsoft’s Azure Hardware Systems and Infrastructure (AHSI) organization, the team behind Microsoft’s expanding Cloud Infrastructure and for powering Microsoft’s “Intelligent Cloud” mission. Microsoft delivers more than 200 online services to more than one billion individuals worldwide, and AHSI is the team behind our expanding cloud infrastructure. We deliver the core infrastructure and foundational technologies for Microsoft's cloud businesses including Microsoft Azure, Bing, MSN, Office 365, OneDrive, Skype, Teams and Xbox Live.
As a Senior Hardware Engineer – FPGA & Platform Security on SPARC, you will help define and build the hardware root of trust that protects Azure’s fleet, from silicon and FPGA prototypes through firmware, BMC, and datacenter deployment. You will translate security architecture into clear requirements, prototype and validate features such as secure boot, attestation, and secure recovery, and partner with silicon, firmware, and industry teams, including open efforts such as Caliptra and OCP S.A.F.E. This opportunity will allow you to deepen your expertise in hardware-rooted security, influence open industry standards, and see your work ship at hyperscale. This role is based in Redmond, WA or Mountain View, CA and requires three days per week in the office.
Responsibilities
Define requirements, specifications, and interface definitions for server platform features, including trust and integrity capabilities such as secure boot, attestation, and firmware recovery.
Lead bring-up of new server, SoC, and FPGA-based platforms, from first power-on through firmware, BMC, and OS boot, and work with hardware and firmware partners to resolve issues quickly.
Set up, maintain, and evolve lab infrastructure, including racks, networking, power, debug tooling, and remote management access, so engineers can validate new platforms efficiently.
Prototype and integrate root-of-trust and HSM capabilities (for example, Caliptra) on FPGA and emulation platforms, and develop validation plans that cover normal, fault, and recovery scenarios.
Build diagnostics, telemetry, and automated recovery tools that help fleet hardware detect problems, report its health, and return to a known-good state with minimal manual intervention.
Debug complex system-level issues across silicon, FPGA, firmware, BMC, and software boundaries, and turn findings into improvements in design, tooling, and process.
Partner with silicon vendors, ODMs, and industry groups such as OCP to drive adoption of platform requirements, mentor other engineers, and create reusable procedures and documentation.

Master's Degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or related field AND 3+ years technical engineering experience OR Bachelor's Degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or related field AND 5+ years technical engineering experience OR equivalent experience

Experience with hardware or platform security technologies such as secure boot, attestation, hardware root of trust, or cryptographic hardware.
Hands-on experience with FPGA design, prototyping, or emulation (Verilog/SystemVerilog and vendor toolchains) and lab bring-up of server or SoC platforms.
Experience with root-of-trust or HSM architectures (for example, Caliptra, TPM, DICE, SPDM) and platform firmware resiliency standards such as NIST SP 800-193.

The S enior Package Design Engineer will be responsible for providing expertise, insight, and support to the Silicon development team through the entire life cycle of the product.  In this role, you will be responsible for the design and implementation of new custom Silicon devices, in particular substrate, interposer, and bridge design. Drive package and PCB co-design: define BGA ballout and bump plans and optimize floorplans with SI/PI, silicon PD/RTL, PCB, DFT and ATE teams to meet system-level specs.

Work with silicon and platform architects, board designers, and thermal, power and performance engineers to balance trade-offs and close on design decisions.
Work with package technologists on the evaluation and recommendation of new packaging technology, device/package qualification and supplier assessment
Work with external partners (OSATs, substrate and interposer suppliers, design-service partners) on design rules, design reviews and tapeout deliverables.
Help design test vehicles that validate new package technologies and design rules.
Identify design risks in new technologies and tool flows early, propose mitigations, and report status and issues to program leadership.
Manage die-to-interposer-to-substrate connectivity and netlists across multi-die designs, and keep them in sync through design changes (ECOs).
Design the package power delivery network (planes, layer stack-up, decoupling capacitor placement) with PI engineers to meet power integrity targets.

For more information about our team, visit https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/quantum .
As a Senior Quantum Software Engineer in High Performance Computing (HPC) Infrastructure, you will be the technical owner of our Linux HPC platform, including compute, job scheduling, shared storage, remote graphical desktop access for users on Windows computers, licensed engineering software, and the Microsoft Azure resources that support them. You will set the standards for how the platform is designed, operated, and supported, and you will deliver dependable, secure, and cost-effective solutions. Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. You will use artificial intelligence (AI) tools and practices across the software development lifecycle in a disciplined manner, taking responsibility for the content of your AI-generated changes to artifacts and applying appropriate tooling and processes. title: Applied Scientist, Product Policy Research & Measurement
description:
About the Team

The Product Policy team develops and implements policies that shape how OpenAI’s technology is built and used. We work with teams across the company to turn complex questions about AI’s benefits and risks into practical guidance for responsible research, product development, and deployment.

About the Role

We are hiring a senior applied scientist to study how AI affects people and society using OpenAI production data, experiments, and social science methods. This role sits at the intersection of applied social science, AI, and product policy. The scientist will own research from an ambiguous question through study design, data collection and analysis, methodological validation, and recommendations. Their work will inform product and policy decisions and, where appropriate, contribute to external publications. We are looking for a hands-on empirical social scientist with exceptional methodological judgment.

In this role, you will:

 - Develop and execute a research agenda on AI’s social impact, including effects on well-being, learning, social connection, trust, and human decision-making, in partnership with product and policy teams.

 - Own empirical studies end to end: define the question and estimand, choose the design, build the dataset, conduct the analysis, and explain what the evidence supports.

 - Analyze large-scale production and behavioral data, linking them to experiments, surveys, or external outcomes when appropriate to measure real-world effects.

 - Design randomized experiments and credible observational studies; test identification assumptions, quantify uncertainty, and distinguish association from causal effects.

 - Develop and validate measures of social outcomes, including human and LLM-assisted annotations; assess measurement error, subgroup performance, and drift.

 - Translate findings into concrete product and policy recommendations, with clear limits on causal interpretation, generalizability, and decision confidence.

 - Partner with Product Policy, Research, Product, Data Science, Engineering, UXR, Legal, and domain experts; contribute rigorous work to external publications when appropriate.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

 - A PhD or equivalent research experience in sociology, political science, psychology, communication, computational social science, or a related empirical field, with demonstrated independent research ownership.

 - Deep expertise in research design, causal inference, experimentation, statistical analysis, and measurement, demonstrated through work you can personally explain and defend.

 - Strong SQL and Python or R skills, with experience independently constructing and analyzing complex behavioral datasets and producing reproducible research.

 - A record of research that informs consequential decisions about technology and people, with the judgment to identify both useful findings and unresolved uncertainty.

 - Clear writing for technical and policy audiences, and experience producing rigorous research papers or equivalent public technical work.

OpenAI is building the next generation of advertising for an AI-powered world. As AI changes how people discover information, explore possibilities, and make decisions, we believe this presents a huge opportunity for small and medium-sized businesses to connect with customers in new ways.

The SMB Ads Marketing team is building this opportunity from the ground up. We define how businesses discover OpenAI’s advertising platform, become successful advertisers, and grow their investment over time. Working closely with Product, Ads Engineering, Data Science, and Sales, we combine customer insight, rigorous experimentation, and fast execution to turn early opportunities into scalable growth.

About the Role

We are looking for an Audience & Content Growth Lead to build the global content and education programs that inspire, inform and engage SMB advertisers.

This is a zero-to-one opportunity to shape how small businesses discover and understand advertising with OpenAI. You will turn customer needs, product capabilities and advertiser success stories into compelling content—from webinars and educational video series to case studies, industry-specific playbooks and creator-led programs.

The role combines two areas of ownership: developing content specifically for SMB audiences and building effective ways to distribute it. You will lead programs directly while partnering with teams that own web, social, lifecycle marketing, growth and regional channels to reach the right audiences at scale.

Success means building an engaged SMB audience and helping businesses move from awareness to understanding, confidence and action.

In This Role, You Will

 - Set the global SMB content strategy and editorial roadmap, grounded in customer needs, industry priorities, and advertiser maturity.

 - Create compelling customer stories, case studies, vertical playbooks, guides, videos, and thought leadership that make advertising accessible and actionable.

 - Launch repeatable education programs through webinars, expert sessions, workshops, and on-demand learning that help businesses get started and improve their advertising.

 - Grow audiences through owned, shared, and partner channels. Build distribution plans with web, social, growth, lifecycle, and regional teams.

 - Develop creator-, expert-, and customer-led programs that combine credible education, authentic storytelling, and relevant audience reach.

 - Scale programs across markets with regional teams. Adapt formats, languages, customer stories, and distribution to local needs.

 - Lead editorial planning, production, agencies, and creative contributors. Maintain quality, accessibility, and accuracy, using AI to support content creation, adaptation, and reuse.

 - Measure audience quality, engagement, learning, and advertiser action with Growth, Lifecycle, and Data Science. Use experiments and feedback to improve content and distribution.

You Might Thrive in This Role If You

 - Bring 10+ years of experience in content marketing, audience development, or customer education, including programs for SMBs or advertisers.

 - Demonstrate ownership of content creation and distribution that grows relevant audiences and drives customer action.

 - Translate complex products into clear, engaging content through strong editorial judgment and storytelling.

 - Build repeatable programs across formats such as webinars, video, customer stories, vertical playbooks, and creator-led content.

 - Lead cross-functional and partner-led distribution, aligning teams around shared priorities and measurable outcomes.

 - Measure learning, intent, and business impact alongside content consumption.

 - Adapt global programs to different markets and audiences in partnership with regional teams.

 - Combine strategy with hands-on writing, editing, creative briefing, and program execution.

Preferred Experience

 - Bring experience with advertising platforms, marketplaces, or technology businesses serving SMBs.

 - Build on experience in advertiser education, customer advocacy, creator partnerships, or partner-distributed learning.

 - Draw on experience in both established technology organizations and startup or zero-to-one environments.

Workplace & Location

 - San Francisco, CA. This role requires a hybrid schedule with an in office requirement from Monday - Wednesday.

title: Certification Architect
description:
About the Team

Customer Education helps customers build the practical skills and confidence to use AI and OpenAI products safely and effectively. We bring together customer insight, learning and enablement expertise, product signals, and measurement to help organizations move from access to durable adoption.

Within Customer Education, the Certification team helps individuals demonstrate competence for in-demand AI skills and helps customers and partners validate that their workforce has the skills they need to meet their AI-enabled business goals. Our work centers on the belief that learners should understand where to go to build skills and capabilities, how to demonstrate them, and what to pursue next. Similarly, Enterprise leaders should understand what each credential signifies and how it supports workforce readiness. We do this with transparency for the overall OpenAI credential framework and providing trusted, role-based certifications that verify practical capability.

About the Role

As Certification Architect, you will define the framework, standards, and assessment architecture that make OpenAI certifications a trusted signal of demonstrated capability.

This is a senior hands-on role on the Certification team that will build reusable foundations for a growing portfolio: clear competency standards, defensible assessments, scalable in-product delivery, and evidence of continued competence.

We’re looking for someone who combines deep certification and assessment expertise with the ability to innovate new and meaningful ways to demonstrate practical AI competence. You will work closely with certification specialists, technical subject matter experts, learning product and engineering teams, operations and policy partners, and stakeholders across the go-to-market organization.

The program is early, and you will help shape how people demonstrate capability in ChatGPT and Codex. Success means building standards that are rigorous, usable, and adaptable as AI technology and professional roles evolve.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

 - Own the credential framework and shared competency standards, distinguishing completed learning, demonstrated skills, and formal certification, with clear capability claims and evidence requirements for each.

 - Establish reusable assessment standards and guidance for certification pods across job-task analysis, competency models, assessment blueprints, performance tasks, scoring rubrics, and passing standards.

 - Own the validation approach and evidence documentation requirements. Partner with pod leaders to validate certification proposals against job relevance, representative task coverage, scoring consistency, fairness, and appropriate interpretation of results.

 - Define exam delivery architecture and requirements with product, engineering, operations, and third parties, spanning registration, identity verification, monitoring, permitted assistance, evidence capture, scoring, human review, appeals, customer support, and record management.

 - Define expectations for continued competence validation post-assessment.

 - Partner with learning, operations, policy, legal, privacy, security, and accessibility teams to align preparation with competencies while protecting assessment integrity and establishing appropriate evidence access, retention, accommodations, and review processes.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have 10+ years experience designing and delivering professional technical IT industry certifications or assessments that support credible claims about what people can do.

 - Have led design of performance-based assessments for AI, software development, technical architecture, or customer-facing implementation roles.

 - Have built credential frameworks, competency models, or shared assessment standards that work across multiple roles or programs.

 - Have led job-task analysis, assessment blueprints, performance-based assessment, rubric design, standard setting, and the evidence needed to support valid and fair certification decisions.

 - Can translate assessment experience requirements into exam delivery specifications for third parties and learning product teams.

 - Have worked closely with certification specialists, psychometricians and subject matter experts to validate assessment and scoring standards and improve assessment quality.

 - Communicate complex standards clearly to technical and nontechnical partners, and build alignment across teams without relying on formal authority.

 - Enjoy hands-on work, from drafting standards and reviewing assessment designs to resolving practical delivery tradeoffs with a small team.

 - Exercise sound judgment in ambiguous environments, balancing rigor, candidate experience, delivery feasibility, and the pace of technology change.

 - Care deeply about accessibility, fairness, and the integrity of credentials that individuals and employers rely on.

 - Build reusable approaches while recognizing where different roles need distinct competency models, tasks, and evidence.

Additional experience that would be helpful includes:

 - Validating AI-assisted scoring, model evaluations, or other automated approaches to evaluating human performance.

 - Working with secure assessment delivery, identity verification, credential issuance, learner records, or assessment technology providers.

 - Developing innovative approaches to recertification, ongoing competence, or assessment of authentic work.

 - Building products that serve both individual users and organizations.

OpenAI’s Sales team partners with advertisers to understand their businesses, develop meaningful advertising solutions, and drive long-term growth on the platform while maintaining strong standards for user trust and platform integrity.


ABOUT THE ROLE

This role will focus on growing advertising revenue across Consumer Packaged Goods (CPG), including food and beverage, beauty and personal care, household products, and adjacent everyday consumer categories.

You will own the full sales cycle—from prospecting through deal closure—and build strategic relationships with senior brand, media, and commerce decision-makers. We’re looking for sales leaders to build and develop high-performing teams, deepen strategic customer relationships, and shape OpenAI’s growth across this industry.

Our customers span health systems, payers, pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies, medical technology companies, and healthcare technology organizations. Your team will help customers identify opportunities to improve workforce productivity, accelerate research and discovery, strengthen operations, and enhance patient, member, and customer experiences.

You’ll be a hands-on leader who coaches teams through complex enterprise sales cycles, builds executive relationships, and helps customers move from experimentation to scaled deployment. Success requires understanding how healthcare and life sciences organizations evaluate technology, establish trust, and adopt AI responsibly.

You’ll also help define our industry go-to-market strategy, operating model, and playbooks. Working across commercial, research, clinical, operational, and technical stakeholders, you’ll guide your team in identifying high-value opportunities and building credible business cases for adoption.

We’re hiring across our growing Healthcare and Life Sciences sales leadership team. Specific responsibilities and team scope will reflect the opportunity and your experience.

In this role, you will:

 - Recruit, develop, and lead high-performing enterprise sales teams serving strategic healthcare and life sciences accounts across North America.

 - Build a strong coaching culture through deal reviews, account strategy sessions, customer engagement, and structured development.

 - Shape industry and segment-specific go-to-market strategies, including account segmentation, prioritization, executive engagement, and territory planning.

 - Drive disciplined pipeline generation, accurate forecasting, and consistent execution across complex enterprise opportunities.

 - Guide consultative sales cycles involving business leaders, IT, research and development, clinical teams, operations, security, privacy, compliance, procurement, and legal.

 - Help customers connect AI capabilities to measurable outcomes across knowledge work, research, administrative workflows, commercial operations, and patient and member engagement.

 - Coach teams to build business cases grounded in industry economics, implementation feasibility, organizational readiness, and customer priorities.

 - Help customers move from pilots to broader adoption through clear success criteria, executive sponsorship, deployment planning, and change management.

 - Partner with Product, Solutions Architecture, Technical Success, Legal, Security, Finance, and Marketing to support customer success and industry growth.

 - Bring structured feedback to Product and leadership on industry needs, integration requirements, adoption barriers, competitive dynamics, and emerging opportunities.

 - Establish a culture of accountability, customer focus, and operational excellence within a low-ego, collaborative environment.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

 - 15+ years of enterprise sales, go-to-market, or sales leadership experience, including significant experience leading teams selling into large healthcare or life sciences organizations.

 - A proven track record of building and scaling enterprise sales teams responsible for complex strategic accounts and substantial revenue targets.

 - Demonstrated ability to coach senior Account Directors through opportunities involving multiple decision-makers, extended evaluation cycles, and significant organizational dependencies.

 - Deep expertise in one or more healthcare and life sciences segments, such as providers, payers, pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies, medical technology, or healthcare technology, including their distinct priorities, buying processes, and operating models.

 - Experience leading consultative, multi-product, or platform-based enterprise sales involving executive sponsors, technical buyers, and clinical, research, commercial, or operational stakeholders.

 - A track record of developing new go-to-market motions and turning early customer adoption into repeatable, scalable growth.

 - Demonstrated ability to help customers evaluate technology investments through measurable business value, implementation feasibility, and long-term adoption.

 - Strong operational rigor across forecasting, pipeline management, territory planning, and performance management.

 - Sound judgment in positioning AI use cases with clear value, appropriate scope, and attention to customer requirements for privacy, security, governance, and human oversight.

 - The ability to operate effectively in a fast-moving, ambiguous environment while helping teams maintain focus and execution discipline.

 - A low-ego leadership style with a demonstrated commitment to developing talent, building trust, and creating high-performing teams.

 - Proven experience leading enterprise sales teams serving large, complex healthcare or life sciences accounts.

 - Strong understanding of enterprise buying processes within healthcare or life sciences, including how business, technical, operational, privacy, security, and compliance stakeholders evaluate and adopt new technology.

title: Firmware Engineer, Robotics
description:
About the Team

We are building general-purpose robotics. In the short term, we are focused on robots to support skilled workers to build our future infrastructure. In the long term, we imagine everyone having a personal robot doing anything they need. Progress is rapid, and based on a foundation of co-design between robotics hardware and ML research.

About the Role

As a Firmware Engineer, you will define and drive the architecture of embedded systems for next-generation hardware products. You will own foundational firmware decisions across real-time execution, device bring-up, hardware interfaces, fault handling, safety mechanisms, and production readiness.

We’re looking for someone with deep experience building safety-critical or high-consequence systems, where failures can have meaningful consequences. You should be comfortable reasoning about risk, designing for diagnosability and graceful degradation, and creating engineering practices that raise the reliability bar for the entire team.

You should also be unusually good at moving fast. Sometimes the right answer is a carefully reviewed architecture that will endure for years; sometimes it is getting a rough-but-useful prototype working by the end of the afternoon so the team can learn something concrete tomorrow. We value engineers who know the difference, make that call well, and can operate credibly in both modes.

You will be both a technical leader and a hands-on builder: setting direction, reviewing critical designs, unblocking the hardest problems, and writing production firmware when it matters most.

Our embedded stack uses a lot of Rust. Extensive experience in the language is a big help!

In this role, you will:

 - Rapidly bring up new hardware and set execution pace for the team.

 - Lead firmware architecture for embedded systems spanning boot, RTOS/runtime behavior, peripheral control, power management, communications, and field diagnostics.

 - Define engineering standards for reliability, fault tolerance, observability, and maintainability across the firmware stack.

 - Design and review safety-critical mechanisms, including fault detection, recovery paths, watchdog strategies, redundancy where appropriate, and safe-state behavior.

 - Build quick, scrappy prototypes when speed of learning matters, then harden the right ideas into production-quality systems.

 - Partner closely with engineers in hardware, software, and AI research from early prototype through production.

 - Build rigorous bring-up, validation, and release processes for embedded platforms.

 - Establish testing strategies across unit, hardware-in-the-loop, integration, stress, and failure-injection testing.

 - Drive root-cause analysis for subtle hardware, firmware, and system interactions.

 - Make clear tradeoffs across performance, memory, power, schedule, and safety.

 - Mentor firmware engineers and help shape a culture of urgency, technical rigor, practical judgment, and high-quality execution.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have extensive experience developing firmware in an iterative environment.

 - Get a thrill from bringing up new hardware and taking end-to-end ownership over ensuring it works.

 - Have led architecture and delivery for complex embedded products that shipped to real users or operated in demanding production environments.

 - Are deeply fluent in low-level languages (we use Rust!) and comfortable working close to hardware under real-time constraints.

 - Understand embedded systems from first principles, including interrupts, scheduling, memory layout, buses, DMA, timing behavior, and failure modes.

 - Have strong instincts for defensive design, fault containment, validation depth, and post-deployment diagnosability.

 - Know when to build the durable system and when to produce the fastest credible artifact that unlocks the next decision.

 - Communicate clearly across disciplines and can turn ambiguity into sound technical direction.

 - Care about building systems that are not only fast and capable, but also trustworthy.

 - Make heavy use of Codex, Claude Code, or similar AI-assisted coding systems to accelerate implementation, prototyping, debugging, and iteration.

Nice to have:

 - Experience with Rust in embedded environments.

 - Experience with Embassy or other async embedded Rust frameworks.

 - Familiarity with mixed-language firmware architectures, including introducing Rust incrementally into existing C/C++ systems.

 - Experience with ARM Cortex-M or Cortex-R platforms, RTOSes, and low-power embedded designs.

 - Experience building firmware for sensor-rich, latency-sensitive, or tightly integrated electromechanical products.

We’re looking for a strategic, hands-on individual contributor to join our GTM Strategy & Growth team and help shape how we grow and scale our B2B business across products, customer segments, and routes to market. This is a generalist role for someone who combines strong product intuition with thoughtful GTM strategy and can flex seamlessly between strategic thinking and operational execution.

You’ll translate business priorities into clear growth strategies, operating plans, and cross-functional execution. Your work may span product launches, commercialization models, customer growth initiatives, market expansion, and the systems and processes that help the business scale.

You should be highly analytical, comfortable working across a range of products and business problems, and experienced navigating complex cross-functional environments. Experience with technical or API-based products is valuable, but the most important qualities are strategic range, sound judgment, and the ability to turn customer, product, and market insights into practical recommendations and action.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

 - Drive go-to-market strategy across products, customer segments, and routes to market, partnering closely with Product and GTM leaders to shape growth priorities and commercialization approaches.

 - Develop goals, launch success metrics, and operating KPIs for new initiatives, and monitor performance in partnership with Data Science and Analytics teams.

 - Develop growth strategies and strategic bets across new products, capabilities, customer motions, and market opportunities.

 - Develop customer segmentation frameworks and tailored strategies for different customer profiles, industries, and stages of adoption.

 - Partner with Product teams to provide structured customer feedback, market insights, and prioritization input that informs product roadmap decisions.

 - Collaborate with Pricing, Finance, and Product teams to develop commercial models, packaging, and monetization strategies, ensuring downstream GTM execution aligns with the broader commercial strategy.

 - Conduct market, competitive, and customer research to identify whitespace opportunities and inform strategic decision-making.

 - Partner cross-functionally with Sales, Customer Success, Marketing, Product, Finance, and Operations to align on priorities and execute against business goals.

 - Analyze business performance and identify opportunities to improve GTM strategy and operating plans based on data, customer insights, and market dynamics.

You might thrive in this role if you:

title: Security Incident Response Team Manager
description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

Ensuring that advanced AI benefits humanity requires protecting the research, infrastructure, and trust that make its development and deployment possible. OpenAI Security defends our model IP, people, products, and users against sophisticated adversaries across GPU supercomputing, multicloud environments, datacenters, and emerging agent systems. The Security Incident Response Team (SIRT) leads the response when those defenses are tested—establishing what happened, limiting harm, and strengthening our ability to protect frontier AI.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for a hands-on technical leader to build the incident response team that protects OpenAI as AI capabilities and the threats surrounding them evolve. You will command consequential incidents, lead technically demanding investigations, and make containment and recovery decisions when evidence is incomplete and the stakes are high. You will also shape how frontier models change incident response: using OpenAI’s own technology to help responders connect evidence, test hypotheses, and act effectively at a scale that manual workflows cannot support. Partnering with Research, Infrastructure, Product Security, Enterprise Security, IT, and Engineering, you will build exceptional responders, dependable AI-powered capabilities, and stronger defenses through every investigation.




IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Hire, coach, and develop exceptional incident responders who combine investigative depth, engineering ability, and sound judgment. Build a team that challenges assumptions, surfaces uncertainty early, and uses AI to expand its capabilities. Develop technical leaders who can make and explain difficult decisions under pressure.

 - Lead incident command for complex threats to OpenAI’s research, products, and infrastructure. Establish severity and scope, coordinate investigation workstreams, and weigh containment options against ongoing exposure and disruption to research or production.

 - Build and ship agentic capabilities using OpenAI’s models for evidence collection, investigation context, response coordination, and bounded response workflows. Partner with platform engineers to integrate tools and data, evaluate accuracy and failure modes, and ensure reliable, auditable operation with human approval for consequential actions.

 - Set investigation standards for sophisticated adversaries and insider threats across identity, endpoints, cloud, Kubernetes, and large-scale compute. Help responders reconstruct activity, test competing hypotheses, preserve evidence, and make uncertainty explicit.

 - Drive incidents to verified closure. Work with accountable owners to validate containment and recovery, document remaining risk, and track corrective actions that reduce the likelihood or impact of recurrence.

 - Coordinate with engineering, infrastructure, legal, privacy, and other stakeholders throughout an incident. Give executives clear updates on impact, uncertainty, decisions, and the next update without overstating what the evidence supports.

 - Build sustainable on-call coverage, escalation paths, and handoffs across regions. Balance urgent response with training and planned improvements, and protect the team’s ability to recover after demanding incidents.

 - Build readiness into new research and infrastructure capabilities with their owners. Exercise playbooks, escalation paths, and containment options, including scenarios involving agents operating across systems at scale.

 - Turn incident evidence into stronger defenses with Detection Engineering, Threat Intelligence, Security Observability, and security platform teams. Identify what should have exposed an intrusion earlier, what prevented a faster or more confident investigation, and which capabilities would have changed the outcome. Translate those findings into tested improvements with clear owners.

 - Prioritize improvements using incident outcomes and readiness evidence. Measure response quality and effectiveness, make tradeoffs explicit, and address recurring friction without reducing success to ticket volume or speed alone.

 - You bring strong AI fluency and an AI-first builder mindset. You have used models or agents to improve real investigation or response workflows and can show validated results. You understand their failure modes and pair ambitious automation with rigorous evaluations and human judgment.

 - You are a hands-on builder with deep investigation expertise across identity, cloud, host, and infrastructure systems. You can prototype tools, write scripts or code, and coach responders through difficult evidence questions, including unfamiliar parts of the stack.

title: Thermal Engineer
description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

OpenAI’s Hardware organization develops silicon and system-level solutions designed for the unique demands of advanced AI workloads. The team is responsible for building the next generation of AI-native silicon while working closely with software and research partners to co-design hardware tightly integrated with AI models. In addition to delivering production-grade silicon for OpenAI’s supercomputing infrastructure, the team also creates custom design tools and methodologies that accelerate innovation and enable hardware optimized specifically for AI.


ABOUT THE ROLE

We are looking for an experienced Thermal Engineer with 7+ years of experience in thermal management of IT hardware from chip/package to system levels. You’ll work alongside experts in thermal, mechanical, electrical, software, and systems engineering to support the design, analysis, and validation of thermal solutions that ensure the reliability, efficiency, and longevity of mission-critical hardware. This position requires strong analytical skills, hands-on testing experience, and the ability to work in a fast-paced, cross-disciplinary environment.


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Design and optimize thermal solutions for data center hardware, including chips, power modules, and system-level cooling architectures

 - Evaluate thermal performance at the chip, package, and board levels, addressing challenges related to power density, heat dissipation, and thermal interface materials

 - Perform thermal modeling and simulation to predict temperature profiles and identify thermal bottlenecks

 - Collaborate with cross-functional teams to integrate thermal management strategies into hardware design, from concept to mass production

 - Support lab testing and validation, including the setup of thermal experiments, data acquisition, and troubleshooting of thermal performance issues

 - Design and select thermal components, such as cold plates, heat sinks, fans, vapor chambers, and thermal interface materials (TIMs)

 - Work with firmware and electrical engineers to define and implement thermal control algorithms for dynamic power and cooling management.

 - Conduct feasibility studies and trade-off analyses to evaluate cooling technologies and improve system thermal efficiency

 - Partner with suppliers and manufacturers to support the development of custom thermal components and ensure quality in production


QUALIFICATIONS

 - Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Thermal Engineering, or a related field (Master’s preferred).

 - 7+ years of industry experience in thermal design, simulation, and validation for IT hardware

 - Proficiency in thermal simulation software and CAD tools

 - Strong understanding of heat transfer principles, thermodynamics, and fluid mechanics, with an emphasis on electronics cooling

 - Hands-on experience with thermal testing equipment, including thermocouples, infrared cameras, wind tunnels, and P-Q characterization setups

 - Experience in chip/package-level thermal analysis, including die-level heat spreading, and package thermal modeling

 - Ability to analyze experimental data, identify root causes of thermal issues, and implement corrective actions

 - Strong problem-solving skills, with the ability to perform first-principles calculations to support design decisions.

 - Self-driven, detail-oriented, and able to work independently or collaboratively in cross-functional engineering environments


PREFERRED SKILLS

 - 10+ years of industry experience in thermal design, simulation, and validation for IT hardware

 - Extensive experience with data center hardware or high-performance computing systems at scale

 - Practical experience in developing advanced cooling technologies

 - Familiarity with thermal control algorithms and dynamic thermal management techniques

 - Understanding of reliability testing, failure analysis, and thermal stress testing for electronic components

 - Experience working with suppliers and manufacturing partners to support thermal solution development and production ramp-up

title: Threat Detection and Response Engineering Manager
description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

OpenAI’s mission depends on developing and deploying powerful AI responsibly. Security makes that possible by protecting our research, people, products, and users while enabling progress. We defend sensitive research and other intellectual property, customer data, and the infrastructure behind frontier AI—from GPU supercomputing and multicloud environments to datacenters and emerging agent systems. Threat Detection Engineering builds and operates the detections and investigative workflows that turn adversary activity into effective response.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for a hands-on technical leader to guide the engineers who identify and investigate threats to OpenAI and build the capabilities to contain them. You’ll hire and develop engineers, set technical direction, and prioritize risks to OpenAI’s intellectual property, customer data, and critical infrastructure.

Your team will take an agent-first approach across the detection and response lifecycle, using OpenAI’s models to develop detections, triage signals, investigate suspicious activity, and support bounded response and continuous improvement. You’ll turn advances in model capability into dependable defenses, own their effectiveness, and work with security, research, and infrastructure partners to ensure findings lead to effective action. You’ll establish where agents can act independently and where human judgment and approval are essential.




IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Hire, coach, and develop engineers. Set clear expectations, provide regular feedback, grow technical leadership, and build a team that reviews work rigorously and learns from missed detections and noisy signals.

 - Set a threat-informed roadmap. Prioritize detection work based on how external and internal actors could target the systems where we train and evaluate frontier models, the production services that run inference and power our products worldwide, the datacenter hardware and networks that support both, and the devices, identities, and applications employees rely on. Balance investment in emerging threats with closing known coverage gaps and keeping existing detections effective.

 - Own detection and investigation as a complete workflow. Embed agent-driven triage and investigation in the detections your team operates. Surface findings when the evidence points to a likely threat that warrants action. When a finding warrants formal incident response, bring the evidence to the Security Incident Response Team (SIRT) and support the investigation SIRT leads.

 - Build response and containment capabilities tailored to our infrastructure. Work with infrastructure and system owners to develop and test the controls responders need to contain threats in their environments. Define when human approval is required and how to verify that containment worked.

 - Apply models across the detection engineering lifecycle. Use OpenAI’s models to help develop threat hypotheses, author and test detections, deploy and tune them, and incorporate investigation findings into better coverage. Evaluate the effectiveness of individual agents and the complete workflows they support.

 - Turn model advances into tested defenses. Prototype new approaches using OpenAI’s models, evaluate them against realistic adversary behavior and analyst baselines, and move successful experiments into production. Use operational evidence to identify model limitations and partner with Research and Engineering to address them.

 - Anticipate emerging threats. Translate adversary intelligence and incident findings into testable detection hypotheses. Work with researchers and infrastructure owners on risks specific to a frontier AI lab, such as increasingly capable agents operating across systems with access to sensitive research. Determine what evidence would reveal compromise and what response would be effective.

 - Establish the visibility needed to detect, investigate, and respond. Partner with Security Observability and infrastructure owners to define telemetry and forensic data requirements. Drive improvements where missing evidence, unreliable data, or limited controls prevent the team from identifying threats or taking effective action.

 - Engineer for measurable security outcomes. Use replay, adversarial validation, and regression testing to assess whether workflows find intended threats, distinguish benign activity, and reach defensible conclusions. Establish code review, documentation, staged rollout, monitoring, and rollback practices. Measure coverage, investigation accuracy, time to identify threats, and effectiveness of response.

 - Contribute during incidents. The Security Incident Response Team (SIRT) leads formal incident response. Your team contributes investigative expertise and uses incident findings to improve detections.
   
   


YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU:

 - Think like an adversary and demand evidence as a defender. You question whether apparent coverage would survive a determined attacker, distinguish plausible explanations from supported conclusions, and stay accountable for threats that existing tools and playbooks miss.

 - Have managed security or software engineers and can demonstrate how you have hired, coached, developed technical judgment, and improved a team’s ability to deliver.

 - Are a hands-on builder who can prototype tools, write and review code, and guide engineers through complex detection, investigation, and response designs.

 - Bring strong AI fluency and have built systems that test how models or agents can improve cyber defense. You have evaluated real security workflows against meaningful baselines and can explain what improved, what failed, and what you changed. You understand model failure modes and design reliable workflows with bounded permissions and clear human decision points.

 - Have built or operated threat detections and led technical investigations. You understand adversary tradecraft and can assess evidence, scope, and uncertainty across complex environments.

 - Understand how identity, endpoint, cloud, Kubernetes, and infrastructure telemetry supports investigations. You can reason about response and containment in unfamiliar systems and work with their owners to build practical capabilities.

 - Have used testing and operational feedback to improve security outcomes. You can explain tradeoffs among coverage, accuracy, speed, and human workload, and choose measures that reflect whether threats are being found and addressed.

 - Can build a focused roadmap and strong cross-functional partnerships in a rapidly changing environment. You enable researchers and engineers to move quickly while following through on security requirements and dependable operations.

title: Manager, Sourcing - MTO (Jewelry)
description:
ABOUT QUINCE
Quince is a destination for builders, creators, innovators, and operators who want to come together and challenge the status quo. Our mission is simple: make really high quality essentials for really low prices, fairly and sustainably. We deliver on that mission through a unique manufacturer-to-consumer (M2C) model eliminating the layers of traditional retail that add cost and result in consumers paying more than they need to. We find, build relationships with, and work directly with the manufacturing partners behind some of the world’s finest products. From there, our teams design smart, efficient operational processes  and build and deploy proprietary technology, AI, and analytics to help us scale fast.
What began with a small assortment of elevated basics has quickly grown into a cross-category brand spanning apparel, accessories, home goods, and more. Today, tens of millions of people across a growing number of countries come – and return – to Quince because they trust us to deliver.
OUR CULTURE
Quince is a culture built for builders by builders. Our way of working starts with a blank sheet of paper. We question conventional thinking, use technology and data to uncover new opportunities, and move quickly to turn ideas into reality. We aren’t interested in replicating how others do retail. We’re building a better way – at a speed and scale unlike anything that’s been done before.
We dream big and chase the hard problems others shy away from. Rejecting long-held assumptions is part of our company's DNA.  Where conventional wisdom says you have to choose – soft or durable, speed or rigor, quality or price – we ask why that trade-off has to exist in the first place.
Our pace is fast and the bar is high because our customers expect a lot from us and we refuse to let them down. We believe the best results come from challenging ourselves, learning from one another, and building on each other's strengths.
Here, responsibility is not determined by role, tenure, or seniority. Every team member - no matter their level - has the opportunity to drive our business and shape our trajectory.
If you’re someone who likes to imagine new possibilities and build better systems rather than plug-in to outdated ones, Quince is the place for you.
THE ROLE
Sourcing Manager, MTO (Jewelry)
We are seeking a  Sourcing Manager, MTO to own and drive the complete made-to-order workflow for jewelry—from order placement through final customer delivery—ensuring our 3-week fulfillment promise is met reliably, with zero defects and exceptional customer experiences. Reporting to the VP of Sourcing, the ideal candidate will leverage jewelry manufacturing expertise, meticulous operational discipline, real-time visibility into production workflows, and an obsessive commitment to quality and delivery to scale our partnership model and prove that speed, quality, and affordability can coexist.
Success in this role means consistently delivering 98%+ on-time delivery, maintaining first-pass yield of ≥98%, achieving zero customer returns attributable to manufacturing defects, building a real-time order tracking system that provides complete visibility from factory to end customer, and enabling Quince to scale jewelry MTO volume while maintaining the highest quality standards. This role offers the opportunity to make a significant impact on our business, build a world-class supply chain partnership, and shape the future of how premium jewelry is made and delivered.
Responsibilities
Own end-to-end production planning and scheduling across manufacturing partners; translate demand forecasts into detailed daily/weekly production workflows that meet the 3-week delivery window.
Build and operate a real-time order tracking system with complete visibility from order intake through factory production, QC, packing, shipment, and final customer delivery; ensure ≥98% data accuracy and daily updates.
Establish and maintain quality control standards across manufacturing partners; monitor defect rates, first-pass yield, escalate quality misses immediately.
Serve as primary operational liaison with manufacturing partners and conduct weekly operational reviews covering schedule adherence, quality, delivery performance, capacity, and risk mitigation with domestic and international suppliers.
Coordinate logistics and fulfillment; ensure correct packaging, labeling, and shipment to freight forwarders; track deliveries through final customer receipt and manage any post-delivery issues.
Create daily MTO standup and weekly operational dashboard tracking on-time delivery, defect rates, lead times, inventory levels, and production bottlenecks; provide monthly reporting to leadership.
Monitor and respond to production risks in real-time; flag orders at risk of missing the 3-week window within 24 hours; drive rapid problem-solving across manufacturing, quality, and logistics.
Qualifications
Required:
Minimum 5 years of jewelry manufacturing experience, including direct exposure to Jewelry manufacturing, quality control, and production management processes.
Proven track record of managing production workflows, schedules, and timelines in jewelry or related manufacturing environments, with experience delivering on accelerated timelines.
Direct experience tracking orders and managing fulfillment from factory through shipping and customer delivery (end-to-end visibility and accountability).
Demonstrated ability to manage quality control, defect tracking, root-cause analysis, and corrective action closure in a production environment.
Strong experience coordinating with manufacturing partners or managing supplier relationships in production-critical roles; comfort with cross-partner communication and escalation.
Strong Excel/Google Sheets skills and experience building or managing production tracking systems (ERP, MES, custom dashboards); ability to learn new software tools quickly.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills; comfort with data-driven decisions and identifying process improvements from operational metrics.
Exceptional written and verbal communication; ability to create clear, actionable reports and escalation summaries for multiple stakeholders.
Obsessive attention to detail; defects and missed deadlines are intolerable to you; you catch problems before they reach customers.
Calm under pressure; ability to manage competing priorities and operational escalations with composure and rapid decision-making.
Collaborative and relationship-oriented; you build strong partnerships with manufacturing teams, quality leads, logistics partners, and cross-functional stakeholders.
Experience working cross-functionally with merchandising, sourcing, and production teams
