title: Adventure Readiness Specialist
description: About Rivian Rivian is on a mission to keep the world adventurous forever. This goes for the emissions-free Electric Adventure Vehicles we build, and the curious, courageous souls we seek to attract. As a company, we constantly challenge what’s possible, never simply accepting what has always been done. We reframe old problems, seek new solutions and operate comfortably in areas that are unknown. Our backgrounds are diverse, but our team shares a love of the outdoors and a desire to protect it for future generations. Role Summary As an Adventure Readiness Specialist, you are a critical part of the Rivian Service team during our peak seasonal periods, helping us provide seamless care that keeps owners focused on their adventure and their Rivians ready for the journey ahead. During our seasonal surges in delivery and service demand, you’ll be on the front lines, helping our team navigate the high-volume peaks and ensure every owner’s journey continues uninterrupted. This role is also an exciting entry point, offering a hands-on, development experience that is specifically focused on preparing you for a future as a Service Technician. Responsibilities This is a dynamic role where you will spend time learning and contributing across three key areas: Vehicle & Site Operations: Receive, inspect, and process incoming vehicle inventory. Maintain the quality and delivery readiness of our vehicles through washing, detailing, and charging. Manage vehicle logistics, including lot organization, shuttling vehicles, and secure key management. Maintain a clean, safe, and highly organized service center environment, adhering to 5S principles. Service Production Support: Assist technicians with basic vehicle repairs, focusing on Pre-Delivery Inspection (PDI) tasks and Express Lane work. Learn to safely use basic hand tools and power tools under direct supervision. Support the workshop by maintaining tool and equipment readiness. Training & Career Development Participate in our TRAIL program—a guided path through hands-on learning, technical training, and professional growth. Receive mentorship and on-the-job training for the Service Technician role. Complete Rivian Learning Network (RLN) modules. Explore a dedicated pathway into a long-term career as a Service Technician. Maintain a flexible, “all-hands-on-deck” mindset by providing cross-functional support to other areas of the business as needed, ensuring overall site success while prioritizing primary technical training objectives. Qualifications High School Diploma, GED, or other recognized high school equivalency credential preferred. Previous technical experience (e.g. automotive repair, mechanical maintenance, or electrical work) or experience in an adjacent technical industry (e.g. aviation, HVAC, or manufacturing) is highly preferred. A strong desire to learn, a high degree of adaptability, and a passion for working with your hands. Excellent communication and teamwork skills. Must be at least 21 years old and possess a valid driver’s license with no driving-related suspensions or revocation of Driver’s License (within a 3-5 year period). Ability to work a flexible 40-hour week, which may include varied shifts, weekends, and holidays. Physical exertion may be required to perform occupational tasks (sitting, standing, walking, bending, kneeling, carrying, reaching, pushing, pulling, and lifting up to 50 lbs. Frequent use of hands for purposes of grasping and using tools correctly, entering data, writing communications, or calling customers or internal partners. Ability to see, read, and interpret documents such as governmental regulations, safety rules, operating and maintenance instructions or schematics. This role may require regular interaction with customers and their families, 3rd party affiliates, and suppliers within Rivian facilities, on mobile service routes, or at community outreach events. Pay Disclosure The hourly range for this role is $19.99 - $22.88 for Illinois (Chicago-Metro) based applicants. This is the lowest to highest salary we in good faith believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. An employee’s position within the salary range will be based on several factors including, but not limited to, specific competencies, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, geographic location, shift, and organizational needs. The successful candidate may be eligible for annual performance bonus. We offer a comprehensive package of benefits for full-time and part-time employees, their spouse or domestic partner, and children up to age 26, including but not limited to paid vacation, paid sick leave, and a competitive portfolio of insurance benefits including life, medical, dental, vision, short-term disability insurance, and long-term disability insurance to eligible employees. You may also have the opportunity to participate in Rivian’s 401(k) Plan and Employee Stock Purchase Program if you meet certain eligibility requirements. Full-time employee coverage is effective on their first day of employment. Part-time employee coverage is effective the first of the month following 90 days of employment. More information about benefits is available at rivianbenefits.com. You can apply for this role through careers.rivian.com (or through internal-careers-rivian.icims.com if you are a current employee). There is no fixed deadline for this application; applications are accepted on an ongoing basis until the role is filled or the opening is no longer needed. Equal Opportunity Rivian is an equal opportunity employer and complies with all applicable federal, state, and local fair employment practices laws. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, ancestry, sex, sexual orientation, gender, gender expression, gender identity, genetic information or characteristics, physical or mental disability, marital/domestic partner status, age, military/veteran status, medical condition, or any other characteristic protected by law. Rivian is committed to ensuring that our hiring process is accessible for persons with disabilities. If you have a disability or limitation, such as those covered by the Americans with Disabilities Act, that requires accommodations to assist you in the search and application process, please email us at candidateaccommodations@rivian.com. Candidate Data Privacy and Technology Rivian may collect, use and disclose your personal information or personal data (within the meaning of the applicable data protection laws) when you apply for employment and/or participate in our recruitment processes (“Candidate Personal Data”). This data includes contact, demographic, communications, educational, professional, employment, social media/website, network/device, recruiting system usage/interaction, security and preference information. Rivian may use your Candidate Personal Data for the purposes of (i) tracking interactions with our recruiting system; (ii) carrying out, analyzing and improving our application and recruitment process, including assessing you and your application and conducting employment, background and reference checks; (iii) establishing an employment relationship or entering into an employment contract with you; (iv) complying with our legal, regulatory and corporate governance obligations; (v) recordkeeping; (vi) ensuring network and information security and preventing fraud; and (vii) as otherwise required or permitted by applicable law. Rivian may share your Candidate Personal Data with (i) internal personnel who have a need to know such information in order to perform their duties, including individuals on our People Team, Finance, Legal, and the team(s) with the position(s) for which you are applying; (ii) Rivian affiliates; and (iii) Rivian’s service providers, including providers of background checks, staffing services, and cloud services. Rivian may transfer or store internationally your Candidate Personal Data, including to or in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, and the European Union and in the cloud, and this data may be subject to the laws and accessible to the courts, law enforcement and national security authorities of such jurisdictions. How We Use AI in Our Hiring Process: To ensure transparency, we want candidates to know that Rivian uses iCIMS Talent Cloud Artificial Intelligence (TCAI) and AI-enabled tools to assist with screening, reviewing, organizing and highlighting profiles and applications that match the key requirements for each role. AI does not make hiring decisions: Qualified candidate applications are reviewed by a member of our team, and all decisions throughout the process are made by humans. We use AI to support efficiency and consistency, not to replace human judgment. We are committed to a fair, thoughtful, and equitable experience for every candidate. Participation in AI profile matching is entirely voluntary. If you prefer that your profile not be used in this process, you can opt out at any time. Opting out means your profile will be excluded from automated matching and will not be surfaced for additional roles through this system. Your current application remains active and will not be affected in any way. Interview Integrity & AI Policy Our interview process is designed to evaluate your personal technical foundation, real-time problem-solving logic, and structured capabilities. Therefore, the use of assistive generative AI tools to formulate or deliver your solutions during live interview sessions is not permitted. We care most about how you think — how you make sense of unclear requirements, weigh trade-offs, and explain why you chose one approach over another. We value your unique human perspective, your authenticity, and the journey it takes to reach a solution. Please note that we are currently not accepting applications from third party application services.

This goes for the emissions-free Electric Adventure Vehicles we build, and the curious, courageous souls we seek to attract. As a company, we constantly challenge what’s possible, never simply accepting what has always been done. We reframe old problems, seek new solutions and operate comfortably in areas that are unknown. Our backgrounds are diverse, but our team shares a love of the outdoors and a desire to protect it for future generations. Role Summary Rivian’s Autonomy Eval Infrastructure team builds the software that helps engineers understand and improve the ML models behind our driving systems and gives release teams evidence they can trust. Within Autonomy’s AI Platform organization, we connect model development with evaluation workflows, metrics, triage and visualization across simulation and real-world vehicle data. As a metrics-platform engineer, you will build backend services, Python libraries and data pipelines that turn model outputs into reproducible measurements and useful comparisons. Working alongside Perception, Planning and Systems engineers, you will learn how models behave, investigate regressions and help turn evaluation findings into better models and data, as well as trusted release scorecards. You will own well-scoped components from implementation through deployment and operation, with support from senior engineers on design and complex trade-offs. Joining this newly formed team offers the opportunity to help shape a shared platform while developing your software engineering and distributed-systems skills. Responsibilities Build and test services, APIs and libraries for registering metric definitions, computing results and retrieving them consistently across engineering tools. Implement scalable metric-processing pipelines with safe retries, incremental computation and backfills. Make missing inputs, failed jobs and incomplete results visible. Capture code, metric, model, dataset and scenario versions so a reported result can be traced to its inputs and reproduced. Build tools for comparing model versions and exploring results by scenario, geography, vehicle platform and operating conditions, using consistent aggregation and denominators. Work with model developers to run evaluation experiments, inspect predictions and investigate failure patterns. Help translate findings into targeted evaluation datasets and regression tests. Integrate metrics into evaluation workflows, CI regression checks and release scorecards, and connect results to recordings and triage tools for investigation. Improve automated tests, performance, observability and deployment tooling. Debug production issues and document the components you support. Work with engineers in Palo Alto, London and Belgrade to turn user needs into maintainable software, participate in design and code reviews, and deliver improvements iteratively. Qualifications 2+ years of software engineering experience, or equivalent demonstrated experience building and maintaining substantial software systems. Strong Python programming skills and a solid foundation in data structures, algorithms, software design and debugging. Practical SQL skills, with AI coding tools expected to support writing and refining queries; ability to validate query logic, results and performance. Experience building backend services, reusable libraries or data-processing pipelines with automated tests, version control and code review. Ability to reason about APIs, data models and component design, explain trade-offs, and identify failure cases such as duplicate, delayed or missing data. Experience with cloud services, containers and CI/CD, and an understanding of how software is deployed and monitored in production. Care with data correctness and basic statistical reasoning, including sample sizes, rates and variability; curiosity about how measurements reflect real driving behavior. Clear written communication and a collaborative approach to gathering requirements, asking for feedback and resolving technical problems. Bonus Points Hands-on experience with ML models using PyTorch or similar frameworks, such as running inference or analyzing prediction errors; experience in autonomy, robotics or simulation. Experience with distributed data processing or analytical storage, such as Spark, Databricks, Delta Lake or comparable systems. Experience with AWS, Docker and GitLab CI, or with developer tools, experiment tracking, data lineage or results visualization. Prior autonomy or robotics experience is welcome but is not required for this role. Availability for a standard 40-hour workweek, including weekends, holidays, early morning, evening, or overnight shifts as required. Ability to travel to regional locations or production plants as needed. Proficient in Windows/Mac environments, work order management systems, and specialized engineering/diagnostic documentation systems. Physical capability to perform occupational tasks (sitting, standing, bending, kneeling, and lifting up to 50 lbs). State mechanic certifications where required by jurisdiction (e.g., Michigan certifications in front end, suspension, steering, brakes, electrical, and HVAC). Experience & Leadership: 5 to 8+ years of automotive repair experience preferred, with extensive experience in bumper-to-bumper diagnostics. 3 to 8+ years of hands-on experience working on vehicle High Voltage (HV) systems and HV diagnostic work. Experience in leadership or supervisory roles (e.g., Shop Foreman, Team Lead, or Technical Mentor) preferred. Demonstrated background in continuous improvement, process standardization, and escalation management. Spectrum of Advanced Technical Skills: High Voltage (HV) & Power Electronics: Deep understanding of high-voltage architecture, High-Voltage Interlock Loops (HVIL), charging isolation, and safety power-down protocols using appropriate PPE. Capable of diagnosing complex HV faults and isolation issues. Low Voltage & Network Electronics: Advanced knowledge of automotive electronics, CAN and LIN bus network communication, reading/leveraging electrical schematics, and performing precise wiring harness repairs. The ideal candidate is a recognized technical expert in automotive NVH CAE who can solve ambiguous, high-impact problems; influence decisions across engineering organizations; and elevate the capability of the broader NVH team. Lead the development, integration, and application of full-vehicle NVH CAE models, including structural, vibro-acoustic, and statistical energy analysis models. 2. Define simulation methods, target cascades, and technical strategies for complex NVH attributes such as road noise, powertrain/driveline vibration, structure-borne noise, airborne noise, and sound-package performance. 3. Drive robust correlation between CAE predictions and component, subsystem, bench, and vehicle test data; translate findings into clear, actionable design direction. 4. Lead root-cause analysis using methods including modal analysis, frequency response analysis, transfer path analysis, operational deflection shapes, and dynamic stiffness assessment. 5. Serve as a technical authority in cross-functional design and program forums, aligning NVH performance with vehicle targets, timing, cost, mass, durability, manufacturability, and system constraints. 6. Establish scalable CAE workflows, model-quality standards, automation, and best practices that improve analysis speed, fidelity, and repeatability across programs. 7. Develop and review technical recommendations, reports, and executive-ready summaries that enable timely, data-driven decisions. 8. Mentor and develop NVH and CAE engineers; raise technical standards through constructive review, knowledge sharing, and hands-on coaching. 9. Model Rivian Compass Values by asking why to identify root causes, staying open to diverse perspectives, zooming out to optimize vehicle-level outcomes, building together across functions, and over-delivering for the customer Qualifications 1. Advanced proficiency with CAE pre- and post-processing tools such as ANSA, HyperMesh, META, HyperView, or equivalent; and solvers such as Nastran, OptiStruct, Abaqus, or equivalent. 5. Experience with Statistical Energy Analysis tools such as VA One or equivalent, and familiarity with NVH test and data-analysis tools such as Siemens Simcenter Testlab, LMS, HEAD Acoustics, or equivalent. 6. Demonstrated ability to lead complex technical workstreams, influence cross-functional decisions, and deliver solutions under program timing constraints. 7. Strong Python or comparable scripting experience for simulation automation, data processing, visualization, and workflow improvement. 8. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain complex technical tradeoffs to technical and non-technical audiences. 9. Role Summary We are looking for an Electromagnetic Compatibility Engineer who seeks to enter the growing EV marketplace. Our team focusses on providing EMC technical expertise for current and next gen vehicle platforms of autonomy, infotainment, body controllers, power conversion, propulsion, dynamics etc. You will be assessing the electromagnetic interactions between circuits & structures integrated into our vehicles and providing design guidance and design validation. Responsibilities General Responsibilities: Work with hardware designers & EMC team to develop the next generation of control electronics for Rivian vehicles. Produce PCB to system-level strategies for high voltage distribution, packaging, grounding, bonding, shielding, and filtering. description:
Who we are
Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.
Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.
About the role
AI is changing how our R&D organization builds and runs software. This is a new role: one leader for Samsara's AI bets across the software development lifecycle. You'll own two efforts that started and whatever comes next.
Dev Agents builds in-house and integrates vendors such as Claude and Codex. That includes an Agent Gateway that serves internal MCPs, managed access to skills, and cloud runners that fan work out to cloud agents.
SRE AI is an agent that does the first-line work of an on-call engineer. It already runs on real incidents in production: it writes a root cause analysis, escalates severity when it has proof, and can roll back the deployment it identified as the cause.
This is a new role. You'll lead a team of five to 10 senior engineers, from Senior to Staff. You'll work directly with every R&D leader and with the developers who use what you build.
This is a remote position open to candidates based in North America.
What makes this unique
One leader across the lifecycle. You own AI for the whole software development lifecycle, for our R&D organization.
Room to try things. Try, fail, learn. One bet in five landing is a good outcome.
Already in production. SRE AI runs on live incidents today, and two teams use it as first responder.
A senior team. Principal, senior staff, staff and senior engineers who work without a roadmap.
Build, don't hand off. This is hands-on leadership. You'll work from the details, not from a PRD.
Why this role matters
Real-world impact at scale
Engineers on every team take turns on-call, which costs roughly 10 to 15 percent of headcount. The goal is an agent that is first responder to every page, so people are only woken up when a human is needed, and arrive with the root cause in hand.
Make SRE AI first responder for five teams, and the default for every team by the end of 2027.
Within 12 months, the median developer ships as fast as today's 90th percentile.
Unique technical challenges
Choose which experiments to run for a root cause analysis agent when no playbook exists.
Decide when to build, integrate or buy as model prices and capabilities shift roughly every quarter.

You will be the connective tissue between Product, Hardware Engineering, Operations, Planning, Manufacturing, Quality, Sourcing, and Logistics, driving cross-functional alignment on schedule, cost, and supply readiness for complete systems rather than individual commodities.

You want to impact the industries that run our world: Your efforts will result in real-world impact – helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, reduce emissions, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.

We set up our employees for success and have built a culture that encourages rapid career development, countless opportunities to experiment and master your craft in a hyper growth environment.

Mastermind and power NPI programs end-to-end
Champion next-generation device and accessory programs from bold concept stages through EVT, DVT, PVT, explosive ramp, and full mass production, taking full ownership of the end-to-end supply chain master plan
Drive flawless launch readiness in close lockstep with world-class JDM partners and internal operations engines, optimizing BOM+MVA, mastering development E&O, mitigating risk, and executing aggressive ramp curves
Command program-level cost, precision scheduling, and strategic risk, pitching clear, high-impact decisions and trade-offs to executive leadership
Establish and enforce rigorous build-readiness criteria and high-stakes gate reviews at every critical phase—covering materials, custom packaging, and global logistics
Engineer lead-time-driven backward-scheduling from OK2MP through demanding REL/CRT testing to secure critical PO release deadlines with total precision
Strategically classify process paths early (Full PLCM vs. Legacy Fast-Track exception) and drive ironclad stage-gate documentation from day-one kickoff
Galvanize cross-functional alignment and exert high-impact influence
Serve as the indispensable single point of accountability and catalyst for supply chain excellence across Product, Engineering, Operations, Planning, Manufacturing, Quality, Finance, and Marketing
Unify diverse stakeholders around top priorities, resolve friction with agility, and guide executive decisions with compelling options and bold recommendations
Partner dynamically with Hardware Engineering on DFM, design-for-cost, and proactive supply-chain risk mitigation right at the drawing board
Lead high-octane schedule stewardship, synchronizing supply roadmaps directly to the stage-gate timeline and orchestrating high-alignment weekly core-team reviews
Run dynamic program cadences (core team syncs, readiness reviews, executive updates) that catalyze action and drive transformative momentum
Orchestrate seamless, structured handoffs to sustaining Supply Chain Managers post-MP ramp, ensuring long-term operational success and flawless execution
Neutralize supply risks and drive world-class partner performance
Join forces with Sourcing, Planning, and global manufacturing leaders to guarantee resilient supply lines, crush long-lead bottlenecks, and deploy bulletproof contingency strategies
Power Sourcing initiatives with aggressive cost targets, actionable should-cost insights, and high-stakes supplier negotiations across complex system BOMs
Relentlessly hunt down and resolve capacity, supply, quality, or logistics bottlenecks before they ever threaten the critical path
Spearhead the strategic Materials Risk Buy approval workflow, evaluating financial exposure and securing rapid executive alignment
Manage high-impact engineering changes with precision, driving seamless inventory disposition and cutover plans
Oversee NPI Material Spend and NMS budgets with absolute fiscal rigor across tooling, NRE, and ORT investments
Revolutionize supply chain operations with cutting-edge AI and automation
Architect high-leverage playbooks, intelligent workflows, and custom tooling that supercharge productivity across the entire global supply chain organization
Transform complex data into game-changing insights through futuristic dashboards, predictive risk analytics, and compelling executive briefings
Pioneer autonomous AI agents and automated workflows to handle routine program tasks, status roll-ups, and data pulls, freeing your bandwidth for high-value strategic leadership

title: Assembly Technician
description:
About Standard Bots

Standard Bots is America's largest manufacturer of AI-native industrial robots. Full-stack robots—hardware, software, and AI—all designed and assembled in Glen Cove, New York. The company makes AI-native robots anyone can buy and deploy, with customers ranging from family-owned machine shops to the Fortune 500. Customers include Sunoco, Lockheed Martin, NASA, and the U.S. Army, along with hundreds of manufacturers nationwide. Standard Bots raised a $200 million Series C at a $1 billion valuation from RoboStrategy, General Catalyst, Amazon Industrial Innovation Fund, and Samsung Next.


About the role

You'll build the robots that are showing up on factory floors across the country. Standard Bots is moving fast from prototype to high-volume production, and the people on the assembly line are the most important people in the building — this role sits right at the center of that. You'll work alongside the Production Supervisor and the engineering team, turning parts into precision robotic systems that are ready to work.

📍 Location

This is a full-time, on-site role at our Glen Cove, NY manufacturing facility, working first shift, Monday through Friday. We're unable to sponsor visas for this role.


What you'll do

- Assemble production robots and components to spec, following work instructions — hands-on work that takes a pile of parts and turns it into a finished machine.

- Run quality checks throughout the build, not just at the end, and report issues to the Production Supervisor as soon as you spot them.

- Keep your workspace safe and organized, in line with company and industry standards.

- Handle material movement and distribution to workstations so the line keeps running.

- Contribute to continuous improvement on the production floor — if you see a better way to build, we want to hear it.


What you'll bring

- A high school diploma or equivalent.

- 2+ years in a mass production or manufacturing environment.

- 1+ year of hands-on assembly, maintenance/repair, or tool experience.

- The ability to lift up to 50 lbs.

- Sharp attention to detail — you catch things, and you don't let things slide.

- Clear communication: you flag issues quickly and work well within a team.

- The ability to prioritize and stay focused when things are moving fast.

- A habit of showing up every shift ready to execute, and pride in clean, accurate assembly work.


Nice to have

- An Associate's or Bachelor's degree.

- Experience in automotive, aerospace, industrial, or electromechanical manufacturing.

- Machine shop or CNC equipment experience.

- Familiarity with OSHA standards and workplace safety practices.


Compensation and Benefits

The salary range for this role is $30.00 to $36.00 per hour, depending on experience. We are open to a variety of seniority levels for this role and will build compensation packages that are commensurate with seniority and skill level. Base salary is just one part of the overall compensation at Standard Bots. All Full-Time Employees are eligible for Employee Stock Options. We also offer a package of benefits including paid time off, medical/dental/vision insurance, life insurance, disability insurance, and 401(k) to regular full-time employees.

title: director, Coffeehouse Concepts Design - Catalog
location: 2401 Utah Ave S #800, Seattle, Washington, United States
description:
Now Brewing – director, Coffeehouse Concepts Design - Catalog! #tobeapartner
From the beginning, Starbucks set out to be a different kind of company. One that not only celebrated coffee and the rich tradition, but that also brought a feeling of connection. We are known for developing extraordinary leaders who share this passion and are guided by their service to others.
The director, Coffeehouse Concepts Design - Catalog is the enterprise leader responsible for creating a coherent, commercially viable and globally scalable catalog of approved Coffeehouse assets. The role connects brand and design intent with sourcing, planning, commercialization, technical documentation, release readiness, adoption and long-term sustainment. The director turns a complex assortment into a governed portfolio that is easier to specify, buy, build, maintain and evolve.
This leader will establish one strategic view across furniture, fixtures, finishes, décor, plants, lighting and related art assets, while enabling regional relevance and clear exception pathways. The role directs a team of catalog professionals and works across Concepts, Formats and Standards, Industrial Design, Art, Coffeehouse Integration, Sourcing, Planning, Construction, Facilities, Operations, Finance, Technology and global market teams.
As a director, Coffeehouse Concepts Design - Catalog, you will…
Set catalog strategy and portfolio direction
Define the multi-year Catalog strategy and architecture, category priorities and roadmap across global and regional needs.
Lead comprehensive assortment reviews to retain, evolve, consolidate or retire items based on brand alignment, performance, demand, cost, supplier readiness and lifecycle stage.
Identify white-space opportunities and new intellectual property needs, translating unmet functional, aesthetic and regional requirements into prioritized development briefs.
Own governance and lifecycle management
Establish clear decision rights, intake criteria, stage gates, change control, exception pathways and release cadences for new, revised and retired catalog assets.
Create a trusted source of truth for asset status, ownership, specifications, cost, supplier, testing, release timing, regional applicability, inventory and retirement plans.
Lead annual major releases, quarterly sustainment and defined urgent-change pathways while protecting enterprise readiness and minimizing deployment disruption.
Drive commercialization and release readiness

title: Analyst Relations Senior Manager
description:
Who we are
About Stripe
Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.
About the team
Analyst Relations is a core pillar of Stripe’s enterprise marketing function. The Analyst Relations team creates experiences for the analyst audience that build advocacy and trust, strengthen relationships, and generate insights that inform Stripe's product and go-to-market strategy. Our team crafts high-quality content and builds deep partnerships across product, sales, and marketing to give analysts an accurate, nuanced picture of how Stripe operates and where we're headed. Plus, we bring external perspectives back into the business.
This is an opportunity for a collaborative marketer who excels at translating complex fintech concepts and synthesizing market feedback into accessible insights that sharpen Stripe's strategy.
What you’ll do
You’ll own the global analyst relations strategy and execution for Stripe’s payments, fraud prevention, and agentic commerce portfolio. Reporting to the Head of Analyst Relations, you’ll build trusted analyst relationships, lead evaluations and research engagements, and develop clear, engaging, evidence-backed narratives about Stripe’s products and strategy.
You’ll work cross-functionally to deepen analyst understanding of Stripe and turn analyst feedback into actionable recommendations. The role combines strategic counsel with hands-on work: developing research submissions and briefing materials, preparing executives, and orchestrating cross-functional programs.
Responsibilities
Design and deliver programs that maximize influencer and customer awareness, consideration and recommendation of Stripe’s products and services globally, particularly for payments, fraud prevention, and agentic commerce
Build and maintain trusted relationships with key analysts across firms such as Gartner, Forrester, IDC, and coverage-specific firms
Craft clear, differentiated narratives aligned to market trends
Lead strategy, preparation, and execution of analyst evaluations and research cycles, ensuring high-quality submissions and effective cross-functional workstreams
Prepare senior leaders for high-impact analyst engagements with tailored insights and executive-ready materials
Synthesize analyst insights into actionable recommendations for product strategy and go-to-market alignment
Act as a trusted advisor to Stripe product and marketing leaders, providing expert guidance on market sentiment
Who you are
We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.
Minimum requirements
5+ years of experience in analyst relations, product communications, or a product marketing role
Proven results of managing analyst evaluations and research cycles, including submissions for major analyst reports
Demonstrated ability to drive results cross-functionally with product and marketing teams to develop clear, data-driven market-facing narratives
Strong written and verbal communication skills, including developing analyst submissions and briefing materials for senior executives
Ability to learn complex technical products and explain their capabilities, differentiation, and customer value accurately to external audiences.
This role requires approximately two weeks of travel per quarter.
Strong references from the analyst community
Preferred qualifications
Experience running executive communications and briefing preparation programs
Strong understanding of fintech concepts, trends, and industry dynamics

title: EU Government Relations Manager
description:
Who we are
About Stripe
Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.
About the team
The Government Relations & Public Affairs team represents Stripe to governments, regulators, industry partners, and broader stakeholder audiences. We help policymakers understand the businesses building on Stripe, and help Stripe understand the policy decisions that affect them. Our EU work sits at the intersection of financial services, technology and economic policy. The team works closely with Policy Strategy, Legal, Communications and regional product and go-to-market teams to translate Stripe’s experience and our users’ needs into effective policy engagement.
What you’ll do
We are looking for an EU Government Relations Manager to advance Stripe’s priorities in Brussels through effective advocacy and strong relationships with policymakers. You will bring deep expertise in either payments and financial services policy or technology policy, and use that expertise to influence EU legislative and regulatory debates that matter to Stripe and the businesses we serve.
This is an advocacy-led role: you will develop and execute engagement strategies, build relationships across the EU institutions, and make persuasive arguments for policies that help European businesses start, grow and compete. Working closely with Policy Strategy, Legal and business colleagues, you will turn Stripe’s policy positions into practical advocacy, exercising judgment about where, when and how to engage.
The position is based in Brussels and reports to the Head of EU Government Relations. Its primary focus is the EU, working closely with colleagues across EMEA and globally.
Responsibilities
Develop and execute EU advocacy strategies for an agreed portfolio of issues, setting clear objectives, identifying opportunities to shape the policy making process.
Build and maintain relationships across the EU institutions, developing a strong network of policymakers, officials and advisers.
Represent Stripe directly in policy discussions, making clear, persuasive arguments grounded in our business, our users’ experiences and the needs of Europe’s digital economy.
Bring deep subject expertise to Stripe’s advocacy in either payments and financial services or technology policy, while building the knowledge needed to engage effectively across a broad waterfront of issues.
Work closely with Policy Strategy, Legal, Product and Go-To-Market colleagues to develop and refine advocacy positions, drawing on their expertise and ensuring our engagement reflects commercial and technical realities, and the needs of our users.
Build support for shared policy objectives through trade associations, industry coalitions and engagement with other companies and stakeholders.
Gather political and regulatory intelligence to guide advocacy decisions, keeping colleagues informed of material developments and recommending when and how Stripe should act.
Who you are
We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.
Minimum requirements
At least 5 years of relevant experience in government relations, advocacy, public affairs or public policy, including direct experience of EU policymaking and engagement.
Deep expertise in either payments and financial services policy or technology policy. Expertise in both is not required.
A demonstrated track record of developing and delivering advocacy strategies and influencing legislative or regulatory debates.
Strong understanding of EU institutions, political dynamics and legislative processes, with experience building productive relationships with policymakers and officials.
Sound political judgment: the ability to identify what matters, assess opportunities to influence outcomes, and recommend a practical course of action.
Curiosity about unfamiliar products and policy issues, and the ability to build working knowledge beyond your area of specialism.
Excellent written and spoken English, including the ability to turn complex issues into clear, persuasive arguments and adapt them to different audiences.
Proven collaborator who is resourceful, detail-oriented, and able to work both independently and as part of a team.
Willingness to travel for meetings and events.
Passionate about Stripe’s mission of helping ambitious businesses grow and thrive.
Empathy, humility, and some comedy.
Preferred qualifications
Experience working in a high-growth, rapidly scaling environment.
Industry experience working in technology, payments, merchant or financial services.
A willingness to work with a diverse group of policy, regulatory, and product nerds who embrace Stripe’s policy issues, our users and each other.
Experience in the other policy domain: technology policy for a payments and financial services specialist, or payments and financial services policy for a technology specialist.
Knowledge of the business landscape and experience with relevant business associations in the EU.
Globally-minded and interested: while the focus will be on the EU and the wider EMEA region, given Stripe’s global presence, projects will inevitably become broader than that and the person will have to translate and explain what’s happening in the region to a global audience within Stripe.

These tools sit at the center of how Stripe operates. Every team relies on them to stay aligned, make sound decisions, and move quickly, so every improvement we make compounds across the company. Recent advances in AI give us an opportunity to rethink what these tools can do.
We’re an AI-native team reimagining how Stripe plans, decides, and executes. You’ll lead the StripeOS engineering team as it builds the next generation of Stripe’s planning and execution tools. You’ll work hand in hand with product managers and designers to define what we build, turning ambitious ideas into the right technical solutions. You’ll combine full-stack engineering with emerging AI capabilities and guide your team through open-ended problems where the right product, interface, and architecture emerge together. Drive the team’s vision for AI-native workflows: rethink how Stripe employees plan, decide, and execute with AI at the core, and build agents and assistants that synthesize context, automate repetitive work, and help people make better decisions

As AI becomes central to how businesses are built and run, businesses like Stripe face a new set of questions: how infrastructure for AI should operate, what responsibilities sit at the infrastructure layer, and how to keep that infrastructure open, secure, and trusted.  We are seeking to work with a colleague who combines substantive AI-policy knowledge with the interpersonal skills to earn trust with policymakers. External Advocacy :  Establish trusted working relationships with congressional offices and administration officials across political parties.  Lead engagement with internal stakeholders alongside the Federal and State GR teams to recommend advocacy priorities for Stripe’s AI-policy portfolio, connecting developments in Congress and the executive branch to the needs of Stripe, and the businesses and developers they serve. Connect AI-infrastructure policy to Stripe's work in payments and agentic commerce, and share relevant US developments with international government relations colleagues. Keep clear records of engagements, decisions, and follow-up so the team can judge progress against its policy goals.
Policy Acumen: Examine Federal and State legislation, proposed regulations, and government guidance on model access, AI governance, privacy, cybersecurity, and accountability. Recommend specific changes and turn those recommendations into achievable advocacy plans. Working with the Policy team, this role will assist in the development of our positions on competition, interoperability, and access to proprietary and open-weight models, informed by the practical needs of developers and businesses of different sizes.
Strategic Leadership : Assess how national-security policy, export restrictions, cross-border data rules, and the treatment of models developed outside the United States could affect an AI platform offering access to multiple providers. Work with legal and technical colleagues to separate established requirements from unresolved questions. Recognize when an emerging controversy or government inquiry requires a rapid response. Bring together the right colleagues, establish the facts, and help leaders choose a proportionate course of action.
Collaboration:  Work with product, engineering, legal, privacy, security, and communications colleagues to understand operational realities before making policy recommendations or external commitments. Help the organization reach decisions when priorities differ. Find common ground with other companies, trade associations, researchers, and public-interest organizations. Build support for specific policy outcomes without losing sight of where interests diverge.
Thought Leadership: Write concise policy recommendations, meeting briefs, regulatory submissions, and executive preparation materials. Make clear recommendations on decisions or actions required.

At least 8 years of relevant work in government, public policy, government relations, or technology advocacy, including meaningful responsibility for AI or closely related technology-policy issues.

Personal credibility with officials and staff, supported by examples of earning trust, sustaining relationships, and working effectively with people whose political or policy views differ from your own.

title: Global Market Access Solutions Manager
description:
UL Solutions is seeking a Global Market Access Solutions Manager with strong technical depth in global market access, product compliance, conformity assessment, and regulatory data. The role provides the solution expertise behind UL Solutions’ digital offerings, including AI-enabled services, Global Compliance Management (GCM), and builds partnerships with industry associations, standards bodies, and technical committees that influence how compliance requirements are defined and met.

UL Solutions in association working groups, technical forums, and standards development activity. The role helps make UL Solutions’ digital offerings credible, usable, and adopted through solution definition, activation, adoption, and customer education, and it strengthens that credibility through association and standards partnerships. Solution Definition and Technical Discovery

Activation, Adoption, and Education

• Diagnose technical and data-related adoption barriers, resolve what falls within scope, and bring in the right expert for the rest.
Commercialization and Market Development
• Identify recurring customer problems that could become repeatable offerings, and help assess which are worth investment.
• Develop technical solution narratives, use cases, reference workflows, and technical-commercial playbooks that scale beyond individual customer engagements.
• Partner with the Business Development Specialist and Commercial Teams to qualify and advance high-potential opportunities.
Industry Association and Standards Partnerships
• Build and maintain working relationships with industry associations, standards development organizations, trade groups, and technical committees relevant to UL Solutions’ digital and compliance offerings.
Data & Innovation
• Represent UL Solutions in technical committees and working groups, contribute to standards and guidance documents, and track changes that affect solution requirements.
• Develop joint activity with associations, including technical webinars, member briefings, white papers, and conference sessions, that builds market understanding of digital compliance.
• Capture technical and regulatory patterns from customer and association engagement and turn them into evidence-based recommendations for Product and leadership.
Required
• Bachelor’s degree in a technical field or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
• Strong technical expertise in a relevant field, such as EMC/wireless, connected products,
conformity assessment, regulatory compliance, or market access.
• Ability to communicate complex technical concepts clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.
• Strong customer-facing presence and the ability to uncover underlying needs and distinguish symptoms from the real problem.
• Ability to influence across functions and organizational levels without relying on direct authority.
• Strong written, presentation, facilitation, and interpersonal communication skills.
• Experience participating in industry associations, standards committees, or technical working groups.
Preferred
• Experience with GCM, GMA research, digital certification, regulatory data, or compliance platforms.
• Enterprise software, subscription, data, or advisory background; customer success, solutions consulting, or technical business development experience.

description:

Our platform serves as the technology backbone for modern transit networks, transforming antiquated and siloed public transportation systems into smart, data-driven, and efficient digital networks. With hundreds of agency partners around the world, Via is recognized as the leading transportation technology and service provider globally.
As a Director of Strategic Pursuits at Via, you will lead our most important new business opportunities from first conversation to signed contract. You’ll work with cities, transit agencies, and operators who are rethinking how their communities move, and you’ll own the strategy that turns their goals into winning proposals and long-term partnerships. Our team is made up of talented, collaborative people who are passionate about making public transit better, and at Via, the work we do together translates into real impact for the people who depend on it every day.

Own the strategy for Via’s highest-value, most complex pursuits, from early market shaping through RFP response, negotiation, and award
Build relationships with prospective partners at the most senior levels, becoming a trusted advisor long before a procurement is issued and helping shape how agencies think about what’s possible
Develop a clear win strategy for each pursuit, grounded in a deep understanding of the agency, the competitive landscape, and the community the service is meant to support
Use service data, benchmarks, and performance insights to make the case for Via’s approach and to inform pricing, scope, and commercial structure
Independently lead high-stakes negotiations with executive stakeholders, turning politically sensitive and highly complex situations into agreements that work for both the partner and Via
Partner closely with Partner Success to ensure a seamless handoff from pursuit to launch, so that what we promise is what we deliver
Bring what you learn in the market back to Via, influencing our roadmap, positioning, and approach to new geographies and service models

10+ years of experience in complex, senior-level public sector environments, working with city governments, transit agencies, and elected officials
Experience with public procurement, including RFPs, negotiations, and contracting, and a sharp instinct for what evaluators and decision-makers care about
Quantitatively inclined and data savvy; you use complex data sets to build a compelling case and influence senior stakeholders both internally and externally
An entrepreneurial relationship builder who brings clarity and confidence to ambiguous, politically sensitive situations, turning them into opportunities to build trust
An exceptional communicator and storyteller, in writing and in the room, who can make a complicated idea feel simple and persuasive
A reliable, motivated self-starter who shapes the way things are done and sets a standard others aspire to
A natural leader in every sense, someone whose judgment, presence, and way of operating raises the quality of the work and the people around them, regardless of title

As a Field Manager on Via’s Operations team in the UK , you are the force that keeps our services running reliably for the communities that depend on them. Run daily onsite operations, ensuring safe, reliable, and accessible transportation for our riders.

The role is intended to translate operating needs, production data, analytical results, and integrity findings into executable treatment strategies. As well as holding single-point accountability for program performance, vendor delivery, budget, data quality, and continuous improvement across the asset.
Serve as the single point of accountability for the Eagle Ford chemical program, including corrosion inhibitors, scale inhibitors, paraffin treatments, emulsion breakers, methanol, H₂S scavenger, biocides, batch treatments, and other specialty chemicals. Own the program from strategy and planning through field implementation, performance monitoring, optimization, and vendor management.
Key Accountabilities
The role is accountable for cost forecast, budgeting, invoices and purchase orders, chemical-vendor performance, chemical usage optimization, program updates, and coordination of applicable MOCs and work-management activities.
Program Ownership and Optimization
Develop and maintain the Eagle Ford chemical-management strategy, annual plan, budget, performance targets, risks, and improvement roadmap.
Establish treatment philosophies and governance for continuous injection, batch treatments, H₂S scavenging, methanol, emulsion breakers, and specialty applications.
Use production conditions, chemical usage, analytical results, operating feedback, and integrity data to identify under-treatment, over-treatment, poor performance, and cost-reduction opportunities.
Maintain clear roles, escalation paths, decision rights, and handoffs among Program Engineering, Operations, Production Engineering, Facility Engineering, Integrity Management, Finance, Supply Chain, and vendors.
Technical Performance and Integrity
Monitor chemical injection rates, batch-treatment execution, H₂S scavenger efficiency, inhibitor residuals, corrosion coupons, water chemistry, bacteria, solids, emulsions, and oil-analysis results.
Coordinate corrective actions when treatment performance falls outside established targets or analytical data indicates elevated corrosion, scale, bacteria, separation, or flow-assurance risk.
Maintain a closed-loop relationship with Integrity Management so corrosion-monitoring and inspection results inform chemical-treatment decisions, and chemical-program changes trigger reassessment where appropriate.
Support failure investigations and root-cause analyses where chemical performance, corrosion, scale, bacteria, paraffin, emulsion, or H₂S may be contributing factors.
Vendor, Commercial, and Cost Management
Own program-level chemical-vendor relationships and establish expectations for safety, service quality, technical support, chemical delivery, equipment reliability, reporting, responsiveness, and cost.
Lead vendor performance reviews, track actions to closure, and escalate recurring performance issues.
Develop the annual chemical forecast and track actual spending, treatment rates, product costs, and variances.
Validate invoices, purchase orders, delivered volumes, chemical usage, and applicable service charges.
Partner with Supply Chain on sourcing strategies, bid evaluations, contracts, renewals, product trials, and commercial improvements.
Partner with Chemicals Subject Matter Expert on technical oversight, treatment philosophy guidance, chemistry expertise, benchmarking, vendor evaluations, emerging technology assessments, and strategic support for optimization of the Eagle Ford chemical program.
Data, Reporting, and Governance
Maintain accurate chemical inventories, treatment recommendations, injection rates, usage records, analytical results, cost data, vendor actions, and program risks.
Provide routine program updates covering safety, treatment effectiveness, reliability, cost, emerging risks, and required decisions.
Maintain auditable program documentation, technical recommendations, KPI records, vendor reviews, and analytical-data files.
Coordinate MOCs, risk assessments, and site-specific documentation when chemical products, treatment strategies, equipment, or operating conditions change.
Work Environment & Leadership Expectations
Operate effectively in a fast-paced, high-volume environment with shifting priorities and tight execution timelines.
Demonstrate ownership, urgency, adaptability, proactive communication, and disciplined follow-through.
Build productive working relationships across Facilities Engineering, Automation, Operations, Construction, Maintenance, Supply Chain, HSE, vendors, and engineering contractors.
Prioritize competing demands while maintaining design quality, safety, documentation, and stakeholder alignment
Essential Experience and Education
Bachelor’s degree in Chemical Engineering, Petroleum Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Chemistry, or a related technical discipline. Directly relevant experience may be considered in lieu of the specified degree.
Minimum 7 years of progressively responsible experience in upstream oil and gas operations, production chemistry, facilities engineering, integrity management, or chemical-program management.
Minimum 5 years of direct experience supporting U.S. onshore production operations. Candidates without an engineering degree should have at least 10 years of directly relevant oil and gas production-chemistry or chemical-program experience.
Demonstrated ability to lead root-cause investigations and corrective actions involving chemical performance, injection-system reliability, corrosion, scale, bacteria, paraffin, emulsions, or H₂S.
Experience coordinating MOCs, risk assessments, and field implementation activities associated with chemical, equipment, or treatment-strategy changes.
Strong analytical, financial, organizational, written, and verbal communication skills.
Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and experience with operational databases, chemical-management systems, SAP, Power BI, or similar business systems.
Ability to lead cross-functional work across Operations, Engineering, Integrity Management, HSE, Finance, Supply Chain, Maintenance, and chemical vendors.
Ability to travel to field locations, work in operating-facility environments, and comply with applicable field-access, driving, PPE, and HSE requirements.
Desirable Criteria
Demonstrated experience managing or optimizing production-chemical applications such as corrosion inhibitors, scale inhibitors, paraffin treatments, emulsion breakers, H₂S scavengers, methanol, biocides, and batch treatments.
Strong working knowledge of corrosion, scale, bacteria, paraffin, H₂S, emulsions, flow assurance, chemical compatibility, and production-separation performance.
Experience interpreting production data, chemical usage, analytical results, corrosion-monitoring data, water chemistry, bacteria results, oil analysis, and integrity findings to make treatment decisions.
Experience managing chemical vendors, technical-service expectations, product trials, program KPIs, budgets, forecasts, purchase orders, invoices, inventory, and cost optimization.
